    while the panel stays open; the manager may change the design then
    (`MainWindow::canChangePrintSettings`, as 3D Print's windows: the
    tool previews nothing). When it closes (`MaterialsDialog::whenClosed`)
    the tool reads its materials again once the model is idle and the
    panel shows them (`commandInputsChanged`), its inputs and picked
    bodies as they were; logged `Material tool: materials read again,
    <n> offered, new: <names>`.
  - **Appearance** (`appearance`): one of the chosen material's
    appearances (mitcad#1055), its default first and chosen when the
    material changes; disabled while the material offers one (or for
    Default). One chosen among several goes as `appearance_id` of
    `set_body_material` and `set_component_material`, in the place of
    `appearance`, and hides Keep appearances set by hand; Material ›
    material › appearance of the context menus picks the same.
  - **Bodies** (`bodies`): bodies and components (a component's default
    material, `set_component_material`), picked in the view or the
    Browser; the preselection fills it, a face selected before stands for
    its body. Its row note says what they have now (`3 bodies: PLA Basic,
    1 body: PETG`, `1 component: Default`, `1 body: varies with Color`;
    `targetsSummary`), read for a model command without a preview
    (`CommandSession::refreshRowNotes`).
  - **Keep appearances set by hand** (`keep_appearance`), shown while a
    picked body has an appearance set by hand that the material does not
    offer (`handSetLooks`: not among its `appearance` and `appearances`,
    mitcad#1067, as the model's `replace` keeps an offered one; its note
    names them): on, the commands leave `appearance` out (the
    model keeps those); off, `appearance: replace`. It takes the place of
    the windows' Replace Appearance question.
  - OK: `set_body_material` per body with the item's `library` (a
    library's material is copied into the design by the same undo step),
    `set_component_material` per component. Logged `Material tool:
    <material>/<appearance> to <n> bodies`, `Material <id> set for <n>
    body(ies), appearance replace|keep`, `Default material of <name>:
    <id>` (the component's name, `Root`); a library's material is remembered for Material ›'s recent
    list.
- **Appearance** (`solid.appearance`, SOLID › MODIFY; mitcad#46,
  mitcad#53): **Appearance** (`value`) as the Material tool's tile, its
  picker listing Default (none of its own), then the appearances of the
  class of the first target body's material (its `body_material`, by the
  `materials` query's `class`) under the class's title, for an FDM
  Plastic or a Resin then General Plastic's, then the rest under This
  Design and the library's under their classes' titles (Metal, General
  Plastic, FDM Plastic, Resin, Other; mitcad#1133), as a material's Add…
  (mitcad#1102, logged `Appearance picker sections: FDM Plastic 16 |
  General Plastic 6 | This Design 1 | Metal 8 | Resin 3 | Other 14` for a
  PLA; `appearanceSwatch`); **fx** (`value_fx`, its rows' lists grouped
  the same way without a class first); **Bodies** and
  **Faces** (Default takes a face's own away). OK:
  `set_body_appearance` per body, `set_face_appearance` per body of the
  faces. Logged `Appearance <id> for <n> body(ies)[, <m> face(s)]` (the
  expression with the fx).
- **The picker** (`LibraryPicker`): a frameless window titled `Material
  Picker` or `Appearance Picker` under the pointer (not a Qt popup: the
  Windows UI tests' posted input reaches it as a dialog's), a search field
  and the entries under their headings with swatches. Typing narrows the
  list (contains, any case), Up and Down move, Enter or a click chooses
  (`DocumentHost::chooseInCommand` sets the tile's input), Esc or another
  window taking the activation closes it. Logged `<log> opened: N
  entries, current <name>`, `<log> search at x,y`, `<log> item <name> at
  x,y`, `<log> search: <text>, first <name>`, `<log> chose: <name>`,
  `<log> closed` (`Material picker`, `Appearance picker`).
- **The fx** (the bindings of mitcad#861, which the windows' assignment
  panel wrote): **Varies With** (`varies`: None, the configuration's
  options from the `configure` query, then the user parameters with a
  `values` limit; its note says when the design has none) and a row per
  value (`row0`…`row15`, a drop-down labelled by the value, `Black (now)`
  for the design's value now): **As above** (the tile's value), Default
  (a material: the root's default material) and the materials or
  appearances under their headings with swatches (`choiceImageSize` 16).
  OK writes `switch(Option; value; result; …; default)` with the tile's
  value as the default (`bindingExpression`) to every target
  (`expression` of `set_body_material`, `set_body_appearance`,
  `set_face_appearance`); a library material a row names is copied into
  the design first and named by its name. When the first target follows
  a `switch()` (`material_expr`, `appearance_expr`,
  `face_appearance_exprs`), the tool starts with the fx on and its rows
  (`OptionMapping::parse`, `bindingTable`; values the option no longer
  lists keep their rows), logged `<tool>: the targets follow
  <expression>`; another target picked reads its binding again until a
  row or Varies With was changed. The fx off and OK set the tile's value
  by hand, which removes the expression. A component's default material
  is refused with the fx (`A component's default material cannot vary
  with an option: pick its bodies.`). Logged `<tool> varies with Color: 2
  rows`, `Material tool: varies with Color to 1 bodies: <expression>`.
- **Entry points:** `BrowserController::openMaterial` with bodies or a
  component (Material › More…, a material binding's Edit…) and `openAppearances` with targets (Appearance… of the
  menus, Find in Design's Appearance…, an appearance binding's Edit…)
  start the tools (`startCommand`, logged `Material tool for bodies F1.b0`,
  `Material tool for component C0`, `Appearance tool for F1.b0, F2.b0
  F2:top`); without targets they open the windows. Send to Slicer's Assign…
  (after an import added materials) closes Send to Slicer and starts the
  Material tool with the bodies printed; Edit materials… of its material
  rows' pickers (mitcad#1141) opens the window on the row's material
  (`openMaterialsOf`, logged `Materials opened for bodies F1.b0`), and so
  does the Material row of Property Sets
  (its value and its pencil, mitcad#761), on the body's material or the
  component's default: they edit the material, the tool assigns one.
- **AppKit** (mitcad#1066): the native command form shows the tile, the
  fx as a compact push button with the `fx` artwork (a template image, no
  title) at the end of the tile's line (`fxToggle` with `besidePrevious`,
  pressed while it is on, `input_<id>`),
  the rows captioned by their value (`labelFor`, logged `Panel <tool>
  label row0: Black (now)` as in the Qt panel) with each option's swatch at
  `choiceImageSize` and the headings bold and disabled in their drop-down.
  The picker is an AppKit popover under the tile (`showNativePicker`,
  `platform/NativePicker.hpp`): the `LibraryPicker` stays the Qt presenter,
  shown off the screen, and the popover binds its search field and list
  (typing, Up, Down, Return, a click, Escape, a click outside), so its
  filtering, choosing and logs are the shared ones; logged `Native picker
  libraryPicker at input_material: <n> rows`. Its window is titled
  `Material Picker` or `Appearance Picker`, its search field
  `libraryPickerSearch`, an entry `libraryPickerList.item.<name>`.
- Tests: `tools/ui-material-tool-test.sh` (a library material for two
  bodies and Ctrl+Z, a binding made earlier shown, the fx bound and the
  option switched, the Appearance tool on a body and a face, a
  component's default, the windows without Assign),
  `tools/ui-windows-material-tool-test.ps1` (ctest
  `app.ui-windows-material-tool`), `tools/ui-macos-bindings-parity-test.sh`
  (ctests `app.ui-macos-bindings-parity` and
  `app.ui-macos-native-bindings-parity`: the fx and rows of both tools, both
  pickers, the fx off, three bodies, a face bound to an option added in
  Configurations, in Qt and AppKit), `tools/ui-bindings-test.sh`,
  `tools/ui-material-test.sh`, `app/tests/material_tool.cpp` (`app.unit`:
  the options, the rows and their expression, the summary). In the test
  scripts `ui_picker_choose "Panel Material input material" "Material
  picker" "Shop PETG"` chooses in a picker, `ui_choose_text` in a row.

### Transparent bodies and components

A display state like the light bulb (mitcad#1093), to look inside an
assembly while its housing stays in sight. The model keeps it per body and
per occurrence (`set_body_transparent`, `set_occurrence_transparent`;
[commands.md](../core/model-api/src/commands.md#transparent-bodies-and-occurrences-mitcad1093)):
saved with the design, one undo step per change, independent of the
light bulb and of the appearance and material.

- **The entry:** **Transparent**, a checkable entry, in the view's context
  menu (after Hide ›; for the bodies of the selected bodies, faces, edges
  and vertices and the selected components) and in the Browser's menus of
  body rows and component rows other than the root (after Show When…;
  for the body and component rows selected with the row, or the row
  alone). Checked while every one of them is transparent; choosing it
  makes them all opaque, else all transparent
  (`BrowserController::setTransparent`, through
  `DocumentHost::runVisibilityCommands` as the light bulbs, so in every
  mode): one command is its own undo step (`Make Body2 Transparent`),
  several are one (`Make Transparent`, `Make Opaque`). Those already in
  the wanted state are left out. Logged `Context menu checked:
  Transparent` while checked, and `Transparent: Body2, Part:1` /
  `Opaque: …` when done.
- **The eye stays two-state** (owner 1.11.2026): a click shows or hides as
  before. A shown transparent body or component (its own state: a body
  in a transparent component keeps its own eye) has the half-open eye
  (`eye-half`, `kEyeTransparentRole` in `BrowserPanel.cpp`); hidden, the
  closed eye; a hidden transparent one is transparent again when shown.
  Logged when it comes and goes: `Browser eye Root/Bodies/Body2:
  transparent`, `Browser eye Root/Bodies/Body2: opaque`. The AppKit
  outline draws the same half-open eye (mitcad#1352,
  `BrowserPanel::PresentationRow::transparent`;
  `app.ui-macos-native-browser-markers`).
- **The view** (`OcctViewer`): the `instances` query's `transparent` (the
  body's, or an occurrence's on its path) becomes
  `BodyDisplay::transparent`. A normal body so is drawn in the shaded
  styles as a ghost in its own appearance's colour (transparency 0.75)
  with its face boundaries as edges (no separate hidden-edge objects); the
  wireframe styles draw it as every body. It hides nothing for the pick
  places (`occluded`). Logged `View transparent: 1 body` (`none`) when the
  count changes.
- **Picks go through** (`setPickLast` in `PickContext.hpp`): the owners
  of a transparent body, its faces, edges and vertices and their
  highlights come after everything else under the cursor, so a click and
  the hover take the opaque body behind it, and the transparent body only
  where nothing else is under the cursor; the active component's
  priority (mitcad#420) does not bring it forward. The Browser's rows
  select it as always.
- **Rendered view:** the opacity of its material and its faces' materials
  times `render::kTransparentOpacity` (0.3; `render::seeThrough`), in the
  live rendered view, Render Image and `mitcad-cli render`.
- Tests: `core/model-tests/assembly/src/transparency_tests.rs`
  (`core.model.assembly`), `tools/ui-visibility-test.sh` and
  `tools/ui-windows-visibility-test.ps1` (ctest `app.ui-windows-visibility`):
  Transparent on the housing body from its Browser row, its row's
  half-open eye, and a click where the inner body lies behind the housing
  selecting the inner body; undone, the click takes the housing again.

## Actions and tools

Commands without a panel set `kind` to `Action` (runs at once: Create
Sketch, Undo, Fit, Command Search) or `Tool` (an interactive tool in the
view: the sketch tools), a `mode` (`Model`: outside sketches, `Sketch`,
`Any`) and `run`. No command runs while a feature command is active,
except those with `duringCommands` (Fit, standard views, camera, visual
styles, grid, environment, Preferences, the shortcut overview). A `Model`
feature command whose first input takes profiles (Extrude, Revolve) can
also start in a sketch: the sketch is finished first and its selected
profiles go to the command. The view the sketch was opened from comes
back as Finish Sketch brings it; once the command's card is placed, the
sketch and the body it lies on are shown inside the free area the cards,
the ribbon and the view cube leave, fitted into it when that view (a
zoomed one, or one fitted to the larger free area before the command's
card took its place) shows them elsewhere (mitcad#1227,
`MainWindow::showSketchLeft`, `OcctViewer::showInFreeArea`; logged `View
for Extrude from the sketch: fitted; the box at x,y to x,y, the area at
x,y to x,y (inside)`, `kept` when nothing moved;
`tools/ui-extrude-from-sketch-test.sh` and
`app.ui-windows-extrude-from-sketch`, the steps
`tools/ui-scripts/extrude-from-sketch.mitcad-ui`). Measure is `Mode::Any`:
in a sketch, the sketch pauses as for sketch panels; sketch curves and
points are measured in the application on the shapes the view shows, the
rest by the model's `measure` query. Each pick goes to the query with its
occurrence
(`SelectionItem::occurrence`, mitcad#646), as do the selection card's
measurements, so that the model measures bodies and datums of components
where the view shows them (in the design's coordinates). For two parallel
planar faces or planes the panel shows `Offset: <d> mm`, their distance
along the normal, under the closest distance and the angle.

Measure's picks prefer the body (mitcad#869). Its Selection Filter is
Faces, Edges and Vertices (the default), Bodies, or Sketch Curves and
Points. With Faces, Edges and Vertices the inputs put sketches behind the
bodies (`InputDef::sketchesBehind`, `OcctViewer::setSketchesBehind`,
`PickContext.hpp`'s `setPickYield`): a shown sketch's curves and points,
which the view draws over the bodies, come after the bodies' faces, edges
and vertices under the pointer, so a sketch point on a body's corner or
a sketch line on its edge or face gives the body's (a sketch in the
middle plane of a symmetric extrusion), and the hover highlights what the
click takes. A sketch's curve or point is picked where no body is under
the pointer; those of the sketch that sketch mode edits keep their place
(`CommandHost::editedSketch`). Sketch Curves and Points takes only sketch
curves and points (its own inputs `sketch_a` and `sketch_b`, as Bodies has
`body_a` and `body_b`), also where they lie on a body.

Parallel planes in Measure (mitcad#1161): `between.main` selects the
query's `offset` as **Distance**, with **Minimum distance** immediately
below only when the closest-point `distance` differs by more than 1e-6
mm. The same rule applies to a face and datum plane and to different
bodies or occurrences. Other pairs keep the closest distance as main.
The query's `main_points` supply the displayed delta, tooltip and line:
perpendicular to the planes, from a common projection where available,
otherwise from the first face's centre along the normal. History and
copied values use the same result labels. `Inspect Measure` logs the
main `distance`, any distinct `minimum distance`, and `plane dimension
from (…) to (…)`. Its `Inspection::measurementWire` opts into
`PreviewStyle::MeasurementWire`: a non-selectable, opaque wireframe in
the theme's dimension colour on the topmost layer. A perpendicular gap
inside a stepped body remains visible; other inspection and feature
previews keep their existing depth and transparency. The viewer logs the
actual displayed wireframe, transparency and layer for the regression.
The three platform wrappers for the shared
`tools/ui-scripts/measure-planar.mitcad-ui` exercise real face picks,
the two result rows, perpendicular endpoints and the single-row case.

Axes in Measure (mitcad#647): a pick with an axis (a cylindrical,
conical or toroidal face, a circle or an arc, a construction axis) shows
`Axis: through (x, y, z), direction (dx, dy, dz)` (its point, the centre
of a round face or a circle), and the view draws the axis as a line
through the pick while the panel is open (with the closest distance's
line and the axis distance's). Every pair with an axis, a straight edge
or a normal has an `Angle` (axes and edges 0 to 90°, against a plane
from the plane). With an axis on one side the panel adds `Axis distance:
<d> mm` and `Axis from (…) to (…)`: parallel axes their distance, skew
ones the common perpendicular, meeting ones 0 and the point, an axis and
a vertex or a construction point the perpendicular distance, an axis and
a plane parallel to it the offset; two circles or arcs also `Centre
distance: <d> mm`. The main Distance stays above them. The log line
(`Inspect Measure: …`) adds `axis (x, y, z) along (dx, dy, dz)` per pick,
`axis distance <d>`, `center distance <d>` and `axis lines <n>` (the axes
drawn).

View and file commands are `Action`s with an empty tab (menus, search,
shortcuts).

**Shortcuts and macOS.** `def.shortcut` is the default key (Restore
Defaults and the saved settings go by it); `def.alternates` are further
keys while the shortcut is the default (Redo's Ctrl+Shift+Z, Fit's F6 and
Delete's Backspace on macOS). A platform's other default is an
`#ifdef Q_OS_MACOS` in the definition; nothing is remapped at run time. Qt
makes `Ctrl` Cmd and `Meta` Control on macOS. Fit is Cmd+0 there (F-keys
are media keys); Backspace as Delete loses to a focused text field (the
browser and timeline handle it in `keyPressEvent`); no default is Cmd+H,
Cmd+M, Cmd+Q, Cmd+Space or Cmd+Tab. Menu actions Qt's text heuristic could
move to the application menu get no role (`MainWindow::createMenus`);
Exit, Preferences (Cmd+,) and About have their roles, and macOS has a
Window menu.

**Keys per context** (mitcad#720). A command's shortcut contexts
(`CommandRegistry::shortcutContexts`, `ShortcutContext`) come from its
`mode`: Model, Sketch or both (`Any`), Sketch too for a profile feature
(Extrude, Revolve), Command Panel (a command's panel is open) for
`duringCommands`. Two commands may share a key unless a context of the
one is a context of the other; a conflict's message names where they meet
("S is used by both Command Search and Fit Point Spline in a sketch.
Change one of them."; the others "in the model" and "while a command
panel is open"; a reserved key: "Ctrl+F is reserved for Search Timeline.
Choose another key for …"). A command of several contexts has a key in each, the same one
by default: `shortcuts/<id>` in the settings is its key in every context
(as before), `shortcuts.model/<id>`, `shortcuts.sketch/<id>` and
`shortcuts.commands/<id>` a context's own key, written only where the keys
differ. `MainWindow::updateActions` sets the context by the mode
(`setShortcutContext`: Sketch, a command's panel, else Model) before it
enables the actions, and the actions of several contexts then carry that
context's key; `effectiveShortcuts`, `shortcutHint` and the native menus
follow it. Keys that differ by context are logged at the start and after
Keyboard Shortcuts, one line per command: `Shortcut keys of tools.search by
context: Model S, Sketch F3, Command Panel S` (`(none)` for a cleared
key).

Keyboard Shortcuts (`framework/ShortcutDialog`) is a tree: Command,
Context (a fixed width, the longest text's) and Shortcut. A command of one
context is one row; a command of several is a row with its contexts
(All for the three, else their names: "Model, Sketch" for Extrude) and
the key of every one, or Varies when they differ, and a child row per
context (Model, Sketch, Command Panel), collapsed unless its keys differ.
With the context filter (All Contexts, Model, Sketch, Command Panel) on
one context, every command of that context is one flat row of that
context's key alone, and the Context column is hidden (mitcad#730). The
row the user selected last is selected again when the rows are made
again (a filter change, Restore Defaults) if its command is shown: a
context's row becomes the command's flat row, and back to that context's
row (its command's rows opened) when all contexts are shown. The row
picked that way is not remembered in place of the user's, so All, Model,
All comes back to the Sketch row the user chose. The reserved keys
(`fixedShortcutBindings`, by `reservedShortcuts`: one row per name with
all its keys, such as Ctrl+F for Search Timeline and Return, Enter for
OK) are muted, read-only rows of their contexts whose key reads `Ctrl+F
(reserved)`: under the command of the same id when it is listed (Search
Timeline, its rows then open), else after the commands. Search Timeline,
Rename and Delete have the tooltip "Works while the Browser or the
timeline has the keyboard focus", the others "Reserved; this key cannot
be changed". They cannot be recorded, cleared or reset: Enter, F2, a
double-click or a click on the key shows "Ctrl+F is reserved for Search
Timeline." as a tooltip at the row. The search finds them by name or key
(Ctrl+F finds Search Timeline). Their names are those the UI shows
(Search Timeline, Rename, Delete, OK, Cancel), as conflict messages name
them. A click on a Shortcut cell, Enter or F2
records the next key on that row (Esc or Enter again keeps the old one);
a key changes the row's contexts only: a command's row all of them, a
context's row (or a flat row) its own, so the command's keys come apart
and join again as they are given. A selected row's icon is drawn in the
selection's text colour. Delete or the row's menu (Clear Shortcut) clears a key, Reset to
Default restores one; Down goes from the search to the first row found.
OK with a conflict shows its message and selects the row to change (the
command changed last, in the context where the keys meet). Its log lines,
for the UI tests: `Keyboard Shortcuts opened`, `Keyboard Shortcuts row:
Command Search | Sketch | S` (the current row: command, context, key in
portable text, `Varies` or `(none)`; a reserved row `Search Timeline |
All | Ctrl+F (reserved)`), `Keyboard Shortcuts expanded:
Command Search`, `Keyboard Shortcuts recording: Command Search | Sketch`,
`Keyboard Shortcuts key: Command Search | Sketch = F3` with `Keyboard
Shortcuts keys of Command Search: Model S, Sketch F3, Command Panel S`,
`Keyboard Shortcuts recording cancelled`, `Keyboard Shortcuts context
filter: Sketch` with `Keyboard Shortcuts columns: Command, Shortcut` (the
columns shown) and `Keyboard Shortcuts selection kept: Fit Point Spline |
Sketch`, `Keyboard Shortcuts reserved: Search Timeline | Ctrl+F is
reserved for Search Timeline.` (a reserved row's key asked for), `Keyboard Shortcuts conflict at: Fit Point Spline |
Sketch`, `Keyboard Shortcuts conflict: <message>` and `Keyboard Shortcuts
saved`. `tools/ui-command-test.sh` and
`tools/ui-windows-shortcut-contexts-test.ps1` drive it by its keys: Command
Search expanded, its Sketch row F3, Fit Point Spline S, OK; then F3 for
the spline too, which OK refuses, and, filtered to Sketch, F5 on Command
Search's one row, which leaves its other keys alone (no Context column,
the spline's row selected again after the filter passed Model), All
Contexts again with Command Search's Sketch row selected (Model, then
All Contexts once more, still the Sketch row), and Search Timeline's
reserved Ctrl+F row under it, where Enter records nothing and says why.
S then
searches in the model and draws the spline in a sketch, where F3
searches.

### Pinned commands

Any command of a group's menu can be pinned to the toolbar (mitcad#1001).
Every command row of a group's menu and of its submenus (`Ribbon`'s
`GroupMenu`) has a ⋮ button in a column at the right of the rows, drawn
on the row under the mouse (also a disabled command's: pinning needs no
enabled command) or chosen with the keys; the button, a right-click on
the row and the Menu key (or Shift+F10) open the row's menu:

- **Pin to Toolbar** (**Unpin from Toolbar** when the command is pinned;
  disabled for a command that already is a button of its group);
- **Change Keyboard Shortcut…**: Tools > Keyboard Shortcuts opens at the
  command's row, selected and in sight with the search cleared (all
  contexts shown when the context filter hid it), the keyboard on the rows
  so that Enter records its key (`ShortcutDialog::showCommand`,
  `MainWindow::editShortcuts(id)`; logged as `Keyboard Shortcuts at
  Sweep`).

Opened by the keys, the row's menu has its first entry chosen. Rows that
are not commands (the submenus themselves, the Select group's filters)
have no ⋮. Where the platform shows a group's menu natively (macOS's
`NSMenu`, `mac::showMenuImages`), the ⋮ column, the right-click and the
Menu key of `GroupMenu` do not reach its rows; the pinned buttons' own
menu works there.

A pinned command is a button in its own group (mitcad#1084): the group of
its `CommandDef` (`tab`, `group`), on its tab, after the group's own
buttons (its `pinned` commands, split buttons and extras), in the order
the group's commands were pinned (`Ribbon::addPinnedButtons`,
`ribbonPinned_<id>`; the same action as everywhere: icon, tooltip,
enabled state). There is no separate Pinned group (mitcad#1001 had one at
the end of the tab). The group's caption menu lists the command as
before. A pinned button runs its command; its right-click menu has Unpin
from Toolbar and Change Keyboard Shortcut…; dragged along the group's
pinned buttons, it takes the place where it is dropped among them (the
others make room while it moves; the group's own buttons stay first). A
command that already is a button of its group is not shown twice (a pin
kept from an earlier version stays until it is unpinned), and its row's
Pin to Toolbar is disabled. In a narrow window the groups collapse to
their names from the right, Create last (`Ribbon::fitGroups`,
`Ribbon::fitPage`). Before a group collapses, its pinned buttons fold,
the last one first (mitcad#1111): they leave the row and stay in the
group's caption menu, which lists every command of the group; the group
collapses only when its own buttons do not fit either, so pinning a
command never hides its group's own buttons. The order in which the
groups collapse is unchanged, and the same in both chrome layouts. A
group of pinned buttons only (none of its own) shows its name alone once
they have all folded. A change of a group's folded pins is logged as
`Ribbon pinned folded SOLID/CREATE: solid.sweep` (`... : none` when they
are all back); a folded button logs no place. Docked can also scroll the
groups (`ClassicRibbonPage`). Both chrome layouts show them. The
native AppKit ribbon (`MainWindowNative`, the experimental macOS
frontend; mitcad#1074) shows the same pinned buttons in their groups,
after the group's own (`native.ribbon.pinned.<id>`), each with Unpin from
Toolbar and Change Keyboard Shortcut… as its right-click menu; in a narrow
window they fold first by the same rule (`framework/RibbonFit`,
mitcad#1357), logged with the same line. Its group
menus (NSMenu, without a row's ⋮ button) end with two submenus that list
the menu's commands as its rows do (a subgroup's in a submenu of its
own): **Pin to Toolbar**, where a pinned command is checked and choosing
it unpins it (disabled for a command that already is a button of its
group), and **Change Keyboard Shortcut**, which opens Keyboard Shortcuts
at the command chosen; both act once the menu has closed. Logged `Native
toolbar menu SOLID/CREATE solid.sweep: Pin to Toolbar` (`Unpin from
Toolbar`, `Change Keyboard Shortcut…`), then the lines below of the
shared pins.

The pins are the user's preference (`framework/ToolbarPins`): the setting
`toolbarPins/<TAB>` is the tab's command ids in order, joined by commas
(`toolbarPins/SOLID=solid.sweep,solid.loft`); a tab without pins has no
key. A command is kept under its own tab, the one its group is on, and
`ToolbarPins::pins(tab, group)` gives a group's pins. Each pin, unpin and
drag is saved at once and kept across sessions. The lists that earlier
versions saved for the Pinned group are the same setting, so each of
their commands goes to its own group. When the toolbar is built, an id
that names no command any more is dropped with a log line (`Toolbar pins:
dropped solid.gone from SOLID: no such command`), an old id of a command
(`CommandRegistry::alias`) becomes the command's, a command kept under
another tab than its own (one that moved, as to the Make tab, mitcad#1049)
goes to the end of its own tab's pins (`Toolbar pins: moved
<id> from SOLID to MAKE`), and the setting is written again
without them.

Log lines: `Pinned to toolbar: Sweep (Solid)`, `Unpinned: Sweep (Solid)`,
`Pinned order SOLID/CREATE: Loft, Sweep` (after a drag), `Ribbon group
SOLID/CREATE pinned: solid.loft, solid.sweep` (the group's pinned buttons
made again with these) and `Ribbon group SOLID/CREATE pinned: none`, and
for UI tests the places in [Logs that UI tests read](#logs-that-ui-tests-read).
Tests: `toolbarPinsTests` in `test_app` (pin, reorder and unpin update the
setting; an unknown id is dropped; a Modify command pinned on the Solid
tab is one of MODIFY's pins; a group's pins reorder among themselves; an
old per-tab list is read into the groups, a moved command going to its
own tab; unpinned, it is gone from its group),
`tools/ui-sketch-create-menu-test.sh` (both layouts: Sweep pinned from its
row's ⋮ is a button in CREATE after its own buttons and starts Sweep, Loft
pinned by the Menu key, dragged before Sweep, Draft pinned from the MODIFY
menu is a button in MODIFY, folded before MODIFY in a narrow Floating
window, Sweep unpinned from its button's right-click, Draft and Loft from
their rows, no Pinned group; the window narrowed until Sweep's button
folds: CREATE's own buttons stay, Sweep starts from the CREATE menu,
unpinned there the row is as before, mitcad#1111; Change Keyboard
Shortcut…) and `tools/ui-windows-pattern-options-test.ps1` (the keyboard:
Sweep's row, the Menu key, Pin to Toolbar; in session 0's 1028 px window
Sweep's button folds while Create Sketch, Extrude, Revolve and Hole stay
in place, Sweep starts from the CREATE menu; Unpin from Toolbar from its
row, the row as before; no Pinned group). `tools/ui-pinned-toolbar-look.sh <dir>` pictures
the Solid tab with Sweep and Loft pinned in Create and Draft in Modify in
both layouts, light and dark (a one-off visual check).

### The quick-access group

A capsule of one-click commands that stays on every tab and in sketch and
drawing modes (mitcad#1090, `framework/QuickAccessGroup`): in the
Floating layout's title row after the workspace tabs (`TitleBar::
setQuickAccess`, the row part `titleQuickAccess`), in the Docked toolbar's
tab row after the tabs, right of Undo and Redo (`Ribbon::addTabRowWidget`,
as high as the tabs with smaller icons, `setCompact`: in the bar beside
the groups it took about 210 px from them, and at 1280 px the Drawing
tab's Text group collapsed). Its buttons are the commands' registry
actions (`RibbonButton`, 18 px icons in Floating, the cards' capsule
material as the Undo and Redo pair has it): their icon, enabled state and run; a disabled one stays
in place. Each button's tooltip (`quickAccessTooltip`, at most 80
characters) names the command and its key, and while it is disabled why:
"Save (Ctrl+S): no unsaved changes". The reason is
`MainWindow::unavailableReason`, in `isAvailable`'s order: the read-only
window, an open command's panel, the sketch or what else is open, a
command only for sketches, else the command's own
`CommandDef::disabledReason` (or "not available now").

The commands are those of the File, Edit, View and Tools menus (the
actions named `command_<id>`, submenus included), in the menus' order;
the default ones a build registers but no menu has come after them. The
default set is New Design (`file.new_design`), Open (`file.open`), Save
(`file.save`), Print (`file.print`, mitcad#1089), Design Properties
(`file.design_properties`, mitcad#1088) and Preferences
(`tools.preferences`); a command this build does not register is simply
left out (logged as "not in this build"). The group's ⋮, and a
right-click anywhere on it, open its menu: the four menus as submenus
with their commands as checks (their submenus as submenus), then Reset to
Default and Hide Quick-Access Toolbar. A check adds the command to the
group, at its place in the menus' order; Reset to Default goes back to the
default set; Hide Quick-Access Toolbar hides the group (below).

The whole group can be hidden (mitcad#1189): Preferences › Display ›
**Show quick-access toolbar**, after the Layout choice, checked by
default (the setting `quickAccess/visible`, `QuickAccessSettings::loadVisible`
and `saveVisible`; no key is shown), and the menu's Hide Quick-Access
Toolbar, which unchecks the same setting. Unchecked, the group is not
shown at all, neither its buttons nor its ⋮: the title row's part
`titleQuickAccess` is gone and the row closes up (the design's name has
the room from the tabs on, and nothing folds), and in the Docked layout
the tab row closes up after the tabs. The change takes effect at once,
without a restart, in either layout and in the AppKit toolbar
(`QuickAccessNotifier::visibilityChanged`, which the group, the AppKit
window's `refreshNativeActions` and an open Settings window's check box
follow). The choice of commands (`quickAccess/commands`) stays as it is,
so checking the preference again brings back the same buttons. Logged:
`Preferences: quick-access toolbar shown|hidden`, `Hide Quick-Access
Toolbar chosen`, and the group's `Quick access toolbar shown|hidden` (at
the start too). The command search finds the setting's page
(`tools.preferences.display`) by "quick access", "quick-access" and
"toolbar".

The choice is the user's preference (`framework/QuickAccess`,
`QuickAccessSettings`): the setting `quickAccess/commands` is the checked
ids joined by commas, an empty value none, no key the default set (Reset
to Default removes it, so a later build's defaults apply). Ids of
commands this build lacks are kept, so they show once a build has them.
Each check is saved at once.

When the title row is too narrow for the unfolded group and the design's
whole name (with its box), the group folds before the name would be cut:
only the ⋮ shows, and its menu lists the shown commands first
(`TitleBar::updateQuickFold`, after the row's layout). The Docked
toolbar does not fold it; the toolbar's groups collapse instead. The
native AppKit frontend shows the same group after its workspace tabs, from
the same setting and rules (mitcad#1113, docs/native-macos-ui.md "The
quick-access group").

Tests: `quickAccessTests` in `test_app` (the File commands in the
registry with their keys, tooltips and search words, Save's state and
reason, no reserved keys left for them; the choice read from and written
to the settings, none, Reset to Default; the menus' order; the tooltips;
whether the group shows, shown by default, told once per change, the
choice of commands kept while hidden),
`tools/ui-quick-access-test.sh` and `tools/ui-windows-quick-access-test.ps1`
(both layouts: the default buttons, Save disabled for an unchanged saved
design and enabled after an edit, View › Look At added from the group's
menu, read back, Reset to Default; on Linux the fold in a narrow window;
Show quick-access toolbar off in Preferences hides the group in both
layouts, the title row's part gone, on shows the same buttons again, Hide
Quick-Access Toolbar in the group's menu hides it, and the next start
reads it back hidden; on Linux Preferences is found by the search "quick
access").
`tools/ui-quick-access-look.sh <dir>` pictures the group in both layouts,
light and dark, its menu and the folded group (a one-off visual check).

### Measure's panel

The Measure panel is one layout in the order of the task, top to bottom,
in the Floating and the Docked layout, at the default width (300) and a
width the user dragged (mitcad#1010, mitcad#529):

1. **Picks**: the Selection Filter, its choices on a line of their own
   under its label so that `Faces, Edges and Vertices` is whole at the
   default width (`InputDef::fieldBelow`), and the selections.
2. **Result**, right under the picks (`Inspection::values` and `groups`,
   shown by `framework/ResultRows` in place of the text,
   `CommandPanel::setInspection`): the pair's values first, the main one,
   **Distance**, in a larger type (its tooltip: the points it is measured
   between), right under it **Δx**, **Δy** and **Δz** from the first of
   those points to the second, rows of their own whenever the pair has
   them (mitcad#1167), its distinct **Minimum distance**, then **Angle**, **Axis distance**
   (its tooltip: where it is measured) and **Centre distance**; then a
   group for each pick, titled by its kind (`Selection 1: cylindrical
   face`, `Selection 2: straight edge`, `Selection 1: sketch arc`, `Body
   1: body`; a face's or an edge's geometry from its shape), its values as
   name and value rows: **Diameter**, **Radius**, **Area**, **Length**,
   **Volume**, **Position**, **Axis through** and **Axis direction**, a
   circle without an axis its **Centre**. A group's header folds it
   (kept folded for the panel's next answers). A row is one line, its
   name in its group's column and its value beside it, neither wrapped
   nor cut; where the panel is too narrow for both (coordinates far from
   the origin) the value goes on a line of its own under its name
   (`ValueLine`). Each row's context menu has **Copy**, its value's number and unit
   (`40 mm`). The macOS AppKit form shows the same rows in place of the
   text (mitcad#1354, `AppKitCommandForm::setInspection`): in a tinted
   box right under the picks, the names in a column, the main value bold
   and larger, a value too long for the width wrapping under its line
   rather than cut, the groups' headers folding their rows, each row's
   menu with Copy; the same log lines, the rows' places and the groups'
   headers included (`app.ui-macos-native-panel-rows`).
3. **History** at the bottom, folded when the panel opens (*Measure's
   history*); unfolded, the panel's page scrolls its rows into sight
   (`QScrollArea::ensureWidgetVisible`) in a low window.
4. **Close** (`CommandDef::closeOnly`) in place of OK and Cancel, which
   did the same; Enter and Esc close it too.

Measure measures: what kept a measurement as an annotation (Keep as
Dimension, Annotate ▾ and a history row's Keep as Dimension) is the Make
tab's Annotate group since mitcad#1049 (*The Make tab*).

No text explains the layout. The section under the result
(`commands/MeasureHistoryView`) is added under the result and the message
(`CommandPanel::addSection`).

- **Log.** `Panel Measure result values: Distance = 40 mm, Δx = 24 mm, Δy = 32 mm, Δz = 0 mm, Angle = 0°, …`
  and `Panel Measure result Selection 1: cylindrical face: Diameter = 10
  mm, …` as the rows are set; with the panel's places `Panel Measure
  result <name> at x,y` (a group's rows `Panel Measure result <n> <name>
  at x,y`, `… out of sight` folded), `Panel Measure result group <n> at
  x,y` (` (folded)`) and `Panel Measure result: <n> rows, one line each`
  (or `…, under their names: <name>, …` and `…, cut: <name> (<needed> of
  <width>)`); `Measure history at
  x,y (open|folded)`, `Measure history menu at x,y` (` (disabled)`),
  `Measure controls: none clipped` (or `Measure controls clipped: <name>
  (<needed> of <width>)`), `Panel Measure Close at x,y` and, as every
  panel logs it, `Panel Measure inputs: none clipped` (or `Panel <command>
  inputs clipped: <key> label|choice (<needed> of <width>)`: an input's
  label or a choice's current text cut). Clicks:
  `Panel Measure result group <n> folded|unfolded`, `Context menu: Copy`
  and `Panel Measure result copied <name>: <value>`, `Panel Measure Close
  clicked`.

Tests: `tools/ui-measure-test.sh` and `tools/ui-windows-measure-test.ps1`
(the order top to bottom, the panel at most 300 wide with no control's
text clipped and every result row on one line, in both layouts; the
groups' titles and rows; the distance copied; a group folded; Close and
Esc), `tools/ui-measurement-objects-test.sh` and
`tools/ui-windows-measurement-objects-test.ps1` (no Keep as Dimension
or Annotate in the panel, a history row's menu, Close; the Make tab's
Dimension).

### Measure's history

Each finished measurement of the Measure panel (one or two picks with a
result) is a row of its history (mitcad#648; `commands/MeasureHistory`,
`commands/MeasureHistoryView`, `MainWindowMeasureHistory.cpp`). The
inspection gives the row (`Inspection::record`: what was picked, its main
values, the main value alone and the picks' kinds, the inputs that hold
the picks) and the session hands it to the host when the panel shows it
(`CommandHost::inspectionRecorded`); the window keeps the rows and the
panel shows them at its bottom (*Measure's panel*), in the Floating and
the Docked layout.

- **Header.** `History (<n>)` folds and unfolds the list; it is folded
  when a panel opens (mitcad#1010). Its **⋯** menu has **Copy All** and
  **Clear** (disabled without rows).
- **Rows.** Newest first, one line each: its number, its main value and
  the picks' kinds (`3.  6.843 mm   Face ↔ Face`; of two picks the
  distance, of one its volume, diameter, length, area or position);
  cut at the panel's width, the row's tooltip has what was picked in full
  (`Face of Body1 ↔ Edge of Body2`; a body's name, a construction
  feature's name, `Plane XY` for the origin's) and its main values
  (`Distance 40 mm`, `Angle 90°`, `Offset`, `Axis distance`, `Centre
  distance`, the circles' `Radius` and `Diameter`; of a single pick also
  its `Length`, `Area`, `Volume` or `Position`). The first pick's row
  becomes the pair's when the second pick follows in the same panel; a
  pick that replaces the second makes a new row; the same picks again (a
  row shown again) update their row in place. The list scrolls past four
  rows, so the panel does not grow past the screen.
- **Show again.** A click on a row, or its context menu's **Show**, puts
  its picks back into the panel's inputs (`CommandSession::restoreInputs`,
  with the Selection Filter they were made with): the panel measures them
  again, highlights them and draws its lines. A row whose picks the view
  no longer has (a body or a face gone) is grey and its tooltip says `The
  geometry is not there any more.`; a click on it measures nothing. The
  rows are checked when a Measure panel opens and when one is clicked
  (not while the model computes).
- **A row's context menu.** **Show** (disabled for a grey row) and
  **Copy** (the row on the clipboard as tab-separated text: number,
  picks, each value); keeping is the Make tab's Dimension (mitcad#1049). Copy All copies every row, one per line, newest
  first; Clear empties the history and its numbers start from 1 again.
- **Lifetime.** The history lasts while the design is open, also across
  closing and opening the panel; opening or creating another design
  empties it. It is not saved with the design.
- **Log.** `Measure history: <n> rows` and `Measure history row <n>:
  <picks>: <values>` (` (gone)`) whenever the rows change; their places
  `Measure history row <n> at x,y` (`… out of sight` folded or scrolled
  away) with the panel's places; `Measure history opened|closed`,
  `Measure history row <n> menu` with `Context menu: Show | Keep as
  Dimension | Copy`, `Measure history menu clicked` with `Context menu:
  Copy All | Clear`; `Measure history showed row <n>`, `Measure history
  row <n>: gone`, `Measure history copied row <n>: <text>` and `Measure
  history copied <n> rows: <text>` (tabs as ` | `, lines as ` / `),
  `Measure history Clear clicked`, `Measure history cleared`.

Tests: `app/tests/measure_history.cpp` (the rows' rules),
`tools/ui-measure-test.sh` and `tools/ui-windows-measure-test.ps1` (three
measurements, three rows, the history unfolded, a row copied from its
menu, all rows copied and cleared from ⋯, the first shown again; one row
in the Floating layout). `tools/ui-measure-test.sh` also checks the
picks' preference (mitcad#869): with a shown sketch in the middle plane
of a symmetric extrusion, seen from the top, two corners give two body
vertices; with Sketch Curves and Points two sketch points.

### Measurement objects

A measurement kept in the design (mitcad#649; since mitcad#702 an
annotation, *Annotations* below; the model's *Measurement objects* and
*Annotations* in `core/model-api/src/commands.md`;
`MainWindowMeasurements.cpp`, `view/MeasurementDrawing`,
`view/MeasurementOverlay`, `view/Snapshot.cpp`, `view/SnapshotDialog`,
`view/ViewSnapshot.cpp`).

- **Dimension** (the Make tab's Annotate group, mitcad#1049; before it,
  Keep as Dimension in the Measure panel): its one or two picks become
  an annotation (`add_annotation`
  with its picks, their occurrences and the view — its direction, up and
  a pixel's size at its centre, `MainWindow::annotationView` — so that a
  length lies in the plane square to the view, its dimension line on the
  view's upper side; the model chooses the kind — a round pick's
  diameter, an arc's radius, of two picks their offset, axis distance,
  centre distance, distance or angle — the name `Distance1`, `Angle1`, …
  and the next of six colours). Sketch curves and points cannot be
  picked: Dimension takes the model's faces, edges, vertices and datums
  only.
- **The leaders** (the Make tab's Annotate group, *The Make tab*; before
  mitcad#1049 the Measure panel's Annotate ▾): **Note**, **Datum Label**,
  **Feature Control Frame**, **Hole Callout**, **Material** and **Process
  Note**, each a panel of one pick (a face, edge or vertex of a body, a
  body where it was clicked, or a construction plane, axis or point; a
  datum label and a frame a feature, not a vertex or a point; a hole
  callout a hole's round face or rim; a material or process note a body)
  whose OK (Add) puts the leader on that pick, pointing where it was
  clicked (`SelectionItem::at`, in the pick's component's coordinates, as
  the model keeps it; `MainWindow::addAnnotationFrom`): Note's **Text**
  field, Datum Label's **Letter** (empty: the model's next free letter, A
  to Z without I, O and Q, then AA …), Feature Control Frame's
  **Tolerance…** (the **Feature Control Frame** dialog, *Annotations*
  below; logged `Feature Control Frame tolerance chosen: <characteristic>`).
  A hole callout's text is written by the model from the hole's feature
  (`4x Ø6.6 THRU`, `⌴ Ø11 ↧ 6.8`, `M8x1.25 - 6H ↧ 15`; the model's *Hole
  callouts and the reference look*), a material note's from the body's
  material and a process note's from its print settings (the model's
  *Material and process notes*); a pick the model refuses is reported
  with the reason (`Annotation <kind> not added: …`). The change runs
  outside the panel's undo range as a light bulb's does
  (`runAnnotationCommand`): an undo step of its own.
- **Browser.** The root's **Annotations** folder is one row, shown while
  there are any; its tooltip counts them and the broken ones (the row in
  the failure colour with the warning icon then). A double-click and its
  menu's **Annotations…** open the Annotations window; the menu also has
  Measure.
- **Export Snapshot** (View menu, command search; `view.export_snapshot`,
  also in read-only designs): a dialog with the file (PNG or JPEG,
  Browse…), **Size** (2 × or 4 × the view, or **Width** in pixels with the
  view's aspect; at most 16384 pixels a side), **Transparent background**
  (PNG) and **Annotations** (All shown, None, or `Group <name> (<n>
  shown)` for each group with shown annotations: that group's only),
  remembered in the settings group `snapshot` (all or none). Once the
  model is idle the view is rendered offscreen at that size
  (`OcctViewer::snapshot`: OCCT's `V3d_View::ToPixMap`, without the
  orientation cube; a transparent background from a render over black and
  one over white) and the annotations are drawn over it at the picture's
  scale.
- **Render Image** draws the shown annotations over the saved PNG or JPEG
  image (its **Annotations** check, on by default; not over OpenEXR),
  through the render's camera (`renderViewProjection` of the job's view).
- **Log.** `Annotations: <name> <kind>[ (hidden)][ in <group>] | <name>
  broken: <why>` (`none`) when they change; `Annotation kept: <name>`;
  the panels' own lines (`Command Dimension started`, `Dimension
  Selection 1: 1 face`, `Done Dimension`), `Annotation <kind> not added:
  <why>`; `Note dialog opened:
  <pick>`, `Note dialog: <lines joined by " / ">` (the Annotations
  window's editor), `Feature
  Control Frame dialog opened: <pick or dimension> <frame as JSON>`,
  `Feature Control Frame dialog: <frame as JSON>`;
  `Snapshot dialog opened: size <2x|4x|width>, transparent <on|off>,
  annotations <all|none|group <name>> (<n> shown)`, `Snapshot dialog
  <field> at x,y` (the dialog's own coordinates; `annotations` the
  combo box), `Snapshot dialog: size = …`, `… transparent = …`, `…
  annotations = …`, `Snapshot dialog: <size> <w> x <h> to <path>`,
  `Snapshot saved <path>: <w> x <h>, transparent|opaque, <n>
  annotation(s)[ of group <name>]`; `Render image measurements on|off`,
  `Render image saved <path> with <n> measurement(s)`.

Tests: `tools/ui-measurement-objects-test.sh` and
`tools/ui-windows-measurement-objects-test.ps1`
(`app.ui-windows-measurement-objects`: two round faces measured in the
panel and kept with Dimension, the Annotate group's Annotations…, a
rim's row shown from its menu in the history and kept with Dimension,
the browser's folder, a 4 ×
snapshot with a transparent background written, saved and opened again).

### Annotations

Dimensions, leader notes, datum labels and feature control frames kept
in the design (mitcad#702; the model's *Annotations* and *Datums and
feature control frames* in `core/model-api/src/commands.md`;
`MainWindowAnnotations.cpp`, `view/AnnotationsWindow`,
`view/AnnotationDialogs`, `view/MeasurementDrawing`,
`view/MeasurementOverlay`). The application draws what the model's
`annotations` query lays out and changes them only through
`add_annotation`, `edit_annotation` and `delete_annotation`, each one
undo step outside a panel's undo range as a light bulb's (`runVisibilityCommands`). Showing
and hiding works in every mode, as a light bulb does; other changes too
while a command's panel is open (the Make tab's Annotations… opens the
window there, mitcad#764), and are refused with the reason (`Annotation
command refused: <why>`) only in Create Sketch's plane pick and a
read-only window.

- **In the view** (`OcctViewer::setMeasurements`, `MeasurementOverlay`,
  painted with QPainter as the camera moves). Every shown annotation is
  drawn in its plane: the extension lines from a little off the measured
  points to a little past the dimension line, the dimension line, an
  angle's arc, the arrows (outside, pointing in, where a length is too
  short on the screen for them), a circle's centre mark, a leader with
  its arrow (a datum label's with a filled triangle on its feature); and
  its text set in the plane — foreshortened as the plane turns away,
  turned round where it would read mirrored or right to left (upright
  text reads upwards), faded out as the plane turns edge on (from about
  17° to the line of sight it is whole, under about 5° it is gone). A dimension's text stands above its line: the value with its
  prefix and own text, deviations or limits stacked after it in a smaller
  size (a fit's in brackets), the text after them; a note's lines start
  at its leader's end; a datum label's letter stands in a square there,
  and a feature control frame's cells in a row of boxes (ISO 1101: the
  characteristic's symbol, the tolerance with Ø and Ⓜ or Ⓛ, each datum;
  the fourteen symbols and the circled M or L drawn in lines, not taken
  from a font that may lack them: `paintCharacteristic`),
  or, under a dimension, centred just below that dimension's line where
  its text is (not dragged on its own).
  **The look of a technical drawing** (mitcad#894, mitcad#902: the
  reference PMI look; ISO 129-1, ISO 3098, ISO 128, ISO 1101;
  `paintMeasurements`), in both background tones: the text in the
  bundled technical lettering (an ISO 3098 type B style font,
  `third_party/fonts/iso-lettering`, a file beside the program loaded at run
  time, `measurementFontFamily`; the UI's font when it is missing), regular
  weight with ISO 3098's tight spacing, with no card or outline under it;
  it is the model's `text_height` (mm) high in its plane, so it grows and
  shrinks with the model like the lines, but its capitals as seen on
  screen (foreshortened as the plane turns away; measured on an H's ink,
  not the font's own cap height) never under 9 pixels
  (zoomed out) nor over 16 (zoomed in), times a picture's scale
  (`measurementTextFloor`, `measurementTextCeiling`); the depth symbol ↧
  is drawn in strokes (an arrow onto a bar) in the glyph's own advance,
  as fonts blur it at that size; a dimension's value
  centred above its line a quarter of that height off. Text reads from the
  bottom or from the right (ISO 129-1): never mirrored, left to right, and
  a text that would run down within 30 degrees of straight down runs up
  instead, so vertical and near-vertical texts read bottom to top from
  every side. Lines are crisp and thin (1 pixel times the picture's scale,
  ISO 128, on the pixel grid: `measurementSnapped`) with no halo;
  arrowheads closed and filled, 30 degrees, a text height long (at
  least 5 pixels), laid in the annotation's plane as its text is (so they
  foreshorten with it, but keep at least 0.6 of their width seen
  obliquely), a datum label's triangle as high, a leader on a
  face ending in a dot (the model's `terminator`), a circle's centre mark
  a cross in its plane; extension lines start half a text height off
  the point the model gives (the picked edge, vertex, or the picked face's
  own outline), a visible gap, and run 0.8 text heights past the
  dimension line; a
  frame's cells two text heights high and a datum label's square outlined
  thinly, not filled, the stem meeting the middle of the side it comes
  to. A note's, a hole callout's and a diameter on a leader's lines are
  1.6 text heights apart, the first level with the landing and the others
  below it, set flush left, and start at the leader's end, or end there
  where the model's `align` says so (the landing then runs on to the
  first line's end); a frame under a hole callout stands below its lines
  flush with their left edge (`measurementDisplays` gives each the
  other's words: `overLines`, `framesUnder`). No pixel sizes are frozen when an annotation is
  added: its default places are in text heights (the model's). An
  annotation of the colour **Auto** (the model's `auto`, a new one's) is
  drawn in the neutral annotation colour of the background tone
  (`measurementAutoColor`: near-black on the light background, a light grey
  on the dark one, not chalk-white).
  Over the model, Auto's ink follows what lies behind it: the overlay
  grabs the view's frame once the camera rests or the scene changes
  (`MeasurementBackdrop`, `Annotation backdrop: W x H` is logged): each
  piece of a line (5 pixels: extension and dimension lines, leaders) and
  each terminator (arrowhead, dot, datum triangle) takes the dark ink over
  a light backdrop and the light grey over a dark one, so that a leader
  stays readable over a body (its tone changes where it leaves the
  body); an annotation's text and frames take one ink, by what lies
  behind most of them (`measurementAutoInk`); no casing or halo. Until a
  frame is grabbed, the background tone's colour.
  Snapshots and Render Image take the tone of the picture's own
  background (`measurementPictureTone`; a transparent snapshot the
  view's). A selected one is drawn in the selection's blue, a hovered one
  in the hover's, with the same thin lines (at most 1.5 pixels) and the
  same text: no band, no box (`Annotation hovered: <name>|none` is
  logged). Its picks are not filled in the selection's colour
  (mitcad#902: only the annotation recolours;
  `MainWindow::addAnnotationHighlights` logs `Annotation picks
  highlighted` and draws nothing). A selection made in the view (or
  another document) takes the highlight away and deselects the window's
  rows
  (`MainWindow::dropAnnotationHighlight`).
- **The mouse.** The overlay lets the mouse through, but watches the
  view's: on an annotation's text or a length's dimension line (an
  angle's arc), seen at least half face on, outside commands and sketches
  (there the view takes picks: `AnnotationActions::active`), it takes the
  press and its release (also the release after a double-click or a right
  click; clicks elsewhere reach the model; the cursor is a hand there,
  and the view's own again, `OcctViewer::restoreCursor`, away from it). A
  click selects
  it (its row in the window, its highlight); a drag of its text or its
  line shows it moving and, released, moves it: the drag in pixels into
  millimetres along the plane's axes (`measurementDragMillimetres`), added
  to the `text_offset` or the `line_offset` in use; a double-click opens
  its editor; a right click its menu (Edit…, Hide, Delete, Annotations…).
- **The editor** (**Edit Annotation**, `editAnnotation`): **Name**,
  **Kind** (the values its picks have, when more than one), **Prefix**
  (the kind's, Ø or R, when not changed; emptied for none),
  **Decimals** (Automatic, 0 to 6), **Text before**, **Text after**,
  **Replace value**, **Tolerance** (None, ± symmetric, Deviations, Limits,
  Fit (ISO 286); **Value**, **Upper deviation** and **Lower deviation**,
  or for Limits **Upper limit** and **Lower limit**, the sizes as they are
  to be written (kept as deviations from the value), in mm or degrees;
  **Fit** an editable list of ISO 286-2's common codes, **Show
  deviations**), **Colour** (Auto first, then Black and Dark Grey,
  mitcad#902: a technical drawing's colours, the bright presets gone; an
  annotation's own colour, an older preset's too, kept and offered as it
  is; Custom… with the colour dialog), **Group** (editable, the groups
  there are), **Shown**; a hole callout shows its text (the hole's,
  **Callout**, not edited); a note
  has **Text** (several lines) instead of the value's fields, a datum
  label its **Letter**, a feature control frame the frame's fields
  (below) and **Placed** (On its leader, or Under each dimension: `on`).
  Every one shows its picks — **First pick** and **Second pick** (a
  leader's **Points at**) and **Plane** (the face or construction plane picked,
  the view's when it was kept, or Automatic) — each with a button:
  **Pick Again…** and **Pick…** close the editor (its other changes run
  first) and wait for a click in the view; **Automatic** gives the plane
  back to the model (mitcad#894: a length's dimension line too, `plane`
  and `line_offset` null: placed outside its bodies again). A radius, a diameter and an angle have no Plane row
  (they lie in their circle's or their sides' plane, and the model takes
  no plane for them); where Kind offers one of them beside a kind that
  takes a plane, choosing it disables the row (`The plane of its
  circle|sides`) and choosing the other enables it again (mitcad#713). A
  frame under a dimension shows neither its pick nor its plane: it stands
  in the dimension's place, as Placed says. Placed set to On its leader
  shows Points at with Pick Again…; the pick then sends `on: null` with
  the new `a` and `at` in one `edit_annotation`. A frame whose pick under
  the dimension is a vertex, a datum point or a whole body
  (`AnnotationEditContext::leaderNeedsPick`: the model refuses a leader on
  them) is asked for that pick on OK (`(pick a with {"on":null})`) instead
  of sending an edit the model refuses; its plane row shows once it
  stands on its leader (the editor opens again after the pick). A broken one says why at
  its top. OK runs `edit_annotation` with the fields that changed — the
  tolerance (a frame's too) only when its fields were changed, limits
  typed as sizes read back as deviations to the fields' four decimals.
  Another kind chosen relabels the tolerance fields (degrees and no Fit
  for an angle) with its value, and drops the tolerance between an angle
  and a length.
- **A pick again** (`MainWindow::startAnnotationPick`): outside commands
  and sketches, the selection cleared, the view's banner says what to pick
  (`Edit <name>: pick a face, edge, vertex or datum again. Esc cancels.`;
  a datum label's or a frame's: a face, edge, construction plane or construction axis,
  no vertex or point; a planar face or a construction plane for the plane) and
  the view picks only that; the click runs `edit_annotation` with `a` or
  `b` (a leader's `at` where the click hit) or `plane: {"pick": …}` and
  opens the editor again;
  a click on nothing or a pick the model refuses keeps waiting
  (`Annotation pick still waited for: <name> <field>`); Esc cancels and
  opens the editor again. Undo, Redo, a command, a sketch, Create Sketch,
  another document, an editor opened, or the annotation gone after a
  refresh ends the pick without opening the editor
  (`MainWindow::endAnnotationPick`, `followAnnotationPick`). While a
  command or a sketch is open the editor's Pick Again… and Pick… are
  disabled.
- **Feature control frame** (the **Feature Control Frame** dialog and the
  editor; `FrameFields`): **Characteristic** (each one's ISO 1101 symbol
  and name, from the model's `geometric_characteristics` query),
  **Tolerance** (the zone's width, mm), **Cylindrical zone (Ø)** and
  **Material condition** (None, Ⓜ Maximum material, Ⓛ Least material)
  only where the characteristic takes them, **Datums** (three editable
  lists of the design's datum letters, in order; none for a form
  tolerance, at least one where it needs one).
- **The Annotations window** (`AnnotationsWindow`; View menu and command
  search `view.annotations`, the Make tab's Annotate group (mitcad#1049), the
  browser's folder): a search field, **Kind** and **Group** filters (All
  groups, No group, each group) with **Show Group** and **Hide Group**
  (the chosen group's annotations, one step), a sortable table — Name
  (a swatch of its colour, or the warning icon with the reason in its
  tooltip for a broken one), Kind, Value (the label; `Broken` in red with
  the reason; a hidden one's too: while the window is open it and the
  editor ask the model to measure the hidden ones, which a refresh
  otherwise leaves unmeasured, mitcad#716), Tolerance, Text (own text
  before or after the value, a
  text in its place, a note's text), Colour, Group, Shown (a check box:
  the light bulb) — and **Edit…**, **Colour…**, **Group…**,
  **Decimals…**, **Tolerance…**, **Show**, **Hide**, **Delete** for the
  selected rows (Decimals and Tolerance for the dimensions among them,
  Tolerance not for angles and lengths together;
  each one `edit_annotation` with `names`, one undo step), and **Add
  Frame…** for one dimension or hole callout that is not broken (a feature control frame
  under it: `add_annotation` with its first pick, `on`, its colour and
  group), and **Text Height…** (Alt+X, mitcad#894; the design's, not the
  rows'): the **Annotation Text Height** dialog, an editable list of Auto
  (with the height it gives, `Auto (2.5 mm)`) and the ISO 3098 series
  2.5, 3.5, 5, 7, 10 mm, a typed height taken from 0.1 to 1000 mm; OK runs
  `set_annotation_text_height` (`null` for Auto), one undo step. The
  Colour column shows `Auto` for an annotation in Auto. Kinds are Distance … Diameter, Note, Datum label, Feature
  control frame and Hole callout (mitcad#902; its Value its lines); a frame's Value is its cells (`⟂ | Ø0.05 Ⓜ | A`, a
  warning in its tooltip for a datum no label has), its Tolerance the
  tolerance cell, its Text `Under <dimension>`. The table has
  the keyboard when it opens (arrows, type-ahead, Ctrl+A); every button
  has its Alt key. A row selected highlights its annotation and its picks in the view
  (`MainWindow::highlightAnnotations`); a double-click opens its
  editor. The window follows the model after every refresh and keeps the
  whole selection (selected at once, `selectRows`); closing it takes the
  highlight away.
- **Several at once:** **Annotation Colour** (Auto, Black, Dark Grey, the
  first's own colour when it is another, and Custom…), **Annotation Group** (editable; empty for none), **Annotation
  Decimals** (Automatic, 0 to 6), **Annotation Tolerance** (the editor's
  tolerance fields; Limits as deviations, the values being several).
- **Log.** `Annotations drawn: <name> = <label> (#rrggbb|auto) | …` (`none`)
  when what is drawn changes; `Annotation label <name> at x,y` and
  `Annotation line <name> at x,y` (a length's line, an angle's arc; the
  label's place is its text's middle, or the middle of the part of the
  text in the view's free area when the middle is past the view's edge or
  under a floating card, mitcad#1168) when
  their places change (also when the view's size or the camera moves
  them, `OcctViewer::logAnnotationPlaces`), with `Annotation text <name> <h> px` (its
  capital height on screen) and, for a leader with a landing, `Annotation landing <name> <l> px,
  bend <b> deg`, `Annotation knee <name> at x,y` and `Annotation point <name> at x,y`
  (mitcad#1168); `Annotations highlighted: <names>` (`none`),
  `Annotation picks highlighted: <name>: <pick>; … | …` (`none`);
  `Annotation pick started: <name> a|b|plane[ with <fields>]`, `Annotation picked:
  <name> <field>: <pick>`, `Annotation pick cancelled: <name>`,
  `Annotation pick ended: <name>`, `Edit Annotation pick
  a|b|plane|automatic plane at x,y[ (disabled)]` (the editor's buttons
  shown, once it shows, again while it settles and when its kind or
  Placed changes, when they change; watched by the test sync), `Edit Annotation dialog: <change>[ (pick
  <field>[ with <fields>])]`; `Annotations Add Frame clicked: <name>`, `Frame added under
  <name>`;
  `Annotation clicked: <name>`, `Annotation double-clicked: <name>`,
  `Annotation <name> dragged: text|line by <x> x <y> mm`, `Annotation
  <name> moved: <command>`, `Annotation command: <command>`, `Annotation
  command refused: <why>`, `Context menu: Edit… | Hide | Delete |
  Annotations…`; `Annotations window opened: <n> annotation(s)`,
  `Annotations row <name>: <kind>, <label>, <tolerance>, <group>, <#colour|auto>,
  shown|hidden|broken: <why>` (`-` for none) when the rows change,
  `Annotations rows: none`, `Annotations shown rows: <names>` (those the
  search and the filters leave, `none`), `Annotations selected: <names>`
  (`none`),
  `Annotations group filter: <group>`, `Annotations show|hide group
  <group>: <names>`, `Annotations Delete clicked: <names>`, and the

  `Annotations Text Height clicked`; the dialogs'
  `<title> dialog opened: …` and `<title> dialog: <change as JSON>`

  Height dialog opened: <height|null> (<shown>)`, `Annotation Text Height

## Sketch mode

Create Sketch (`MainWindow::startSketch`) sketches on the selected plane or
planar face; with none, it waits for a pick (`Mode::PickPlane`). It shows
the origin planes for the pick in every design, whatever the Origin
folder's light bulb says (mitcad#844, replacing mitcad#294's rule that
left them out of designs with components): a view state for the pick only
(`inputActivated` with construction geometry), the light bulb untouched,
so after the pick the origin is as the bulb says. The planes come behind
the model's faces for picking (`OcctViewer::setPlanesBehind` and
`setPlanesByDepth`, as a placement input's do, mitcad#656, mitcad#762):
a click where a face lies in front of a plane, or where a plane runs
through a body, picks the face, also another component's while a
component is active; a click on a plane where no face is picks the
plane. A click on a face the pick refuses (not planar, or left out by the
design policy, which the view's filter does not take) is refused with its
reason also where a plane lies behind it, never picked through it
(`OcctViewer::untestedClickItem`). `updateModeBanner` puts the pick order
back when the pick ends.
The browser's XY, XZ and YZ rows pick the plane too, greyed or not.
Light bulbs work during the pick (mitcad#295): hiding a body lets the
faces behind it be picked, and the pick places are logged again. Logs:
`Create Sketch: origin planes shown`. A face or plane of a component
other than the active one asks first whether to activate that component
(mitcad#960, [Activating the picked component](#activating-the-picked-component)).

The new sketch opens upright (mitcad#692): `MainWindow::createSketch`
sends `sketch.create` with `upright`, and the model stores the own frame
whose y axis is the design's +Z projected onto the plane (+Y on a
horizontal plane), keeping the plane's normal, except on the XZ origin
plane, whose upright frame has the normal -Y (commands.md, "An upright
sketch frame"; mitcad#1060). Entering the sketch looks against its
frame's normal with its y axis up (`OcctViewer::lookAtSketchPlane`), so
the screen's horizontal is the sketch's x and Horizontal, Vertical, the
grid and the dimensions stay level: a new sketch on XY is seen from the
view cube's TOP, on YZ from RIGHT and on XZ from FRONT, the design's +X
to the right (before mitcad#1060 XZ opened from BACK with +X to the
left). Editing a sketch again, Look At on it and the axes indicator use
the stored frame, so existing and imported sketches keep theirs. The
turn logs `Sketch plane seen from FRONT (along 0 1 0)` (`BACK`,
`LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TOP`, `BOTTOM`, or `an oblique side`), on entering the
sketch and on Look At. `tools/ui-sketch-view-test.sh` checks XZ, YZ
and a face facing -Y (`Sketch frame in the design`, `Sketch view`); it
and `tools/ui-windows-sketch-view-test.ps1` check the side for XY, YZ
and XZ after New Design, also after the Sketch Palette's Look At
(`Palette Look At at x,y`).

The sketch draws its own origin and its x and y axes (mitcad#254,
`SketchOverlay::paintAxes`), whatever the Origin folder's light bulb
says (mitcad#739): they are the sketch's reference, not the design's
origin datums. The design's origin keeps its own visibility (hidden in a
new design, `set_origin_visible`): Create Sketch shows the origin planes
only for the pick, and entering the sketch hides them again unless the
light bulb is on; the light bulb is never switched, so nothing is
restored after the sketch. The sketch's origin is snapped to
(`Snap::Kind::Origin`, the fixed origin point made at the first snap),
its axes are snapped onto (mitcad#948, "Snapping onto the axes" below),
and its origin and axes are picks of Sketch Dimension and the constraint
tools (mitcad#500); they are drawn by the overlay, not shown in the 3D
view, so no body pick can take them. Logs: `Sketch axes drawn: …` and
`Design origin hidden in the view; the Origin folder's light bulb off`;
`tools/ui-sketch-origin-test.sh` and `app.ui-windows-sketch-origin`
check XY, XZ and YZ in a new design, an edited sketch and the snap.

The turn to the sketch plane centres the view (mitcad#738). A fit leaves
the camera's centre off what the middle of the free area between the
floating cards shows (`fitToFreeArea`), so a turn about that centre took
the origin off the middle, in a direction of each plane's own.
`lookAtSketchPlane` turns about the point to show in the middle instead:
- Entering a sketch (Create Sketch, Edit Sketch) shows the sketch's
  origin there while the view shows nothing (no bodies, no sketches), or
  shows only sketches and the origin is inside the free area before the
  turn.
- Otherwise, and always for Look At, the view keeps its middle: what the
  middle of the free area showed, projected onto the sketch plane. A pan
  to a far part of a sketch stays, and a sketch on a face keeps that face
  in view, also when the sketch's origin is a corner of the face.
- Entering a sketch on a face seen at a steep angle (mitcad#772): the
  middle of the free area, at the camera's depth, projected along the
  normal can lie far from the face in its plane. When that point is on
  none of the faces the sketch lies on (`MainWindow::sketchFace`, placed
  where the plane's link or the sketch's occurrence shows it), the middle
  of their box goes to the middle of the free area instead. Look At keeps
  the view's middle as above.

The point goes to the middle of the free area without a zoom. Entering a
sketch turns the view after the cards are where sketch mode puts them
(`MainWindow::enterSketch` lays out the Floating layout's cards at once,
`FloatingLayout::layoutNow`, the command card showing the palette), so
the view does not move again once the sketch has started. Logged
`Sketch plane centred on the origin: origin at x,y; free area centre at
x,y` (`on the view's middle`, `on the sketch's face`), in window
coordinates; `tools/ui-sketch-view-test.sh` and
`tools/ui-windows-sketch-view-test.ps1` check the origin of sketches on
XY, XZ and YZ after New Design, and a sketch on a block's top face edited
from the front view, the face edge-on, its middle then in the middle of
the free area.

While it waits for the plane (mitcad#474), a banner at the top of the 3D
view says so, `Create Sketch: pick a plane or a planar face. Esc
cancels.` (`view/ModeBanner`, a child of the view itself, so the Docked
and the Floating layout and the native macOS window show it alike, below
the cards floating over the view's top); hints of the status line do not
replace it, and the MCP's `ui_state` reports it as its `hint` (the status
line beside it as `status_line`). A click on a face that cannot take the
sketch, which the pick's filter neither highlights nor picks, says why: a
face that is not planar (`Create Sketch: <face> is not planar (a
cylindrical surface); pick a planar face or a plane, or make one with
Construct.`: cylindrical, conical, spherical, toroidal, a mesh's triangles
or a free-form surface, such as a thread's) or one the design policy
leaves out (its reason); the mode goes on (`OcctViewer::takeRefusedClick`:
what the click hit of the faces and planes when it picked nothing). A
click where an accepted plane lies behind such a face picks that plane, as
its hover shows. Actions blocked by the pick (the browser's, the
appearance and render dialogs', imports) say `Create Sketch is waiting
for a plane: pick one or press Esc.` instead of `Finish the command or the
sketch first.` (`DocumentHost::changeBlockedReason`). Logs: `View banner:
<text>`, `View banner at x,y WxH`, `View banner hidden`, `Create Sketch:
refused pick <face>: <reason>`; with `MITCAD_LOG_PICKS` the faces a click
hits but cannot sketch on, `Pick refused face <body>/<face> [in
<occurrence>] at x,y`. Test: `tools/ui-sketch-plane-pick-test.sh`.

Finish Sketch
(Ctrl+Enter) leaves it. Editing a
sketch moves the timeline marker to just after it and back when it is
finished; everything in between, marker moves included, becomes one undo
step `Edit Sketch1` (`merge_undo`, commands.md, "Undo, revisions and the saved state").

`sketch::SketchController` is sketch mode: an event filter on the view's
mouse events; it keeps the edited sketch as the `sketch` query gives it
(`SketchModel`, re-read after every change by `refreshScene`), and owns
`SketchOverlay` (QPainter in view pixels: constraint glyphs, dimensions,
tool previews, the snap marker, DOF). Clicks on glyphs and dimension
values select them (`SelectKind::SketchConstraint`, `SketchDimension`; a
fixed entity's lock is `fix:<entity>`); double-click on a value edits it;
dragging a value moves it; dragging a sketch point or curve drags it with
the solver (`sketch.drag` per move, merged into one step). A press on one
of several selected curves and points drags the whole selection together
(mitcad#837): each move is one `sketch.drag` with `entities` (the selected
points and curves of the sketch) and `by`, the offset that brings the
grabbed point to the cursor; a press on an unselected one drags only it,
and the press does not change the selection
(`SketchController::selectionDraggedWith`).

### The Sketch Palette's Create section

The Sketch Palette (`sketch::SketchPalette`) has a **Create** section
above **Constraints** (mitcad#1027): two rows of seven buttons, the
sketch tools the user starts most, drawing and modifying. Both sections
are grids of seven columns with 2 px between the buttons (Floating: 34 x
34 px buttons; Docked: the tool buttons' own size), so the 13 constraints
take two rows (7 + 6), the two sections' columns line up, and the palette
keeps its width (300 px less the card's or dock's margins and the scroll
bar) with nothing clipped, in both layouts. With the section the palette
is taller than the Docked panel at 1280 x 800, so **Finish Sketch** is no
longer one of its rows in either layout: `wrapPalette` takes it out
(`SketchPalette::takeFinish`) and puts it under the palette's scroll
area, at the right, where it stays in sight however far the palette
scrolls (as a command panel's OK and Cancel stay under its inputs); its
places are logged with the palette's as before (`Palette Finish Sketch
at x,y`, `Palette row paletteFinish …`). The AppKit frontend, which shows
the palette without the scroll area, keeps it as the palette's last row.

- **Candidates** (`SketchPalette::isCreateTool`, `createCandidates`): the
  tools and the commands with panels of the Sketch tab's Create and Modify
  groups (Line, the rectangles, circles, arcs, Ellipse, the polygons,
  slots and splines, Point, Text, QR Code, the patterns, Mirror, Project,
  Intersect, Sketch Dimension, Sketch Fillet and Chamfer, Trim, Extend,
  Offset, Move/Copy, the Edit commands, …), not the actions (Delete,
  Cut, Copy, Paste, Construction, Centerline), in the ribbon's order: the
  Create group, then Modify, a submenu's commands together where its first
  one is (as `Ribbon::createGroup`).
- **Counts**: each start of a candidate while a sketch is edited
  (`MainWindow::trigger` in sketch mode, so from the ribbon, the palette,
  a shortcut or the command search) adds one to its count in the local
  settings, `sketchToolCounts/<command id>` (`sketchToolCounts/sketch.line=12`;
  `sketch::countPaletteTool`). A tool started otherwise (an edit's
  double-click, Paste) is not counted.
- **The choice** (`sketch::choosePaletteCreateTools`, plain Qt Core, unit
  tested in `app/tests/palette_create_tools.cpp`): the commands pinned on
  the Sketch tab (`toolbarPins/SKETCH`, [Pinned commands](#pinned-commands))
  first in their order, then the counted tools, the most started first (a
  tie in the ribbon's order), then the defaults, at most 14 and only
  candidates. The defaults, before anything is counted, are Line,
  Rectangle (2-Point), Circle (Center Diameter), Arc (3-Point), Polygon
  (Circumscribed), Slot (Center to Center), Spline (Fit Point), Point,
  Trim, Extend, Offset, Sketch Fillet, Mirror and Sketch Dimension, those
  of them that exist; they also fill the places counts leave. The buttons
  show in the ribbon's order, not by count.
- **When**: the choice is made again only as the palette opens for a
  sketch (`MainWindow::enterSketch` calls `SketchPalette::chooseCreateTools`
