  settings form of the filament set (Filament, Cooling, ...), without
  `filament_density` (Density stands for it) and `filament_colour` (the
  colour is the appearance's, mitcad#1055). The Filament tab's
  **Slicer presets** (mitcad#1062) name the slicer's filament preset the
  material is based on, a row per slicer (Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer, QIDI
  Studio, PrusaSlicer): `filament_settings_id` kept per slicer, which the
  3MF export writes as the filament's preset and as the preset it
  inherits from (the Bambu Studio family's `inherits_group`,
  PrusaSlicer's `inherits_cummulative`), so that the
  slicer starts from its own preset instead of its defaults. Each list
  offers the filament presets of that slicer installed here (the
  `slicer_presets` query, `installedSlicers`) and the names the design's
  materials give it (logged `Materials presets for <slicer>: <n>`). A
  metal, a General Plastic, a resin or an other shows General alone: no
  print settings. Each change is
  `edit_material` with the item's library (the library's file and the
  design's copy, one undo step). Built-in ones are read only: their
  fields and Delete are disabled, Duplicate is the way on. **New ▾** asks
  the class (`Materials new menu: Metal | General Plastic | FDM Plastic |
  Resin | Other`), then where (the place menu above): `create_material`
  with `class` and its class's typical density (7.85 g/cm³ for a metal,
  1.24 for a General or FDM plastic, 1.15 for a resin; another material
  has none typical, so Density takes the keyboard), in a library with
  `library`; **Duplicate** asks where, then `create_material` with
  `based_on` (the copy keeps the source's class; a design's or a
  built-in material by its id, a library's item as `{library, id}`; the
  model names the copy `PLA Plastic (copy)`); the new row is selected and
  its Name takes the keyboard. Delete is `delete_material` with the
  library. The settings
  form's fields are made when the first material is shown, not while the
  window opens with none (mitcad#1018). Logs `Materials
  opened[ without a design]`, `Materials timing:
  total <n> ms[, first opening]` (its opening on the UI thread,
  mitcad#1018), `Materials: <n> items` with `Materials groups: This design
  <n> | This project <n> | My library <n> | Built-in <n>` (the headings as
  shown, their counts the search's matches) and `Materials row: <group>/<id> <name>
  (<place>)[ changed]`, `Materials search: <text>, <n> shown`, `Material
  <name> value <key> = <text>`, `Materials item <name> at x,y` (the first
  row of that name, This design's before a library's) and `Materials
  <place> item <name> at x,y` (`design`, `project`, `user`, `mitcad`),
  `Materials <what> at x,y`
  (`search`; `name`, `copy_to`, `header_duplicate` beside Built-in; `class`,
  `density`, `appearance` on General;
  `new`, `duplicate`, `delete`, `close`; `import`, `import_into`,
  `details`), `Materials editing: <line>`,
  the form's `Materials settings field <key> at x,y` (`clear <key>`, `tab
  <category>` with `tab general`, `search`, `advanced`; a slicer's preset
  row `filament_settings_id.<slicer>`), `Material selected: <name>
  (<place>)`, `Material <name> (<place>) <field> = <value>`, `Material
  created: <id> in <place>`, `Material duplicated: <name> as <id> in
  <place>`, `Material deleted: <name> (<place>)`, `Material copied to
  <place>: <name>`, `Materials changed elsewhere: <name>` (`use`,
  `keep`) with `Material <name>: <cmd>`, and
  refusals `Materials: <cmd> refused: <reason>`
  - **Material properties** (mitcad#1213, `print/MaterialProperties.*`,
    [commands.md](../core/model-api/src/commands.md#material-properties)).
    General's Density is in the design's density unit (g/cm³, lb/in³ in
    an inch design); under Appearances `MaterialPropertiesBox`:
    **Mechanical** (Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, Yield strength),
    **Thermal** (Maximum service temperature, Coefficient of thermal
    expansion) and, for an FDM plastic, **Printing** (Extruder temperature
    and Bed temperature: the filament's `temperature` and
    `bed_temperature`, the Filament tab's own values), each a field
    (`materialProperty_<key>`) with its unit from the `material_units`
    query (the design's system; temperatures in Preferences › General ›
    Temperature unit, the setting `units/temperature`, °C by default); a
    value not given empty with the placeholder "Not given". A field is
    saved at Enter or when it is left (`edit_material`'s `properties` or
    `filament` in the model's units, an emptied one null), a value that
    is not a number refused under the fields. Then "Source: <source>,
    <material>, <grade>" when the material has a reference, and "Values
    are typical: check them against the supplier's data." **New ▾** ends
    with **Browse Material Dataset…** (`MaterialDatasetDialog`, a window
    titled Material Dataset: a search, the dataset's materials and their
    class, the selected one's values in the design's units, a line naming
    the dataset, its licence and that the values are typical, **Create**
    and Cancel), then asks where: `create_material` with `dataset`, the
    new one selected. **Import…** (`materialsImport`) opens a file
    (JSON or CSV), asks where, runs `import_materials` with `conflict:
    ask`; a name there already is asked once in a box titled Import
    Materials (**Keep Existing**, the default, **Replace Values**, **Keep
    Both**, Cancel), then imported in one undo step; the message line says
    "Imported from <file>: <n> added, <n> replaced, <n> kept." and a line
    per row not imported, "Row <n> (<name>) not imported: <reason>", in
    the error colour when there are any; the first one added is selected.
    **Export…** (`materialsExport`) writes the selected one's place's
    materials (none selected: the design's own; a library's whole) as
    JSON or CSV by the file's suffix, in the design's units and the
    preferred temperature unit (`export_materials`). Logs `Materials
    properties: <name>: Young's modulus 29007500 psi | Poisson's ratio not
    given | ...`, `Materials source: <reference>`, `Material <name>
    (<place>) properties = ...`/`filament = ...` through the edit's line
    (`youngs_modulus = 30000000 psi`), `Material dataset opened: <n>
    materials`, `Material dataset search: <text>, <n> shown`, `Material
    dataset selected: <name>: <values>`, `Material created from the
    dataset: <name> (<entry>) as <id> in <place>`, `Materials import
    conflicts: <names>`, `Materials import conflict: keep|replace|keep_both`,
    `Materials import: <file>: added <n>, replaced <n>, kept <n>, <n> not
    valid`, `Materials import row <n> <name>: <reason>`, `Materials
    exported: <n> to <file> (<format>, <units>, <temperature>)`, and the
    places `Materials property <key> at x,y`, `Materials import_materials
    at`, `Materials export_materials at`, `Material dataset search at`,
    `Material dataset item <name> at`, `Material dataset create at`.
    Physical Properties lists each body's material values after Density
    (the `properties` query's `material_properties`).
  - **Variants** (mitcad#1054, `print/MaterialVariantsPage.*`; one
    filament is one material, its values per printer and nozzle its
    variants, [commands.md](../core/model-api/src/commands.md#a-filaments-variants-per-printer-and-nozzle)):
    the last tab of a plastic, after its print settings
    (`SettingsForm::setEndPage`; not while searching). The variants'
    list, one row each: `Bench X, 0.4 mm nozzle` (`Bench Y, any nozzle`)
    and what differs by plain names (`Nozzle temperature 220 °C, Bed
    temperature 55 °C`; `Same as the material` with nothing), a quiet
    line saying what variants are when there are none. **Add Variant ▾**
    is a menu of the printer profiles (`library_items` of printers: their
    `variant_printer` and `nozzle`), one the material has a variant of
    disabled (`<name> (has a variant)`); a choice is `edit_material`'s
    `variant` with its printer and nozzle, the new one selected.
    **Remove Variant** removes the selected one (`variant` with
    `remove`). Under them the selected variant's values in a second
    settings form of the filament set (`setNamePrefix("variant")`:
    `variantSettingsSearch`, `variantSettingsTabs`,
    `variantSetting_<key>`), without density and colour, the material's
    own values as its placeholders: a value typed is the variant's,
    ↺ clears it back to the material's (`edit_material`'s `variant` with
    the key, null to clear). Read only for a built-in. Logs `Materials
    variants: <n>`, `Materials variant row: <label>: <values>`,
    `Materials variant selected: <label>`, `Materials variant add menu:
    <entry> | ...`, `Material <name> (<place>) variant <label> <key> =
    <text>` (`added`, `removed`), the places `Materials variant item
    <label> at x,y`, `Materials variant add at`, `Materials variant remove
    at` and the form's `Materials variant settings field <key> at x,y`.
    3D Print's material rows name the variant each body's printer
    picks (`body_material`'s `variant`): `Shop PLA for Bench X, 0.4 mm
    nozzle`.
  - **Appearances of a material** (mitcad#1055, mitcad#1083,
    `print/AppearancePicker.*`; a filament's colour is its appearance,
    [commands.md](../core/model-api/src/commands.md#a-filaments-colour-is-its-appearance)).
    **Appearances** on General is one list (`materialAppearances`) of
    every appearance the material offers (the `materials` query's
    `appearances`, its default first): each row its swatch (a small lit
    sphere that shows gloss and translucency) and name, never the id (one
    a library's material carries that is not known here: `<material>
    color` for the model's `<id>_colour`, else its id in words, its swatch
    the material's colour), the default marked **Default** in its own
    row; without any, a muted **None** row that cannot be selected. Every
    swatch, here and in the list of materials, has a 1 px edge of the role
    table's `TitleText` (`swatchEdgeColor`), so that a dark one stays
    visible on the dark panel. No separate default drop-down. The list is
    as tall as its rows (at least 3 and its buttons' column, up to 8,
    then it scrolls) and as wide as its names (260 to 320 pixels, a
    longer one elided). Beside it, within its height, **Add…**,
    **Remove** and **Make Default**; a row's context menu has Make
    Default and Remove, and Delete or Backspace on a row removes it.
    **Add…** opens the appearance library as a popover
    (`AppearancePopover`, a frameless window of its own as the tools'
    picker, not a Qt popup, which closes at once in the Windows UI tests'
    session, mitcad#1071): a search field (`appearancePickerSearch`,
    "Search appearances"), then first the appearances of the material's
    class (mitcad#1102: the appearances query's `class`) under its title
    ("FDM Plastic"), the design's and the library's together; for an FDM
    Plastic or a Resin then General Plastic's; then the rest, the
    design's under This Design and the library's under their classes'
    titles in the lists' order, Metal, General Plastic, FDM Plastic, Resin,
    Other (mitcad#1133, `appearanceSections`, as the Appearance tool's
    picker and the Appearances window; an empty
    section left out), each with its swatch and name, the
    material's ones checked, and Edit Appearances… last (the window's
    Appearances). Typing keeps the first match current and hides the
    headings of sections without a match, Return or a click
    chooses it, Down goes into the list, Escape or a click outside closes
    it. A choice adds it (`edit_material`'s `appearances` with it last), selected.
    **Remove** is the list without the selected one; when it was the
    default, the next row becomes the default and is selected (its
    tooltip names it beforehand: `Remove the default; Plastic - Black
    becomes the default`; logged `Materials appearance default removed:
    <name> becomes the default`); **Make Default** makes the selected one the
    default (`edit_material`'s `appearance`, the old one staying in the
    list). Read only for a built-in: the rows can be selected, the buttons
    and the menu's entries are disabled. Logs `Materials appearances:
    Bright Green (default) | Plastic - Black` (`none`), `Materials
    appearance selected: <name>`, `Materials appearance menu: <name>: Make
    Default | Remove`, `Materials add appearance picker opened: <n>
    appearances`, `… picker sections: FDM Plastic 16 | General Plastic 6 |
    This Design 1 | Metal 8 | Resin 3 | Other 14`, `… picker search: <text>, <n> shown`, `… picker chosen:
    <name> (<id>)` and `… picker closed`, `Material <name> (<place>)
    appearance = <id>` and `… appearances = <id>, <id>`, the places
    `Materials appearance_add at`, `Materials appearance_remove at`,
    `Materials appearance_default at` and `Materials appearance row <name>
    at x,y` (at the row's name). The AppKit frontend presents the list,
    its buttons and its context menu through the generic bridge (a native
    table, each row's swatch and name and the default's **Default**, the
    rows `material.appearance.<id>`), and Add…'s popover as the tools'
    picker popover under Add… (mitcad#1068, `showNativePicker`: the
    `AppearancePopover` stays the Qt presenter off the screen, an entry
    `appearancePickerList.item.<name>`, its window `appearancePicker`,
    logged `Native picker appearancePicker at materialAppearanceAdd: <n>
    rows`). Without a design the manager has the same. The purge
    table names a material in two colours by its appearances (`PLA Basic
    (Plastic - Black)`) and shows their volume, computed from the colours,
    read only (`tools/ui-filament-appearance-test.sh`,
    `tools/ui-macos-material-color-test.sh`, ctests
    `app.ui-macos-material-color-parity` and
    `app.ui-macos-native-material-color-parity`).
  (`tools/ui-material-test.sh`, `tools/ui-print-settings-test.sh`,
  `tools/ui-modify-test.sh`).
- **Printers and Processes** (mitcad#655; two managers since
  mitcad#1135): **Printers…** (`make.printers`, `MainWindow::printersCommand`)
  and **Processes…** (`make.processes`, `processesCommand`, icon
  `print-process`, the printed layers with print-settings' gear) in the
  Make tab's 3D Print group (mitcad#1049) after Send to Slicer, each
  opening its manager on the design's printer or process, else none;
  the last row of Send to Slicer's Printer and Process pickers (**Edit
  printers…**, **Edit processes…**, mitcad#1134) and Edit… of Property
  Sets' Printer and Process rows open the manager of that kind (`BrowserController::openProfiles`,
  `print/ProfilesDialog.*`; a picker's key of a library item selects the
  design's copy of it, which the design prints with). Each is a
  non-modal window titled Printers or Processes, laid out as Materials,
  that follows the model; both can be open at once. On the left the
  search (`Search printers`, `Search processes`) and the items of its
  kind under the places' headings by name, the design's choice marked;
  in the Processes manager each place's processes in sub-groups by
  printer (mitcad#1216), one tree level below the place, foldable as the
  places (every group open after a change of the list, so the selected
  item's sub-group is open): the printers by name, then **Any printer**;
  a process's printers are the model's `printers` of its `library_items`
  row (its `compatible_printers`, else those of the preset it inherits
  from as the import keeps them, else its name's `@` part; `processPrinters`
  in `print/ProfilePickerRows.*`), a process for several printers listed
  under each, its row under the printer it was clicked under staying the
  selected one; the search filters every sub-group, the place headings
  count each process once (logged `Processes printers: My library: Bench
  X 2 | Bench Y 2 | Any printer 1`, `Processes printer group: My library
  › Bench X: Fine, Shared`, `Processes selected under: My library ›
  Bench Y`, each row under a printer also `Processes user › Bench Y item
  Shared at x,y`; the sub-groups' native ids
  `printManager.printer.<place>.<printer>`); the sub-groups take the
  tree's indentation, as any level;
  on the right the header as Materials', the line that says where it is
  edited, and the settings form of the printer set (one category,
  Printer: printable space and nozzle, without a tab bar: a form shows
  its tabs only when there are two or more) or the process set (Quality,
  Strength, Speed, Support, Others). Each field is `edit_print_profile`
  in the item's place (a library item with its library and kind, undo
  step `Edit Process 0.20 mm Standard`; a design's item by its id).
  Under the list: **New** (asks where; in the design
  `create_print_profile` with `choose`, the design's choice in the same
  undo step; in a library with `library`), **Duplicate** (asks where;
  `create_print_profile` with `based_on`, in the design also `choose`),
  **Delete** (`delete_print_profile`, asked); **Use in this design** on
  the right makes the selected one the design's printer or process
  (`set_property` of the root's `profile`, a library item with its
  library: its copy reused or made, one undo step; shown only with a
  design, for an item the design does not use; logged `Profile used in
  this design: <kind> <name>`, its place `Processes use at x,y`). Edit
  printers… or Edit processes… on Slicer default opens the manager with
  nothing selected, the same as Property Sets' Edit…. **Import from Slicer…** at the top
  right (mitcad#829) is Send to Slicer's Import from slicer…, the one
  implementation the managers share (`print/SlicerImport.*`,
  `SlicerImportBar`): the same file dialog, `import_print_profile` with
  `into` the place the **Import into** box before the button shows
  (`setPlaces`: This design with a design open, else My library, and the
  other places; shown only with more than one; logged `Processes import
  into: My library` when chosen, its place `Processes import_into at
  x,y`); into the design the root chooses the printer and process read,
  one undo step `Import Print Settings plate.3mf`; its line (`plate.3mf
  imported`) and **Details…** (Import Details) before it; the item of
  the manager's kind that came in is then selected in its place. It
  works while Send to Slicer's panel is open too
  (`canChangePrintSettings`). Logged as 3D Print's: `Imported print
  settings from <file>: printers: …`, `Processes import: <line>`
  (refused: `Processes import refused: <reason>`, the reason on the
  line), places `Processes import at x,y`, `Processes details at x,y`.
  Whether a slicer is installed (the button's ▾) is looked for off the
  UI thread when the window shows (mitcad#1018, `Processes slicers: read
  <n> ms, <n> found`), again at each click and when Import into changes.
  The settings form's fields are made when the first item is shown. Logs
  (`Printers` in the Printers manager) `Processes opened[ without a
  design]`, `Processes timing: total <n> ms[, first opening]`,
  `Processes: <n> items`, `Processes groups: This design <n> | This
  project <n> | My library <n> | Built-in <n>` with `Processes row:
  <kind>/<id> <name> (<place>)[, the design's]`, `Processes search:
  <text>, <n> shown`, `Profile selected: <kind> <name> (<place>)`,
  `Profile shown: <kind> <name> (<place>)[, read only]` with `Profile
  <name> value <key> = <text>`, `Processes editing: <line>`, `Processes
  item <name> at x,y` (the first row of that name) and `Processes
  <place> item <name> at x,y`, `Processes <what> at x,y` (`search`,
  `name`, `copy_to`, `header_duplicate`, `new`, `duplicate`, `delete`,
  `use`, `close`), the form's `Processes settings field <key> at x,y`
  (as Materials'), `Processes new menu: …`, `Profile <name> (<place>)
  <key> = <text>`, `Profile created: <kind> <id> in <place>`, `Profile
  duplicated: <name> as <id> in <place>`, `Profile copied to <place>:
  <name>`, `Profile deleted: <name> (<place>)`, `Processes changed
  elsewhere: <name>` (`use`, `keep`) with `Profile <name>: <cmd>`,
  `Processes closed[ after changes]` and refusals `Processes: <cmd>
  refused: <reason>` (`tools/ui-print-settings-test.sh`,
  `tools/ui-print-managers-test.sh`, `tools/ui-windows-print-managers-test.ps1`,
  ctest `app.ui-windows-print-managers`).
- **Without a design** (mitcad#704, mitcad#1135; Tools › My Library… and
  its window went with mitcad#1135): with no design open
  (`DocumentHost::designOpen`: the window's design was neither opened
  nor saved nor changed, the empty Untitled design a window starts
  with) the managers work through a model of their own, an empty design
  never shown or saved (`LibraryItemsHost`, chosen at each opening and
  refresh by `ManagerHosts`): their places are My library, This project
  in a project, and Built-in, New and Duplicate make the item in My
  library at once (or ask between This project and My library), and the
  window's design does not change. When such a manager closes after a
  change, the open managers read the libraries again
  (`librariesChanged`), and a changed item the design uses is asked
  about there as another design's change. The managers stay in the Make
  tab, the one place for them with or without a design (the command
  search finds them by `my library` too); Tools has no entry of them. A
  manager opened without a design reads its items, the print keys and
  the rest off the UI thread (mitcad#1018, `readAhead`,
  `managerRequests`) and fills its list when the answers come (`Printers
  loaded: read <n> ms, list <n> ms`, `Materials loaded: …`)
  (`tools/ui-my-library-test.sh`, `tools/ui-windows-my-library-test.ps1`,
  ctest `app.ui-windows-my-library`).
- **Hidden built-ins** (mitcad#1270; `print/PrintLibrary.*`: `canHide`,
  `setItemHidden`, `withoutHidden`, `itemContextMenu`): an item of the
  base library (`library` `base`: the built-in printers, processes and
  library materials; not MitCad's own built-in materials such as Steel,
  nor the user's or the project's items, which keep Delete) has **Hide**
  beside Delete (`printManagerHide`, **Unhide** for a hidden one) and in
  its row's context menu (Duplicate, Hide or Unhide; the others
  Duplicate, Delete). The hidden ids are a user setting, QSettings
  `printLibrary/hidden_<kind>` (a list of ids), never in a design or a
  project; hiding is no undo step. A hidden item is left out of the
  managers' lists and counts, and `queryLibraryItems` leaves it out of
  every picker (Send to Slicer's Printer and Process, the Make card's,
  Property Sets', the Material tool's, the body menus'
  Material ▸, a material's Variants tab), unless the design has a copy of
  it or uses it: then it stays, as This design's (`profileSource`), in
  the managers under This design (its copy). **Show hidden**
  (`printManagerShowHidden`, a box under the list, shown while one of
  the kind is hidden or while it is on; not kept) lists them again,
  grayed (`TextHidden`) with Unhide. While My library or This project
  has an item of the kind (`hasOwnLibraryItems`), the Printers and
  Processes managers open with the Built-in group folded (at each
  opening; the user's folding is kept until the next; a search shows
  every group's matches, and the group of the item shown stays open),
  and the printer and process pickers (`profilePickerRows`) list the
  built-ins last under one **Built-in** heading, each by its whole name.
  Logs `Printers hidden: <name>`, `Printers unhidden: <name>`, `Printers
  show hidden: on|off`, `Printers grayed: <names>|none`, `Printers
  folded: Built-in|none` (the folded groups), the rows `Printers row: …,
  hidden`, `Context menu: Duplicate | Hide`, the places `Printers hide
  at x,y`, `Printers show_hidden at x,y` (`Processes …` and `Materials
  …` likewise; Materials has no folding)
  (`tools/ui-hide-built-ins-test.sh`,
  `tools/ui-windows-hide-built-ins-test.ps1`, ctest
  `app.ui-windows-hide-built-ins`; the picker's order in `app.unit`'s
  `profile_picker_rows.cpp`).
- **Import Presets** (mitcad#830; the managers' Import from Slicer):
  With an installed Bambu-family
  slicer found (mitcad#830, `slicer_presets`: Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer,
  QIDI Studio; the Flatpak's too; one with presets of the user's or with
  printers enabled in its setup) the button is **Import from Slicer ▾**,
  a menu of **From a file…** and **Presets of Bambu Studio…** for each
  slicer found (`OrcaSlicer (Flatpak)`; logged `Processes import menu:
  From a file… | Presets of Bambu Studio…`), looked for again at each
  click. Presets of… opens **Import
  Presets** (`print/SlicerPresetsDialog.*`, modal): the slicer at the top
  (a box when several were found), under it **Filter presets** (a field:
  the rows whose name contains its text in any case stay, a group with
  none hides and those with some open while it filters, and clearing it
  brings back which groups were open; a hidden row keeps its tick, which
  still counts and imports, and a group's box then ticks only the rows
  shown; Down or Enter goes to the list, Shift+Tab from the list to it),
  the user's presets under **My printers**, **My processes** and **My
  filaments**, then the slicer's own presets the user enabled there
  (mitcad#871: the printers chosen in its setup, their processes and the
  filaments chosen there, each kind by name in any case; `system` in
  `slicer_presets`) under **Bambu Studio printers**, **Bambu Studio
  processes** and **Bambu Studio filaments**, collapsed at first (Right
  or the arrow opens one) unless a row in it has a same name, and
  unticked, a box each, each group's box ticking all or none of it. A
  preset whose name the target (the place Import into shows) has
  already is in the warning colour with the
  tooltip "My library has a process of this name", unticked, with
  **Same name:** and its own **Copy** (the default: `Fine 2`) or
  **Override** (the existing item's next version) beside it (accessible
  name `Fine: same name`; the row's and the box's accessible description
  say what it meets and what Copy and Override do); choosing in it ticks
  the row. **All same names:** above the list sets every such row's
  choice (the ticks stay), shows their choice when they agree and no
  value when they differ, and shows only with such rows. New user
  presets are ticked. The name column is as wide as the names and the
  group titles, each choice beside its name. Keyboard: the list has it
  at first on its first user preset (else its first group), the current
  row framed; the arrows move it, Space ticks or unticks it (a group:
  all of it), Tab goes to the row's choice (Shift+Tab back) and on to
  Import. **Import** says how many are ticked (`Import 1 Preset`,
  `Import 3 Presets`; plain `Import`, disabled, with nothing ticked;
  Alt+I) and runs `import_slicer_presets` with
  the ticked ones (their inherited values filled in from the slicer's
  system presets; into the design one undo step `Import Presets of Bambu
  Studio`), the line saying `2 presets imported into My library`, for
  one preset its name (`Fine imported into My library`, after a Copy
  `Fine imported into My library as Fine 2`; into the design `Fine
  imported as Fine 2`), and Details… the report; the manager then shows
  the first item of its kind that came in, selected in its place
  (`Profile selected: process Fine (user)`, `Material selected: …`).
  Cancel imports nothing (`Slicer presets
  cancelled`). Logs `Slicer presets opened: <slicer>, <n> presets`,
  `Slicer presets row: <kind> <name>, ticked|unticked[, system][, same
  name: <tooltip>, copy|override]`, `Slicer presets ticked: <n>, <Import's
  text>`, `Slicer presets tick: <name> ticked|unticked`, `Slicer presets
  choice: <name> copy|override`, `Slicer presets same name:
  copy|override`, `Slicer presets all same names: copy|override|none`,
  `Slicer presets filter: <text>, <n> shown` (`Slicer presets filter
  cleared, <n> shown`), `Slicer presets current: <name>`, `Slicer
  presets focus: <name> choice` and the places `Slicer
  presets <what> at x,y` (`slicer`, `same_all`, `import`, `cancel`,
  `item <name>`: its box) (`tools/ui-my-library-test.sh`,
  `tools/ui-print-managers-test.sh`).
  One filament's presets (mitcad#1054, `slicer_presets`' `filament`,
  `printers` and `merge`): a filament of two presets or more in a group
  is one row named as the filament (`Shop PLA`: one material, its box
  ticks its presets, its Same name choice is theirs) with a row per
  preset under it named by its printers and nozzles (`Bench X, 0.6 mm
  nozzle`, the preset's name its tooltip; in the logs `Shop PLA › Bench X,
  0.6 mm nozzle`). With them, **Printers and nozzles in use** heads the
  list when the slicer's filaments are for two or more: a box each,
  ticked; unticking one disables and unticks the variant rows of it alone
  and the import's `printers` leaves them out. When the target keeps one
  filament's presets as separate materials, **Merge the separate
  materials of 1 filament** under the list (unticked; the filaments and
  their materials as its tooltip) makes the import `merge_separate`
  them first, also with nothing ticked (Import reads `Merge`; the line
  `Separate materials imported …`). Logs `Slicer presets printer: <label>,
  ticked|unticked`, `Slicer presets printer tick: <label>
  ticked|unticked`, `Slicer presets row: material <filament>, <n>
  variants`, `Slicer presets merge offered: <n>: <filament> (<material>,
  …)`, `Slicer presets merge: ticked|unticked`, `<log> merged: <name>
  (<ids>)` and the places `Slicer presets printer <label> at`, `Slicer
  presets merge at` (`tools/ui-filament-variants-test.sh`).
- **Property Sets' print settings** (mitcad#640, mitcad#655): under the
  levels, **Print settings** sums up what the most specific level prints
  with (`print_settings` of the body in its occurrence, the occurrence or
  the component), read only: the values are edited in the settings form.
  Process shows the profile chosen: a click opens a drop-down of the
  choosable items by name, no places (choosing sets that
  level's `profile`, with the item's library), **Edit…** after it opens
  the process in the Processes manager, ↺ takes a choice of that level
  away (Edit… and ↺ take the left button only, mitcad#761: a right click
  on them does nothing). Below the root the process lists its own values only, and a row
  **Own settings** of its own names what bodies and components set of
  their own (`Walls`, `3 settings`, `None`; logged `print Print
  Process/own_settings = Walls`), with those values as rows under it,
  each owner as its Source; its pencil opens the level's own values in
  the settings form (`openOwnSettings`, below); the root has none, its
  values are the process. Printer at the root likewise, its Edit… opening Printers and
  Processes; below the root, a plate having one printer, it is one line
  without values (`Bench X`).
  Material shows the body's material (not again in Source): a click or
  Edit opens Materials for the body or the component. Below Printer (at
  the root), Process and Material the values under one heading line per
  category › sub-group (small and bold on a band of the row's width, so
  it does not read as a value), in the key table's order, in the key's own
  unit (a colour as a bordered swatch with its appearance's name, the
  appearance's when unset; Yes and No as in the editors; a value per
  slicer and the filament's density not shown), no Type, and the source
  once: the group's on its row, a row's own where an owner sets it (the
  level shown too: `Body1`), in words with its kind's icon; the name column as
  wide as the names. The level's own values are bold on a tinted row;
  unset ones are the placeholder's grey in italics; computed ones (the
  levels') grey upright; the computed values do not repeat the material.
  A body's level is headed by its name alone (`Body1`). The per-level
  `Print Printer`, `Print Process`, `Print Filament` and `Print Slicer
  (…)` sets are not listed again among the levels. The row names are
  `print <set>/<key>` in the log (`Property sets row: print Print
  Process/layer_height = 0.2 mm (profile Standard (Root))`); the places
  `Property sets print <set>/<key> value at x,y`, `… edit at x,y`, `…
  clear at x,y` (`print Print Process/profile`, `print Print
  Filament/material`).
- **Own settings** (mitcad#655; `print/OwnSettingsDialog.*`,
  `BrowserController::openOwnSettings`): a body's, an occurrence's or a
  component's own process values in the same tabbed settings form as a
  process, as a slicer's per-object settings, in a small non-modal window
  titled `Body1 · Own settings` that follows the model. Every process key can
  be set from its tab; the owner's own values show set, the others show
  what it prints with as their placeholders. A change is `set_property`
  of the owner's `Print Process`, emptying a field or ↺ `remove_property`,
  one undo step each. Opened from Send to Slicer's own-settings links and
  Property Sets' Own settings. Logs `Own settings opened: <title>`,
  `Own setting <owner> <key> = <text>` (`cleared`), refusals `Own
  settings: <key> refused: <reason>`, the form's `Own settings field <key>
  at x,y` (`clear <key>`, `tab <category>`, `search`, `advanced`) and `Own
  settings close at x,y` (`tools/ui-print-settings-test.sh`).
- **Edit Parameters, limits** (mitcad#665; the model's side:
  [Parameter limits](../core/model-api/src/commands.md#parameter-limits)):
  the columns Min, Max, Step, Strict and Slider come after the star (the
  first six keep their numbers, which UI scripts use). Min, Max and Step
  are expressions edited in place (`set_parameter` `min`/`max`/`step`; an
  emptied cell removes the limit); Strict is a check box (`strict`). A
  parameter without a limit of its own shows the limits of the feature
  that uses it (the query's `intrinsic`, such as a pattern's quantity: 1
  to 10000, whole) in grey, with the feature in the tooltip; leaving such
  a cell unchanged sets nothing. A limited value is marked in its Value
  cell (`372 mm → 300 mm ▲max`, `▼min`, `◆step`) with the model's
  `limit_message`, the limit's expression and the parameters it uses in
  the tooltip, and the message line says it after the change. While an
  expression of a parameter with limits is typed, the `evaluate` query
  with `parameter` says at once that it will be limited, or refused by a
  strict parameter. A parameter with a minimum and a maximum of its own
  gets a `QSlider` (its steps when it has a step and at most 10000 of
  them, else 1000 positions); a released handle or a key sets the
  expression to the number in the parameter's unit, a click on the handle
  alone sets nothing. "Only limited" shows only the rows a limit changed.
  A feature panel's value field whose own parameter (when editing) has
  limits shows the same mark as its hint (`→ 300 mm ▲max`) and says it in
  its tooltip (`CommandSession::limitHint`), and a limited sketch
  dimension's tooltip ends with the mark and the model's message (the
  `sketch` query's `limited` and `limit_message`). Test:
  `tools/ui-parameter-limits-test.sh`.
- **Configurations** (mitcad#807; the design note
  [docs/configurations.md](../docs/configurations.md), the model's side:
  [Configurations](../core/model-api/src/commands.md#configurations-options-rows-and-rules)):
  `solid.configurations` (Configurations…, beside Edit Parameters in
  SOLID > MODIFY and in the Edit menu) opens `ConfigurationsDialog`, a
  window of its own (not modal, as Edit Parameters; the same in the
  Floating and Docked layouts) with the tabs Options, Rows, Rules and
  Bindings (mitcad#862). Every
  edit is one model command and one undo step; a refused one stays in its
  cell in red with the reason, and the message line says it. The window
  explains itself (mitcad#967): each of the first three tabs starts with a
  lead line, and an empty list, sheet or canvas shows what to do in its
  place (logged `Configurations lead Options|Rows|Rules: <line>` and
  `Configurations empty Options|Rows|Rules: <text>`):
  Options "Options are the choices a user of this design makes, such as
  Color or Length. Each option is a user parameter." and "No options yet.
  Add Option… makes a parameter an option."; Rows "A row is a ready-made
  combination of the options, with its designation and part number." and
  "No rows yet. Add Row saves the options' values as a row."; Rules "Rules
  take away values and combinations that are not allowed. Most designs
  need none." and "No rules yet. A rule is, for example: when Color is
  Black, Length is at most 1000 mm." ([The rule block
  editor](#the-rule-block-editor)). The window has no Help button: the app
  has no route that opens the user guide.
  - **Options**: the options in choice order. Rows are dragged into their
    order (`InternalMove`; items take no drops, so an option never lands
    under another) or moved with Move Up and Move Down; either is
    `set_configurations` with the new `options`. Add Option… offers the
    user parameters that are no option yet (a closed table's parameter
    columns among them, shown as `k (a parameter column)`;
    `configurations::optionCandidates`) and New Parameter (name, unit,
    value): `add_parameter` (for a new one) and `set_configurations` as one
    undo step `Add Option <name>`. Every row without a value of it takes
    the parameter's current value (`configurations::currentConstant`: its
    expression when it names no other parameter or table, else its value
    as shown), so a closed table with rows takes the option, and a
    parameter column moves to the options with its rows' values
    (`configurations::withOption`, mitcad#1044; the dialog says so when the
    table has rows). Remove Option takes it out of `options`
    and out of the rows (the parameter stays). The columns are named in the
    approved words of mitcad#968 (docs/ui-conventions.md,
    "Configurations"): Option, Unit, Possible Values, Value, Comment, By
    Formula and Used By (logged `Configurations options header: Option |
    Unit | …`). Possible Values, the option's domain (double-click or Edit
    Possible Values…, the window `Possible Values`: List, one value per
    line, the parameter's `values` limit;
    Range, its `min`, `max` and `step`; Table Column (Alt+T, mitcad#849),
    a column of the design's tables as the `values` limit `Table.Column`,
    offered from `formula_help`'s `tables` by the option's kind (a text
    option text columns, a number option the others); Free; a text option
    is a list, a column or free) is one `set_parameter`, sending only the
    limits that change. A column domain shows as the column and its values
    (`Screws.Size: M3, M4, M5`; `configurations::valuesColumn`); while
    rules restrict the option, the cell's tooltip gives its allowed values
    and the rules (`restricted_by`). Value is the option's current value
    (`configurations::valueCell`): the `configure` query's `text`, so it
    follows every choice, row and adjustment; it is edited through
    `configure`, so the cascade runs. Comment is `set_parameter`
    `comment`; By Formula marks an option whose expression is a formula
    (the `configure` query's `driven`): its Value is the evaluated value,
    never the formula, with `Expression: <expression>` as its tooltip, and
    is not edited.
  - **Rows**: a `QTableWidget` with Name, a column per option (texts
    without quotes, numbers as their expressions), a closed table's other
    `parameters` (parameter columns), Designation, Part Number and Supplier
    URL; Only these rows (the table's `closed`, the tooltip "Allow only
    the combinations listed in the Rows tab"); Add
    Row (the next free `Row<n>`, with the options' expressions as they are
    now), Generate Rows from Table… (mitcad#849: the window `Generate Rows
    from Table` chooses a table of the design, its key column and an option
    or a user parameter, offering first the column an option's values come
    from and that option (`configurations::keyOption`); Generate sends
    `generate_configuration_rows`, one undo step, and the message line says
    which rows it added or updated, with any moves; disabled while the
    design has no tables), Delete Row, Set as Default (the default row's
    name is bold), Add Column… and Remove Column (mitcad#999, below) and
    Apply (`apply_configuration`; the moves in the message
    line and the status bar). **Add Column…** (the window `Add Column`)
    makes another parameter a column of a closed table, as the d, P, s
    and k of a library screw: it offers the user parameters that are
    neither an option nor a column (`configurations::columnCandidates`) and
    New Parameter (name, unit, value, as Add Option…), and sends
    `add_parameter` (for a new one) and `set_configurations` with the
    parameter appended to `parameters` and each row's value the
    parameter's current expression (`configurations::withColumn`), as one
    undo step (`Add Column <name>` with a new parameter, else `Edit
    Configurations`). An open table becomes closed with it, Only these
    rows turning on (an open table's rows set options only): the dialog
    says so, and the button's tooltip. The column's cells are edited as an option's (a bare number
    gets the parameter's unit). **Remove Column** takes the current
    cell's parameter column out of `parameters` and the rows
    (`configurations::withoutColumn`, one `set_configurations`); the
    parameter stays with its value. It is enabled while the current cell
    is in a parameter column (not an option's). **Filling a closed table**
    (mitcad#1044, docs/configurations.md decision 12): Generate Rows from
    Table… lists the table's other columns under Columns (Alt+C) as checks,
    all checked, sent as `columns` (the rows set those parameters, made with
    the columns' units when the design has none, the table closed; the
    message names the parameters made). **Import CSV…** (Alt+I; Qt's file
    dialog `Import Rows from CSV`) reads the file and shows the window
    `Import Rows` with `configuration_rows_csv_preview`: the summary, each
    column with what it is (key option, option, parameter column, a new
    parameter, row name, designation, part number, supplier URL), the rows,
    refused cells in red and the table's problem, which disable Import;
    Import sends `import_configuration_rows_csv` (one undo step). **Export
    CSV…** (Alt+X) writes `configuration_rows_csv`'s text to the file
    chosen (`Rows.csv` by default). The sheet selects ranges of cells:
    Ctrl+C copies the block from the top left selected cell to the bottom
    right as tab-separated lines (`configurations::writeBlock`), Ctrl+V
    pastes the clipboard's block (`configurations::readBlock`, a
    spreadsheet's copy) at the current cell, each cell as if typed into it,
    rows added below the last as Add Row makes them
    (`configurations::pasteBlock`), as one `set_configurations`; a refused
    paste keeps each pasted cell in red with the reason. Delete (or
    Backspace) empties the selected cells (`configurations::clearCells`; a
    name stays). The keys work outside a cell's editor and come before the
    application's shortcuts. The AppKit frontend (mitcad#1355) selects the
    same ranges through the sheet's own mouse and keys
    (`NativeCellSelectionProperty`: a press, Shift and Command presses,
    the arrows with or without Shift; a double press or F2 edits a cell;
    each selected cell tinted, the current one framed) and sends Command+C,
    Command+V, Delete and Backspace, and the Edit menu's Copy and Paste, to
    the sheet (`NativeModelKeysProperty`); logs `Native cell selection:
    configurationsRows current=1,3 selected=0,2 0,3 1,2 1,3`. A cell edit is `set_configurations` with the table; a typed
    text gets quotes for a text option and the unit for a bare number
    (`configurations::rowExpression`). Before an option's value is written,
    the row's combination is tried with the `configure` query's `values`
    (nothing changes): a `refused` answer refuses the cell with the rule's
    name and message, and nothing is sent (decision 4: rules hold
    everywhere). Each row is tried so whenever the window reads the model:
    a row that breaks a rule is marked in the cells of the options the
    refusal names (else in its name) with the rule in the tooltip. The line
    above the sheet names the row the options match (`row` of the query).
  - **Rules**: `makeConfigurationRulesPage` (`browser/ConfigurationRulesPage.cpp`,
    a `ConfigurationPage` the window refreshes with itself): the rule block
    editor of mitcad#808, [The rule block editor](#the-rule-block-editor).
  - **The Configuration bar** (`ConfigurationBar`): the content of the
    **Configuration panel**, a left panel of its own between the Projects
    panel and the browser (mitcad#1020,
    `browser/MainWindowConfigurationPanel.cpp`; until then the top of the
    browser): the Floating card `configurationDock` (title Configuration,
    collapsible, its collapsed state kept in
    `configuration/panelCollapsed`; it shares the left column, [The left
    column](#browser-timeline-and-parameters)) or the Docked dock `configurationDock` (above the
    browser's, the Projects dock above it; movable, not closable). The
    panel shows while the bar is present (`ConfigurationBar::isPresent`,
    `presenceChanged`): hidden while the design has no options and no
    rows. The bar sits in a scroll area of its own, so the panel scrolls
    when the column gives it less than its height. With the panel's header
    (Configuration) the row chooser's label is Row (`setHeaderTitled`;
    logged `Configuration bar row label: Row`; mitcad#968), also in the
    AppKit frontend, which presents the same bar in a Configuration card
    of its own between Projects and Browser, one row per option, sharing
    its left column with a dragged, remembered boundary (`native/leftSplit`;
    [docs/native-macos-ui.md](../docs/native-macos-ui.md)). A row combo (`apply_configuration`; `No row` while the options
    match none), then a chooser per option in choice order from the
    `configure` query: a combo of the `allowed` list, a field and a
    `QSlider` for an `allowed` range with both bounds (positions by its
    step, else 100; a released handle or a key sends the number in mm or
    rad), a field alone for a range without both bounds or a free option,
    the value alone for a By Formula one (`driven`; the tooltip `By
    formula: <expression>`). The choosers' tooltips say `Allowed values:
    …` and `Restricted by <rules>`. A value that is not an allowed value
    now is shown but not offered. A choice is `configure` with that
    option's value (a text option's text, a number option's expression with
    the unit for a bare number: `configurations::chooserValue`), one undo
    step. The answer's `moves` (automatic adjustments, Information) show as
    a notice under the choosers and in the status bar (`Length 1500 mm →
    1000 mm: Black is short`; `Only these rows` for the restriction to the
    listed rows); a `refused` answer or a refusal shows in red (Error). The
    widgets are made again only when the choices change; refreshed with the
    browser.
  - **Edit Parameters** marks an option with the configurations icon on
    its name (the tooltip: an option of the configuration, and By formula
    for a driven one); an option the rules restrict now (`restricted_by`)
    shows the restricted range's bounds in grey in Min, Max and Step where
    the parameter has no limit of its own (as a feature's fixed limits),
    else in their tooltips (`Restricted to <bound> by <rules>`), and a
    restricted list in the Value tooltip (`Allowed values now: … (restricted
    by …)`).
  - **The JSON** is read and made in one place,
    `browser/ConfigurationsData.*` (plain Qt Core, `app.unit`:
    `app/tests/configurations_data.cpp`): the table (what the window does
    not edit, `rules` and unknown fields, goes back unchanged), the option
    reports, moves and refusals, and the commands.
  - **Bindings** (mitcad#862, the fourth tab; `ConfigurationBindingsPage`,
    a `ConfigurationPage` the window refreshes first, [Bindings at a
    glance](#bindings-follow-option-suppress-when-show-when)): every
    binding of the design as a table, Item (with the browser's icon of a
    body, a feature's type or an occurrence), Property (Appearance,
    Material, Shown, `Face 1 (side)` with the face's topological name in
    its tooltip, Suppressed), Follows (`Color: Black → Paint - Black, …`,
    `when Holes = Yes`, or the expression, as the card reads them; the
    column that stretches) and Now (what it gives now, with its swatch).
    **Option:** (mitcad#968; All options, or one of the parameters the
    bindings use) and an item search filter it. A binding whose results name no
    appearance or material (`no appearance “paint_purple”`), or that the
    model warns about, is a warning row (yellow, the warning icon in Now);
    the problem is in the row's tooltip and, while the row is selected, in
    the status line (`⚠ no appearance “paint_purple” — 6 bindings, 1
    warning`). The first row is selected when the tab fills with none
    selected, so that the buttons work at once. **Edit…** (or a
    double-click) opens the fx card's editor (`BindingActions::edit`:
    `BrowserController::editBinding`); **Select in Browser** selects the
    item and shows its row (a feature in the timeline too); **Remove
    Binding** sends the property's command with an empty `expression`
    (the value it gave stays, one undo step: `Clear Appearance Expression
    of Body2`). The status line counts them (`6 bindings, 1 warning`, `2
    of 6 bindings`). On **Options**, **Used By** says per option `used by
    N bindings` (the column as wide as its text; the users in its
    tooltip; a double-click shows the Bindings tab filtered by it). Logged
    (`driven by` is the Option filter's key in the log):
    `Configurations bindings filter label: Option:`,
    `Configurations binding Body1 Appearance: <follows>; now <now>[;
    warning <w>]`, `Configurations bindings status: 6 bindings, 1
    warning`, `Configurations bindings selected warning: no appearance
    “paint_purple”`, `Configurations bindings
    driven by Holes, search '': 2 of 6 bindings`, `Configurations option
    Color used by 4 bindings`, `Configurations binding edit|select: Body1
    Appearance`, `Configurations binding removed: Body2 Appearance` (`…
    refused: <reason>`), and the places `Configurations binding Body2
    Appearance at x,y`, `Configurations bindings driven by|search|edit|
    select|remove at x,y`. Test: `tools/ui-bindings-glance-test.sh`.
  Tests: `tools/ui-configurations-test.sh` (Linux: two options and a row
  made and applied, a choice in the bar, a rule's adjustment as a notice,
  the Value column after it, a row value refused with the rule's name, and
  Only these rows adjusting a choice to a listed row),
  `tools/ui-configuration-terms-test.sh` (Linux, mitcad#968: the Options
  headers, the Bindings tab's Option filter, the bar's Row label, the
  Value column with a By Formula option's evaluated value and expression,
  not edited, and after a change in the bar),
  `tools/ui-configuration-tables-test.sh`
  (Linux, mitcad#849: a table column as an option's possible values, rows
  generated from the table, a combination in table rule built and saved,
  and a generated row applied with the rule's adjustment),
  `app.ui-windows-configurations` and
  `app.ui-macos-configurations` (the driver script
  `tools/ui-scripts/configurations.mitcad-ui`: the window opens with the
  approved labels and tooltip as widget properties, a choice in the bar
  changes the body), `tools/ui-configuration-rows-test.sh`
  (Linux, mitcad#1044: Import CSV… of a table of screw sizes through its
  preview, a block of cells copied and pasted, Add Option… taking a
  parameter column, and a size on the bar setting the row's parameter
  column), `app.ui-windows-configuration-rows` (the driver script
  `tools/ui-scripts/configuration-rows.mitcad-ui`: the import, Add
  Option…, the bar) and `app.ui-macos-native-rows-appearances`
  (`tools/ui-macos-native-rows-appearances-test.sh`, mitcad#1355: in the
  AppKit frontend a 2 x 2 block of the Rows sheet selected, copied, pasted
  two rows down and a cell emptied; also the Appearances headings).
- **Property Sets** (mitcad#496): `view.property_sets` (the command
  search: the selected body or component, else the root), the browser's
  menus of a body (after Appearance...) and of a component (after Design
  Policy...) and the view's menu (after Appearance...) call
  `BrowserController::openPropertySets` with a `PropertyTarget` (a body,
  an occurrence path, a component): `PropertySetsDialog`
  (`browser/PropertySetsDialog.*`), a non-modal window titled Property
  Sets, refreshed with the model. It shows the `property_sets` query's
  levels (body, occurrence, component) as top rows, their sets foldable
  below them (folded sets stay folded), each property's key, value (in
  the shown unit), type (an own type's tooltip names its base) and source
  (`ifc, edited` with the source's value as the tooltip; `inherited` for
  an occurrence's component values; `overrides`; computed values greyed,
  read-only). Computed values (check box, on) asks `computed`. A
  double-click or F2 edits a value in place: text typed as the model reads
  it (`1.2 m`, `500 g`, `yes`); an own type with allowed values, and a
  yes/no, as a drop-down over the cell whose change sets it (its arrow
  keys and wheel work without opening its list). Editing an inherited
  value sets the occurrence's own. Typing a key's first letters goes to
  its row (the tree's keyboard search). Add... (level, set, key, type,
  value), Remove (an own stored value; an occurrence's component value
  shows again) and Types... (`Property Types`: the own types with their
  values; Define with name, base type, comma-separated values, unit,
  description; Remove) run one model command each; refusals stay in the
  window's message line.
- **Find in Design by property** (mitcad#496): a search text with a
  comparison (`=`, `<`, `>`, `~`: `FireRating = EI60`,
  `Pset_WallCommon/FireRating = EI60`, `Mass > 10 kg`, `Name ~ wall`)
  asks the model's `property_search` (`FindDialog::setPropertySearch`, set
  by the controller) and lists the bodies and occurrences it found
  (`FindOptions::propertyOwners`): an occurrence by its own or inherited
  value, a body in each of its places; the component and visibility
  filters still apply. A search the model cannot read finds nothing and is
  logged.

### The rule block editor

The Rules tab of the Configurations window (mitcad#808; design:
docs/configurations.md, "Block editor", decision 6) is native Qt, with no
dependency of its own: `configurations/RulesPage` (the tab), on
`configurations/RuleCanvas` (the palette and a `QGraphicsView` canvas)
and `configurations/RuleBlocks` (plain Qt Core: a rule as blocks, read
from and written to the model's JSON). `browser/ConfigurationRulesPage.cpp`
gives the window `makeConfigurationRulesPage`, a `RulesSource` on its
`DocumentHost`: the `configurations` query (the table and its
`problems`), the `configure` query (the options' kinds, units and
domains: `rules::optionInfos`), the
`check_rules` query, `formula_help`'s `tables` (the design's tables and
their columns, for combination in table), and `set_configurations` with the table as the model
has it (through the configurations' JSON adapter, so the options and rows
go back unchanged) and the page's `rules`; Undo and Redo are the model's
`undo` and `redo`.

- **The tab explains itself** (mitcad#967): its lead line at the top,
  "Rules take away values and combinations that are not allowed. Most
  designs need none."; for a closed table (the Rows tab's Only these rows)
  a second line, "Only these rows is on: only the combinations listed in
  the Rows tab are allowed, so rules are not needed." (Add keeps
  working); and while the design has no rules the
  canvas says "No rules yet. A rule is, for example: when Color is Black,
  Length is at most 1000 mm." (else, with no rule selected, "Add a rule,
  or choose one in the list.").
- **The text** (mitcad#965) is the first way to write a rule: the
  selected rule as text, a line per part, in sight under the blocks
  (`&Text`, Alt+T; the hint beside it: "Enter saves the rule, Shift+Enter
  starts a new line, Esc restores it."). The grammar is what the text
  prints (`rules::ruleText`): `when <condition>` or `always` first (no
  such line: always), then `then <action>` and `else <action>` lines,
  `then nothing` for no action, and `when <condition> then <action>` (or
  `always then <action>`) as one line too. The actions are `<option> min
  <value>`, `max`, `step`, `<option> only <value>; <value>…` (also `allow
  only`), `<option> not <value>; …` (also `exclude`), `require
  <condition>[: <message>]`, `forbid: <message>`, `combination in table
  <table> [(<option> = <column>, …)]` and an action the editor has no
  block for as its JSON (`{…}`). Enter, or leaving the text, reads it
  (`rules::ruleFromText`, the inverse of `ruleText`; the condition and the
  values through the expression reader of the blocks) and saves it as a
  block edit is saved (`Edit <rule> as text`, one undo step `Edit
  Configurations`); the blocks are drawn from the saved rule, and a block
  edit writes the text anew. A canonical text reads into a rule that
  prints the same text; any other is read and printed canonically
  (`Color = 'Black'` as `Color == 'Black'`, `AND(a;b)` as `and(a; b)`); a
  line that is the same as the saved rule's keeps that part's own text and
  JSON object, so an unchanged rule is not changed, and the option actions
  of one option on lines one after another are one JSON object. A line
  that does not read is marked (the line in the error colour, the place
  underlined, the caret there), the status line says `Not saved: Line 2,
  column 17: 1000 needs a unit: Length is in mm (1000 mm)`, and nothing is
  sent; the reasons: a line that starts with no keyword, a when that is
  not first or not alone, an unknown action (`maximum is no action: write
  min, max, step, only, not, require, forbid or combination in table`), an
  option the table does not have, min, max or step on a text option, a
  missing value or condition, a number without its unit for an option with
  a unit, a text option's value without quotes (`Black is a text: write it
  in quotes, 'Black'`), a text not closed, a parenthesis without its pair.
  Esc restores the rule's text. An empty rule's text is empty and shows
  example lines made from the design's options (`rules::exampleRuleText`:
  the first text option's first value and the first number option's
  largest value, `when Color == 'Black'` / `then Length max 1000 mm`).
- **The list**: a rule per row, its name (edited in place: double-click,
  F2; Add opens the new rule's name at once; an empty or taken name is
  refused), the enabled check and a warning mark whose tooltip says why:
  `Not saved yet: fill its dashed places`, `Not saved: its else has no action`,
  `Not saved: <the model's refusal>`, or the model's `problems` that name
  the rule. Add, Duplicate (`<name> 2`), Delete; Insert (Add's menu) and
  Delete in the list.
- **Add** (mitcad#966) opens a menu of templates (`rules::ruleTemplates`,
  `ruleFromTemplate`), each a complete rule whose every place is filled
  from the design's options, saved at once (the user replaces its values),
  named for what it does: **Limit a range when…** (`when <the first text
  option> == <its first value>` / `then <the first number option> max
  <its domain's largest value>`, "Limit Length when Color is Black";
  disabled without a number option), **Allow only some values when…**
  (`… then <another option> only <its first value>`, "Length only 300 mm
  when Color is Black"), **Forbid a combination…** (`when and(<A> == …;
  <B> == …)` / `then forbid: Black with 300 mm is not made`, "No Black with
  300 mm"), **Only the combinations of a table…** (`then combination in
  table <the design's first table> (<option> = <column>, …)`, "Combinations
  in Made"; disabled while the design has no tables) and, apart and last,
  **Empty rule** (`Rule <n>`, no condition and no action, for the canvas or
  the text). Each entry's tooltip is the rule's text it makes, or why it is
  disabled; a name already taken gets ` 2`. The rule's name editor opens at
  once.
- **Blocks** (`RuleBlocks`): a rule's `when`, `require` and the values of
  its actions are expression text in the model. Each is read into blocks:
  compare (`==`, `=`, `<>`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, one at the top),
  `and`/`or`/`not` (any case), is one of (`or(x == a; x == b; …)`: one name
  compared with values), names, numbers with a unit (`1000 mm`, `-5 mm`,
  `10 mm^2`), texts, table columns (`Colors.Name`), parentheses around any
  of them. Everything else is a formula block holding its text. A block
  keeps the exact text it was read from and prints it while neither it
  nor a block in it changes, so a rule that is opened and saved keeps its
  text character for character; an edited block prints canonically
  (`Color == 'Black'`, `and(a; b)`, a comparison in a comparison in
  parentheses). An action object of the JSON becomes a block per key
  (`{"option": "Depth", "min": …, "max": …}`: min and max) and is written
  back as one object; an action or field the editor does not know is kept
  as it is (`OtherAction`, the rule's other fields, `comment`).
- **The canvas**: the rule's frame with `when` (or `always`), `then` and
  `else`; value blocks with a plug on their left, action blocks with a
  notch and a tab, empty sockets and the end of a list (`+`) dashed, a slot
  before each action and `+ action` after the last. A value or logic block
  fits only a value socket (an empty one, or a value it replaces, or the
  `+` of and, or, is one of, allow only, exclude); an action fits only a
  then or else slot; the Rule group's entries (when … then, then (always),
  else) apply to the whole rule. A palette entry dragged over the canvas
  highlights where it would go (by the mouse's own press, move and
  release: no platform drag and drop); a block is moved the same way, and
  deleted when dropped on the palette. A new name, number, text, column or
  formula opens its editor at once (a name with the first option, an
  action with the first option, min, max and step with the first number
  option). A new action comes with its values (mitcad#966,
  `rules::fillSockets`): min, max and step its option's smallest value,
  largest value and step (else `1 <unit>`), allow only and exclude its
  first value, require `<the first option> == <its first value>`; it is
  complete and saved at once, and the focus goes to its value, so Enter
  edits it (no empty socket to fill first, never an empty formula block).
  Each palette entry's tooltip (mitcad#967, `PaletteEntry::tip`, also the
  native palette's) says what the block does in one sentence, with an
  example in the text's form: max "Limits an option's largest value.
  Example: Length max 1000 mm.", is one of "True when the option has one of
  the listed values. Example: Color is one of 'Red', 'Black'.", require
  "The combination is allowed only while this holds; otherwise the message
  shows. Example: require Depth >= Length / 4: too shallow.", and so on for
  every entry; the palette's own tooltip says how to drag. Fields (an action's option, a comparison's operator as a menu,
  a message, a table, its columns `Color=Color, Length=Length`) open on a
  click, blocks on a double-click; a formula opens in the Formula Editor
  (`FormulaEditor`, any kind) and is read into blocks again.
- **Combination in table** (`in_table`, mitcad#806, #849): a new block
  opens its table at once, completed from the design's tables as it is
  typed. A table of the design maps each option to its column of the same
  name (else of the same name in another case), keeping the mappings the
  table still has (`rules::inTableColumns`), so the block and its table are
  one complete edit that the model takes. Its columns field opens `Table
  Columns`, a column of the table (or none) per option; for a table the
  design does not have, the columns are typed (`Color=Color,
  Length=Length`).
- **Keyboard**: the palette takes Enter on an entry (put at the canvas's
  focus: its socket or slot, else after the focused action, else the
  then's end or the first empty socket); the canvas takes Left and Right
  (the blocks in order), Up and Down (the nearest place in the row above
  or below), Enter or F2 (edit; on a socket or a slot: the palette),
  Delete or Backspace (the block; on `when` or `else`: that section), the
  menu key or Shift+F10 (Edit, Edit as Formula…, Move Up, Move Down,
  Delete; Add When, Apply Always, Add Else, Remove Else). The labels
  `&Rules`, `&Palette`, `&Blocks` and `&Text` and the buttons `&Add` (its
  menu: `&Limit a range when…`, `&Allow only some values when…`, `&Forbid
  a combination…`, `&Only the combinations of a table…`, `&Empty rule`),
  `D&uplicate`, `&Delete` and `Chec&k Rules` take Alt.
- **Saving**: each edit is `set_configurations` at once, one undo step
  (`Edit Configurations`), when every rule is complete (a name, no empty
  socket, an else with an action: the model keeps no empty else). A new
  block whose editor opens at once and the value typed in it are one
  edit, said when the editor closes (as the block came when Esc cancels
  or nothing changed): an empty text is never a step of its own. An edit
  that leaves an empty socket, or that the model refuses, stays on the
  page (marked in the list, a line under the canvas says why: "Rule 1 and
  Rule 2 are not saved yet: fill their dashed places.", "Rule 1 is not
  saved yet: fill its dashed places.", `Not saved: <the model's
  refusal>`, mitcad#967) until an
  edit completes it. Each empty place is marked with what goes there
  (mitcad#968, `rules::emptyPlaceHint`): its tooltip `Not saved yet:
  choose an option.` (`enter a value`, `add a condition`, `choose a
  table`, `add an action`), and in the AppKit frontend its hit target's
  accessibility label `Empty place: Choose an option`
  (`RuleCanvas::pieceCaption`; the place at a list's end its hint alone);
  user-facing text calls them empty places, or dashed places for their
  look, never sockets or slots; Ctrl+Z in the page takes such edits back one by one,
  then runs the design's Undo; the platform's Redo keys its Redo. A refresh
  of the window keeps them. With Add's complete rules, such drafts come only
  from canvas edits that empty a socket.
- **Check Rules**: the `check_rules` report's
  `lines` (else its parts in words), under the canvas; with changes not
  saved yet it says that the saved rules were checked.
- The editor follows the theme's palette (its block colours are the same
  in both themes; sockets and fields use the palette's base and text) and
  is the same in the Floating and Docked layouts.

Tests: `app.unit` (`app/tests/rule_blocks.cpp`: the round trip of every
rule of the design note and of commands.md, and of rules with formula
blocks; canonical text; every such rule through the text reader and back,
a non-canonical text read canonically, a wrong line's place and reason;
the edits; Add's templates, each a complete rule, the range template
disabled without a number option, an action with its values filled; a
tooltip of its own per palette entry whose example reads; the page on a
design of the test's own, with its text, its status line's words and the
closed table's line; a combination in table whose columns follow its
table) and `tools/ui-configuration-rules-test.sh` (Linux: Add › Empty
rule and "Black is short" typed as two lines in Docked, a wrong line
marked and not saved, the Configuration bar's Length limited by the rule;
a rule built with the keyboard only in Floating; Check Rules lists a value
that is never allowed; Add › Limit a range when… saved at once, its value
replaced by a number dragged from the palette, the bar following it).
`tools/ui-configurations-test.sh` finds the three lead lines and the empty
states in the log.

## Joints

The ASSEMBLE group of the SOLID tab (mitcad#55, `commands/JointCommands.cpp`;
the model's side in commands.md, "Joints"). A joint goes into the active
component; an edit keeps the joint's own (a hidden `component` input). Its
origins are geometry of occurrences inside that component: picks carry
paths from the root (`O1/O4`), which `build` makes paths from the
component, and `load` makes them paths from the root again through the
component's first occurrence. A pick outside the component fails the
build with a message.

- **Joint** (`assemble.joint`, J): Origin A and Origin B (faces with a
  plane, axis or centre; straight and circular edges and sketch curves;
  points, axes and planes: `givesFrame`), Type, Slide Along (sliders),
  Offset, Angle, Flip, and per free motion of the type a Limits check
  (Minimum, Maximum) and a Rest check (Rest Value). The origin inputs
  show the origin's planes only as its light bulb does (mitcad#1030), so
  a hidden origin covers no component. Offset's arrow and Angle's ring stand on the frame
  the model resolves origin B to (else A): the `joint_frame` query, so a
  pick shows where its origin snaps. A driven `position` is kept through
  an edit (hidden input) for the motions the type still has; limits with
  a minimum but no maximum cannot be edited (`canEdit`).
- **As-Built Joint** (`assemble.as_built_joint`): Component A and B (in the
  browser, or bodies they place), Type, Motion Origin (optional), limits.
  `relative` is recorded from the `components` query's placements (B's
  inverse times A's); an edit keeps the recorded one while A and B stay.
- **Joint Origin** (`assemble.joint_origin`): geometry of the active
  component itself, Offset, Angle, Flip; a `frame_override` is kept.
  **Mount Frame** (mitcad#525; commands.md, "Mount frames") makes it a
  mount frame of the part, for placing it from a library: Name, Mounts
  (On a face, Into a hole (its shaft), Onto a shaft (its hole), Grid of
  cells, Foot on a grid), Moves (the joint a placement makes: Fixed, Free
  on the face, Turns, Turns and slides, Slides, as the kind takes them),
  and for a grid Pitch X and Y and Cells X and Y, for a foot Pitch X and Y
  and Footprint X and Y; the feature's `mount`. Logged as `Added joint
  origin JointOrigin1: origin (0, 0, 0), normal (0, 0, 1), mount head
  (shaft, cylindrical)`.
- **Rigid Group** (`assemble.rigid_group`): two or more components; a pick
  inside a sub-assembly stands for the occurrence placed in the component.
- **Drive Joint** (`assemble.drive_joint`): a joint (a feature: the
  timeline, the Joints folder, or the newest drivable one), its Motion and
  the value (Angle or Distance, with a ring or an arrow on the joint's
  frame B). It runs `drive_joint` while the inputs change, as sketch
  commands do (`sketchCommand`), and OK keeps it: one undo step `Drive
  Joint1`. Choosing another motion or joint takes its value where it is
  (a choice's `onChange` may set values; those it leaves NaN are evaluated
  again).
- **Assembly Constraint** (`assemble.constraint`, mitcad#148; the model's side in
  commands.md, "Assembly constraints"): a `constraint_set` in the active
  component, its rows a `listInput` (`rows`, Add Constraint): Geometry 1
  and Geometry 2 (as Joint's origins: `givesFrame`), Type, and per type
  Second Face (center), Offset (align, insert), Angle (angle), Flip,
  Lock Rotation (inserts), Limits with Minimum, Maximum and Rest (align:
  lengths, angle: angles). Type's first option is Automatic, labelled
  with the type the picks fit best (`Automatic (Insert)`), from the
  model's `constraint_row` query (remembered per pair of picks), which
  `build` writes; the other options set it. Geometry 1's occurrence is a
  ghost until the row's Geometry 2 is picked (`ghostUntilPicked`, the
  row's state). A locked insert records the turn where the picks are (the
  query's `twist`); an edit keeps the recorded one (hidden
  `lock_angle`). The preview solves the rows with the joints and
  constraints before them and shows the moved components; OK logs
  `Added constraint Constraint1: insert placed, moved O2; DOF 1`. In the
  browser a set is a row of the Joints folder (icon `constraint`) with
  its rows under it (`Insert (Pin:1, Plate:1)`, red when a row does not
  hold at the marker); the folder's menu has New Constraint.
  `DocumentSnapshot::joint` gives a set as a joint of the kind
  `constraint`, so drags name it. Test: `tools/ui-constraint-test.sh`.
- **Animate Joint** (`assemble.animate_joint`, `MainWindowJoints.cpp`): the
  joint selected in the timeline, else the newest with free motions, its
  first motion through its limits (from where it is to one end, the other
  and back) or once round without limits (a slide ±25 mm): 36 frames, each
  the `preview` of `drive_joint` to the frame's value from the frame
  before (mitcad#454), shown through the preview's `placements`; the
  preview is cleared at the end and nothing changes. Starting a command
  stops it. A contact of a contact set ends it there: the status bar says
  where, logged `Animation of Joint1 stopped by contact at tx 10.01 mm:
  Body2 (Pin:1) and Body3 (Wall:1) in Contact1`.
- **Contact Set** (`assemble.contact_set`, `JointCommands.cpp`, mitcad#454;
  the model's side in commands.md, "Motion studies and contact sets"): a
  model command (`modelCommand`): Components (two or more; a body picks
  the occurrence that places it, as paths from the root) and Suppressed;
  OK runs `add_contact_set`, or `edit_contact_set` of the set the browser
  opened (its entry goes through `startFeatureCommand`'s analysis argument
  to `load`, which keeps its name in the hidden input `set`). Logs `Added
  contact set Contact1: Pin:1, Wall:1` and `Edited contact set Contact1`.
- **Motion Link** (`assemble.motion_link`, `JointCommands.cpp`, mitcad#466;
  the model's side in commands.md, "Motion links"): a `motion_link`
  feature. Type (Gears, Rack and Pinion, Screw, Ratio, Cam), Driver and
  Follower (joints with free motions, `SelectKind::Feature`, from the
  browser or the timeline) with Driver Motion and Follower Motion (the
  joint's motions), the type's sizes (Driver Gear and Follower Gear with
  Internal Gear, Pinion Radius, Lead, Ratio; each size's "From" input
  takes a round face, circular edge or circle whose radius it becomes
  instead of the value), a cam's Cam Profile (a flat face or a sketch
  curve), Follower (Knife Edge, Roller with Roller Radius, Flat Face) and
  Follower Tip, Reverse, and Keep Where They Are (on, but for a cam: the
  build asks the `motion_link_offset` query for the offset that keeps the
  joints where they are) else Offset (an angle or a length, as the
  follower's motion). An edit loads the link with its offset. Logs `Added
  motion link MotionLink1: rack_pinion, Joint1 rz to Joint2 tx,
  satisfied`. Test: `tools/ui-motion-link-test.sh`.
- **Motion Study** (`assemble.motion_study`, `MainWindowMotion.cpp`,
  `motion/MotionStudyDialog`, mitcad#454): a panel beside the window, not a
  command (the window stays usable; a command or a sketch pauses it): the
  study (the first, or a new `Study1` when there is none; the browser's
  Play opens another), Steps, the step slider, Play/Pause (Alt+P), Loop,
  Speed (0.25x to 4x of one step per 40 ms frame), the keys per joint
  motion with their points and the value at the step, Add Key (Alt+K: the
  joint motion chosen at the current step, with the typed Value (Alt+V)
  or where the joint is), Remove Key (the selected row's point at the
  step) and Keep Position (Alt+T: `play_study` to the shown step, one undo
  step, then it closes). Each frame and each slider move is the `preview`
  of `play_study` from the step shown before, shown through its
  `placements` on the bodies as shown when the panel opened; a contact
  pauses it at the step where the bodies touch, and the panel says where.
  Closing it (Close, Esc) clears the preview. Logs: `Motion study Open
  opened: 20 steps, 2 keys`, `Playing Open from step 0`, `Played Open to
  step 20: Joint1 tx 15 mm, Joint2 rz 90 deg`, `Paused Open at step 7
  (paused): …`, `Playback of Push stopped at step 5.005: stopped at
  contact: …`, `Key added to Open: Joint1 tx at step 0: 5 mm`, `Kept Open
  at step 20: …`, `Motion study Open closed`. Tests:
  `tools/ui-motion-study-test.sh`, `tools/ui-contact-test.sh`.
- **Contacts in Drive Joint and drags** (mitcad#454): Drive Joint's
  `drive_joint` answer's warning shows in its panel (`Preview Drive
  Joint: ok, warning: stopped at contact: …`); a drag stops where the
  `joint_drag` query's `contact` says (`Drag of Pin:1 stopped at contact:
  …` once per contact, the status bar too) and its release logs `Dragged
  Pin:1 to where it touches: …`.
- **Ghost of side A** (mitcad#147): once Joint's origin A or As-Built
  Joint's component A is picked, and while B is not, the occurrence placed
  directly in the joint's component that A lies in is drawn as a ghost
  (`withGhosts`), so that B can be picked behind it; A's highlight stays
  shown but takes no clicks (A is deselected by activating its input, which
  shows A normally again, or with the input's clear button). Once B is
  picked the preview shows A where the joint puts it, normally. Logged as
  `View ghosts: O2 (1 body)` and `View ghosts: none`.
- **Previews of placements:** a feature command's preview shows the
  bodies of the occurrences it places elsewhere where the preview's
  `placements` put them (joints, Move/Copy of components; `Preview <name>
  moves O2`).
- **Dragging components** (`OcctViewer::setOccurrenceDrag`,
  `MainWindowJoints.cpp`): in idle mode, a left drag without keys that
  starts on a body moves the innermost occurrence of its path whose unit
  in its parent component has joints, is not grounded and can move (the
  `joints` query's unit: `dof` above 0, or `mobile`, as a link of a
  four-bar linkage); a click on such a body still picks. The pointer's
  point is on the plane through the grabbed point facing the viewer; per
  move the `joint_drag` query gives the occurrences' placements, which
  move the shown bodies; the release runs `drag_occurrence` (one undo
  step `Drag Pin:1`, after the mouse event: `whenIdle`). A dialog that
  takes the mouse cancels it.
  One function decides what a drag on an item does (`dragAnswer`,
  mitcad#150), so the hint and the refusal agree:
  - **Hint:** the pointer over a body that would drag shows the move
    cursor (`OcctViewer::setDragCursor`) and the status bar hint `Drag to
    move Pin:1 (Joint1: rz)` (its unit's joints and their free motions;
    log `Drag hint: …`, `Drag hint: none` when it goes).
  - **Refusal:** in a design with components, a left drag without keys
    that starts on a body that does not drag is neither a drag nor a
    window selection: the status bar says why (log `Drag refused: …`).
    The reasons, the innermost occurrence's first: `Base:1 is grounded`;
    `Clip:1 is in a rigid group with Base:1, which is grounded`; held
    fixed by its joints (`dof` 0 and not `mobile`): `Fixed:1 cannot move:
    Joint2 is rigid` (several: `Joint2 and Joint3 are rigid`, other kinds
    `Joint2 (revolute) and Joint3 (slider) hold it`); no joints of its own
    in its parent component (components do not drag freely): `Plate:1 has
