  `cutPartFace`), **Rotation (°)** (`cutPartRotation`), Rotate 90° Left
  and Right, **Add Copy** (another part of the same body and face), and
  whether it leaves the sheet or overlaps others. A part's menu: Rotate
  90° Left, Rotate 90° Right (`turn`), Add Copy, Delete Component; the sheet's:
  Add Components…, Material…. A part whose body is gone keeps a red box at its
  place (the view's `broken`, as a drawing's). The model's warnings
  (overlaps, parts off the sheet, missing bodies) go to the status bar
  and the log when they change (`Cut sheet warnings: …`, `none`). Tested
  by `tools/ui-drawings-test.sh` (Kind Cut Sheet, two bodies added, DXF
  written).

## Print bed face

A body's print bed face (mitcad#731; the model's `set_print_bed_face`, the
`bodies` query's `print_bed_face` and `export`'s `on_bed`, see
`core/model-api/src/commands.md`, "Print bed faces"):

- **The view's context menu** (`MainWindowContextMenu.cpp`), with one face
  of a body that is not a surface body selected (a right click selects
  it), in a window that can change the design: **Set as Print Bed Face**
  on a planar face (`geometry` `plane`), **Clear Print Bed Face** on the
  body's print bed face instead (the face one of those the stored name
  finds at the marker, `print_bed_face.faces`, by name or by the faces of
  the shape, `Shape::find_faces`). A stored face that is gone or not
  planar (`print_bed_face.error`) is cleared with **Clear Print Bed Face**
  on any face of the body, beside Set on a planar one. A surface body
  that keeps a face (it became a surface body, or a file stored one;
  `print_bed_face.error` `a surface body is not printed`) offers Clear
  Print Bed Face only, on any of its faces, and shows no bed face
  (mitcad#737). Each runs
  `set_print_bed_face` (one
  undo step, `Set Print Bed Face of Body1` / `Clear Print Bed Face of
  Body1`) and logs `Print bed face of Body1: F2:end(…)` / `Print bed face
  of Body1: none`. No new command definitions: the entries are the menu's
  own, as Appearance… and Material… are.
- **Seeing it:** while the context menu of another face of a body with a
  print bed face is open, that face is highlighted in green (not
  pickable), in the occurrence of the face clicked
  (`MainWindow::m_printBedShown`, drawn by `updateIdleView`, cleared when
  the menu closes), logged `Print bed face shown: F2.b0/F2:end(…)`. The
  body's browser row's tooltip adds a line `Print bed face: end face of
  Extrude1` (the role and the feature of the face's name: end, start,
  side, top and bottom; `a face of Base1` for other roles), or `Print bed
  face: gone` / `not planar` / `not used, a surface body is not printed`
  for the model's three reasons, else the model's reason as it is (a
  renamed face whose plane is not found, mitcad#737)
  (`DocumentSnapshot::Body::printBedFace`, `printBedFaces`,
  `printBedError`; `printBedText` in `browser/BrowserPanel.cpp`).
- **Print Analysis** (`inspect.print_analysis`): a new analysis's
  **Bed face** starts with the print bed face of its bodies by the
  export's rule: only when exactly one of them has a usable one
  (`storedBedFace` in `commands/InspectCommands.cpp`, in the occurrence
  the body was taken in), logged `Print Analysis bed
  face: F2.b0/F2:end(…)`; another face picked or the face taken out
  overrides it. Editing a kept analysis keeps its own `bed_face`.
- **Send to Slicer** (`make.print3d`, `files/MainWindowPrint.cpp`) exports with
  `"on_bed": true`, 3MF and every STL file alike: one bed face among the
  bodies turns them onto it and centres them on the plate, several keep
  them as assembled. Logged per 3MF file `3D Print bed: Body1 on F2:end(…),
  plate 128.000,128.000, transform 1.000 0.000 0.000 118.000 | 0.000
  -1.000 0.000 138.000 | 0.000 0.000 -1.000 20.000` (the rows of what moved
  the bodies after the design's placements, three decimals), `3D Print
  bed: kept as assembled: F2.b0, F3.b0` or `3D Print bed: as in the
  design`, each bed face that cannot be used added (`; Body1: the print
  bed face is gone`); per STL file `3D Print bed Body1.stl: …`. A face
  that cannot be used is a warning of the status line, as the export
  says it (`Body1: the print bed face is gone; printed as in the
  design`), with the print settings' warnings.
- Tests: `tools/ui-print-bed-test.sh` and
  `tools/ui-windows-print-bed-test.ps1` (ctest `app.ui-windows-print-bed`):
  Set as Print Bed Face from the context menu on a box's top (the file
  keeps it), a side's menu showing it and offering Set, Clear on it and
  Undo; Send to Slicer to a 3MF file turned over onto the top and centred on the
  plate (the logged transform); Print Analysis starting from it; a design
  whose stored face is gone reported in the log and the status line, then
  cleared from a side's menu, after which Send to Slicer warns no more; a box
  made a surface body by Unstitch that keeps its face, whose menus offer
  Clear only and clear it (mitcad#737).

## Image references

Images placed in the design to model from (mitcad#782; the model's
`insert_image_reference`, `edit_image_reference`,
`calibrate_image_reference`, `set_image_reference_visible`,
`rename_image_reference`, `delete_image_reference` and the
`image_references`, `image_reference_image`, `image_reference_outline`
and `image_info` queries, see `core/model-api/src/commands.md`, "Image
references"). The code: `MainWindowImageReferences.cpp` (the commands,
the refresh, calibration), `view/ImageReferences.*` (the query's entries
as drawn, points on an image and its plane, the log line; plain Qt Core),
`view/ImageReferenceView.cpp` (`OcctViewer::setImageReferences`) and
`view/ImageCalibration.*` (the two clicks).

- **Image Reference** (`insert.image_reference`, SOLID INSERT, icon
  `image-reference`): a panel of a model command (`modelCommand`). Inputs:
  Image (the file's path, typed) with **Choose Image…** under it (a note
  row whose button opens the Import group's file dialog, its filter PNG,
  JPEG, BMP, WebP and, in builds with the HEIF decoder, `.heic` and
  `.heif`; the path goes into Image when the panel shows its inputs
  again, `modelChanged`), Plane
  (a construction plane or planar face, `kPlaneKinds` and `isPlanar`, 0 to 1 so
  that an edit may keep a plane the panel cannot show), X and Y (the
  centre in the plane's frame; a plane picked, or selected before the
  command, sets them to its middle, `centreOnPlane` with
  `image_reference_outline`'s `center`), Angle, Flip, Width (empty: from
  the file, or unchanged when editing; `withAuto`), Opacity % (0 to 100,
  default 50) and Through Bodies. OK runs `insert_image_reference` with
  the file's absolute `path`, `center`, `angle` in degrees, `flip`,
  `width` when typed, `opacity` / 100 and `through` (no label of the
  panel's: the undo step is the model's `Insert Image1`), and logs
  `Inserted image reference from plan.png`. A HEIF file (mitcad#850) is
  decoded first (`heifProblem`, files of at most 32 MB), since MitCad's
  own decoder draws it: one it cannot decode, or any HEIF file in a build
  without the decoder, is refused with its reason (`The image cannot be
  read: the HEIF image cannot be decoded: …`). While the panel is open the
  image's outline is drawn (`viewLines`, from `image_reference_outline`; a
  new image's pixels and pixel size from `image_info`).
- **Editing** (a double-click on the image's browser row, or Edit Image
  Reference in its menu; `MainWindow::editImageReference`): the same
  panel, titled `Image Reference (edit)` and logged `Editing image reference
  Image1 with Image Reference` (`CommandDef::editedKind`), filled from the `image_references`
  entry (`load`, kept as the state's object `image`; the width from the
  entry's `size`; Plane left empty when the entry has an `error`, so that
  another plane is picked). OK runs `edit_image_reference` with every
  value (the plane only while one is picked) and logs `Edited image
  reference Image1`.
- **Calibrate Image Reference** (`insert.calibrate_image_reference`, an
  action, icon `image-calibrate`; also in an image row's menu, for that
  image, refused with `Show Image1 first.` while it is hidden): from the
  ribbon on the shown images, the first click taking the one it lands on
  (the nearest along the ray, within 2 % of its edges, `imageFractions`;
  one image alone takes any point of its plane). It logs `Calibrate Image1
  started` (with several, `Calibrate started on Image1, Plan`) and the
  places a tenth of each image in from its edges through its middle,
  `Calibrate Image1 left at x,y` (right, top, bottom; window coordinates,
  again when the camera comes to rest). The two left clicks in the view
  (the view's own left button off, `OcctViewer::setSketchInput`) are
  points where the clicks' rays meet the image's plane, logged `Calibrate
  Image1 first point (x, y, z)` and `Calibrate Image1 second point (x, y,
  z), d mm from the first`; between them a cross marks the first point and
  a line runs to the pointer (a `ManipulatorOverlay`'s lines). A dialog
  `Calibrate Image1` then asks for the distance, prefilled with the
  measured one in the design's unit (a bare number in that unit, else an
  expression the model evaluates), and `calibrate_image_reference` with
  the two `points` logs `Calibrated Image1: d mm is D mm, s mm per pixel`.
  Esc, a command, or one of its images gone or hidden ends it (`Calibrate
  Image1 cancelled`). The middle and right buttons still navigate.
- **The view** (`MainWindow::followImageReferences`, after each refresh):
  the shown entries with their corners, each picture fetched once by its
  digest (`image_reference_image`, decoded by `decodeImageFile`,
  `view/ImageFile.*`: HEIF through libheif and its HEVC decoder libde265
  in builds with `MITCAD_HEIF`, upright as the file's `irot`, `imir`
  and `clap` say, 8 bits per channel, with its alpha plane; the rest with
  `QImage::fromData`, a WebP file needing Qt's image format plugin),
  logged `Image reference Image1 decoded: 200 x 100 pixels` or `Image
  reference Image1 cannot be drawn: <why>`. Each is a textured quad (at
  most 4096 pixels on a side) with the opacity in its alpha, unlit, both
  sides, in front of a face it lies on (polygon offset); Through Bodies in
  the view's image layer, without depth, just before the sketch halos'
  layer: over the bodies and their edges, under the sketches, previews and
  highlights (logged once `Image references through the bodies: in the
  image layer, before the sketch halos`). Never picked. Logged when it changes: `Image
  references drawn: Image1 50.0 x 25.0 mm 40% behind, Plan 100.0 x 50.0
  mm 70% through` (`imageReferencesLog`), or `… none`.
- **The browser**: the root's **Images** folder (`ImageReferences`, its
  menu Insert Image Reference) and a row per image (`ImageReference`, uid
  its name, icon `image-reference`): its light bulb runs
  `set_image_reference_visible`, F2 `rename_image_reference`, Delete
  `delete_image_reference`; the tooltip gives the file's name and the
  size, or why its plane is not there (the row red).
- Tests: `tests/image_references.cpp` (`app.unit`),
  `tools/ui-image-references-test.sh` and
  `tools/ui-windows-image-references-test.ps1` (ctest
  `app.ui-windows-image-references`): inserted on a plate's top from a
  BMP file, calibrated by two clicks and 80 typed, edited (opacity,
  Through Bodies), hidden, saved, opened again and shown; in the Linux
  test also a HEIF file turned a quarter by its `irot`, decoded upright
  and drawn, and read back from the design after the file is gone.
  `tests/heif_image.cpp` (`app.unit`): HEIF files told from the other
  formats, and files the test makes around `tools/heif-test-fixture.py`'s
  HEVC data (64 x 32 pixels, four coloured quarters, 8 and 10 bits per
  channel) decoded with their quarters where a turn of 0, 90 or 270
  degrees puts them; a file cut short refused with the decoder's reason.

## Bindings: Varies with, Suppress When, Show When

Values that follow expressions of parameters (mitcad#809, mitcad#861; the
model's mitcad#800 and its `expression` fields of `set_body_appearance`,
`set_face_appearance`, `set_body_material`, `suppress_feature`,
`set_body_visible` and `set_occurrence_visible`, see
`core/model-api/src/commands.md`, "Bindings: values from expressions").
The code: `browser/Bindings.*` (the condition dialog, the fx badge),
`browser/OptionMapping.cpp` (the switch() form `OptionMapping`),
`commands/MaterialBinding.*` and `commands/MaterialCommands.cpp` (the fx
of the Material and Appearance tools, mitcad#1059),
`BrowserController::{suppressWhen, showBodyWhen, showOccurrenceWhen}` and
the menus.

- **The menus.** A body's browser row: **Show When…** after Hide/Show; an
  occurrence's row: **Show When…** after Hide/Show; a feature's menu (the
  timeline's, and its rows in the browser): **Suppress When…** after
  Suppress Features. The view's menu: **Show When…** for one body. There
  is one place for a body's appearance and one for its material
  (mitcad#861, mitcad#1059): **Appearance…** and **Material › More…**
  start the Appearance and Material tools, whose fx binds them to an
  option (the submenu Follow Option of mitcad#809 and the windows'
  assignment panel of mitcad#861 are gone). While a
  target follows an expression (a body's appearance or material, a picked
  face's own appearance), its entry carries an fx mark: `boundIcon` on its
  icon and `fx` after its text (`Appearance…  fx`, the text's shortcut
  column; the submenu `Material  fx`);
  logged `Context menu fx: Appearance… | Material` beside the menu's own
  line, which names the entries without the mark (`ui_menu_choose
  "Appearance..."` takes them either way).
- **Suppress When… and Show When…** (`ConditionDialog`, titled `Suppress
  Extrude2 When`, `Show Body1 When`, `Show Board:1 When`): an expression
  field (`bindingCondition`, the parameters' suggestions) with **Formula
  Editor…**, **Remove Condition** (when there is one), OK and Cancel. OK
  runs the command with `expression` (one undo step: `Suppress Extrude2
  When`; an empty field removes the condition and keeps the value), and
  logs `Suppress Extrude2 when Holes = 'No'`, `Show Body1 when …`, `…
  removed`, or `… refused: <reason>`. Logged: `Condition dialog <title>:
  <condition or none>`, `Condition field|formula|remove|OK at x,y`.
- **Varies with**: the fx of the Material and Appearance tools
  ([Material and Appearance tools](#material-and-appearance-tools)),
  which replaced the windows' assignment panel of mitcad#861 and reads
  the bindings it wrote.
- **The marks.** A bound body's, occurrence's or feature's browser row has
  the fx badge after its name with the count of its bound properties (`fx
  3`, mitcad#862: the card below), logged `Browser fx Root/Bodies/Body1:
  Appearance = switch(…)` at each rebuild (the expressions, and a body's
  warnings); a feature suppressed by a
  condition has the badge in the timeline and `Suppressed when …` in its
  tooltip. `DocumentSnapshot` reads `suppressed_when`, `visible_when`,
  `appearance_expr`, `material_expr`, `face_appearance_exprs` and a body's
  `warnings`.
- **By hand.** The Material and Appearance tools without fx, Material ›,
  the light bulbs, Hide and Suppress Features send the value, which removes the expression in the same undo
  step (the model's rule).
- **Light bulbs and Show When** (mitcad#863): a conditioned body's or
  occurrence's light bulb is an fx bulb (the plain bulb with a small fx
  corner badge; a folder's bulb stays plain) whose tooltip gives the condition,
  what it gives now and that a click removes it; the click says so in the
  status bar (`Show When of Body2 removed – Undo brings it back`). The
  Bodies folder's light bulb and Show All / Hide All, the view's Hide of
  several items and Find in Design's Show and Hide leave conditioned items
  to their conditions. See the light bulbs in "Browser, timeline and
  parameters" above; test `tools/ui-show-when-test.sh`.
- Tests: `tools/ui-bindings-test.sh`: no menu has Follow Option; Body1's
  appearance varies with the text parameter Color in the Appearances
  window (its allowed values, nothing written when chosen, the rows filled
  by double-clicks, the next row active), Color = 'Red' in Change
  Parameters turns it red and the menu marks Appearance… with fx; Body2's
  material varies with Color in the Materials window; None keeps the
  shown appearance and undo brings the binding back; three bodies of
  different assignments show the Mixed notice and the first fill writes the
  table to all three in one undo step; Box2 suppressed by `Holes = 'No'`
  and back with Holes = 'Yes'.

**Bindings at a glance** (mitcad#862): what an item follows, in words.
The code: `browser/BindingList.*` (the design's bindings from the
`bodies`, `timeline` and `components` queries, the parameters' values and
the appearances' and materials' names and colours, and the words:
`readBinding`), `browser/BindingsCard.*` (the card),
`browser/ConfigurationBindingsPage.*` (the Configurations window's
Bindings tab) and `BrowserController::{browserBindings, timelineBindings,
editBinding, selectBinding, showAllBindings}`. No query field was added.
The UI says "follows" and "when" for bindings, never "rule" (rules are
the configuration's).

- **The fx badge.** A bound browser row draws a solid pill `fx N` after
  its name (and after a component's radio button; dark blue semibold text
  on a light blue fill, light text on a dark blue fill in a dark theme, so
  that it stays legible on a selected row's band), N its bound properties: a
  body's appearance, material, Show When and each face with an appearance
  of its own; 1 for a feature's Suppress When and an occurrence's Show
  When (`BrowserDelegate::Parts::fx`, the role `kBindingsRole`; the row's
  box with the Rows background reaches its end). The pointer resting on it
  (450 ms, `BrowserPanel::hoverBindings`) shows the card until the pointer
  leaves the badge and the card; a click pins it (a popup: Esc or a click
  outside closes it). The timeline's badge on the icon of a feature with
  Suppress When does the same (`TimelineStrip::badgeRect`; the strip's
  hover pause). A native presentation's rows keep the fx mark on the icon
  (`presentationRows`, `boundIcon`).
- **The card** (`BindingsCard`): `Body2 follows` with the options it uses
  and their values now (`now: Color = Black, Holes = No`), then a line per
  property: a `switch()` over one option (`OptionMapping`), or an `if()`
  whose conditions compare one option with values (`if(Color = 'Black';
  'paint_white'; 'paint_yellow')`, nested ifs too), as a case per value
  (`Black → Paint - White`) with the result's swatch (a filled disc of its
  `display_color` with a darker border, `bindingSwatch`), the current case
  marked ●, a result that names no appearance or material in the warning
  colour. The default case is `otherwise → …` for an option without a list
  of values; for one with a list (its `values` limit) it is named by the
  values it covers (`Red → Paint - Yellow`), or left out when the cases
  list them all. A face is `Face 1 (side)` (its number among the body's
  bound faces and the kind its topological name gives; the name itself in
  the tooltip). A condition reads `when Holes = Yes · hidden now`
  (literals without quotes, `==` as `=`, `<>` and `!=` as `≠`); another
  expression its text so, ids of appearances and materials as their names,
  and what it gives now (`· Paint - White now`), elided with the
  expression as written in the tooltip. A body's appearance and material
  that follow nothing are plain grey lines (`Steel, set by hand`, `Steel,
  the default`, `Paint - Red, from its material`); the model's warnings
  stand under their line. The card is at most 460 px wide, its texts
  elided (whole in their tooltips). **Edit…** per line, a link (the link
  colour, underlined, darker under the pointer): the Appearance window for
  the body or the face (`openAppearances`), the Materials window for the
  body (`openMaterial`), Show When… or Suppress When… (the occurrence's by
  its path). **All bindings of the design**, the same kind of link, opens
  Configurations on the Bindings tab. The card reads the model again after
  every change while it shows.

## Chat (mitcad#947)

The chat panel ([docs/ai-chat.md](../docs/ai-chat.md), `app/agent/`): the
user's own agent (Claude Code or Codex) changes the open design through
the window's live MCP server.

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `view.chat` Chat | shows or hides the panel (View menu, checkable; its button `titleChat` beside the agent indicator in the title row, the Docked toolbar; in the AppKit window the toolbar's `native.chatButton` beside the agent indicator; Ctrl+Shift+L, ⌘⇧L on macOS; the dock's close button too). Any mode, also while a panel is open |

- Place: Floating, the card `chatCard` on the right edge
  (`FloatingLayout::Anchor::Right`: from below the top rows to above the
  timeline, 340 wide; the upper right cards and the orientation cube move
  left of it); Docked, the dock `chatDock` on the right. The panel itself
  is `chatPanel` in both. The AppKit window (mitcad#1075) has the card
  `native.chatCard` at the same place, 340 points wide in a wide window
  (a third of the canvas in a narrow one, at least 280), with the
  inspector, its width handle and the orientation cube's arrows left of
  it: the same `chatPanel`, hidden in Qt, through the presenter bridge, its
  controls under the same names; the message field takes the keyboard
  when the card shows, and the conversation keeps its end in sight.
- The panel (`agent/ChatPanel`): a header (the agent `chatAgent`, or the
  choice `chatAgentChoice` once more than one agent is found: the agents
  found on this computer and the chosen one; another one starts a new
  conversation in it and is saved as `chat/agent`, the last used one;
  mitcad#1289: each Claude Code found is an entry of its own
  (`mcp::assistantExecutables`: PATH, `.local/bin`, npm's folder,
  `.cargo/bin`, the stored PATH's folders, and the Claude Code Claude
  Desktop keeps, `claudeDesktopClaudeCode`: `claude-code/<version>/claude`
  in its settings folders, or `claude-code/<version>/<build id>/claude.exe`
  in the Windows application's `Claude-Data/claude_<id>` folders, the
  highest version's, listed only when there),
  the first one `claude` as before, another `claude-<8 hex digits of its
  path's SHA-256>`, named with its place, "Claude Code (~/.local/bin)" or
  "Claude Code (Claude Desktop's)" (mitcad#1297: by its path in either
  layout, `mcp::claudeDesktopKeepsClaudeCode`); every entry's sign-in state beside its
  name in the list (the item's `kAgentStateRole`, drawn by its delegate;
  the item's text stays the name; the AppKit pop-up shows it under the
  name, the combo's `nativeItemDetailRole`, mitcad#1358): checking, not found, needs an update,
  not signed in, needs an API key, signing in, signed in, signed in as
  *account* (Claude Code's `claude auth status` `email`), ready (an API
  endpoint, a local model, the custom command), then "· same sign-in as
  *entry*" (mitcad#1297: the entries whose programs use one configuration
  folder, `ChatAgent::signInFolder`: Claude Code's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` of
  MitCad's environment, else `~/.claude`, `mcp::claudeConfigurationFolder`;
  MitCad starts every Claude Code with its own environment, so all of them
  share one sign-in; each names the first other one, `sameSignIn` in
  `agent/AccountCheck.hpp`; logged once as `Chat: Claude Code (Claude
  Desktop's) shares the sign-in of Claude Code`), then "· *reason*" of a
  known account failure; every agent found is checked when the panel opens
  (`refreshSetup(true)`), and the list's names and states are logged as
  `Chat agents: Claude Code · signed in as someone@example.com · same
  sign-in as Claude Code (~/.local/bin) | Claude Code (~/.local/bin) · not
  signed in · same sign-in as Claude Code | Ollama · ready` when they
  change; an agent turned off under the assistant menu's Outgoing
  connections (mitcad#1299, `chat/off`) is not in the list and is neither
  checked nor started, and the chosen one turned off gives way to another
  one offered (with none, the state `unavailable` says to check one
  there); New
  conversation `chatNew`, the menu `chatMore`: New Conversation, Clear
  History of This Design, Chat Preferences… (`tools.preferences.agents`)),
  the line Model: `chatModelChoice` (editable: Default model, the agent's
  models (Claude Code's Opus, Sonnet, Haiku; Codex's `model/list`, kept as
  `chat/models/codex`), or a typed name; saved per agent as
  `chat/model/<agent>`, given as `ChatAgent::Start::model`; an idle agent
  restarts with it on the next message, resuming its session; disabled
  while the agent works) and the reported model `chatModel` (dimmed),
  the conversation `chatConversation` (`chatUser`, `chatAnswer` as
  Markdown, `chatTool` rows with `chatToolHead`/`chatToolDetails` and the

  `chatApproval` with `chatAllowOnce`, `chatAlwaysAllow`, `chatDeny` and

- Account failures (mitcad#1126): `core/mcp/src/chat/account.rs` classifies
  failed protocol messages from Claude Code and Codex (structured error
  subtypes/HTTP status and error text); ordinary failed tool results and
  successful assistant text are excluded. `ChatController` keeps an error
  per agent across setup checks and New Conversation. The error-coloured
  state line says the account cannot be used (`chatState=account-error`),
  `chatSetup` **How to fix** opens `chatAccountHelp`/`chatAccountHelpText`,
  and `chatCheckAccount` **Check again** checks sign-in then a fresh,
  context-free, 30-second probe turn (`chatState=checking-account`). The
  probe cannot call model tools, adds no conversation/history entries and
  never replaces the design's saved session. Only a successful probe clears
  the error. Check again always ends (mitcad#1155): a setup check that
  emits no readiness change (the agent's program gone, as at the last
  look) is settled right after `check()` (`agent/AccountCheck.hpp`), and
  the setup check is bounded to 45 s (an unfinished sign-in); a missing or
  outdated agent shows its setup state (`chatState=missing`/`outdated`)
  with `chatCheckAccount` hidden until it is found. A check that fails
  otherwise (network, timeout, agent gone) keeps the account's reason in
  the state line and adds a warning notice `The account check failed:
  ...` (not kept in the history); messages queued at an account failure
  are dropped with the warning `n waiting message(s) were not sent.`
  The duplicate assistant/result error is shown once. An account error
  marks every entry that shares the sign-in (mitcad#1297, logged `Chat: the
  account error is Claude Code (Claude Desktop's)'s too (the same
  sign-in)`), so none of them is offered by `chatOtherAgent`, and a passed

  shares one sign-in with Claude Code (Claude Desktop's): in a terminal,
  claude auth logout and then claude auth login fix it for all of them."
  (`chatAccountHelpText`'s property `sharedSignIn`: the other entries).
  Logged:

## Dogbone

**Dogbone** (`solid.dogbone`, `commands/DogboneCommands.cpp`, mitcad#1011;
the model's `dogbone`, `core/model-api/src/commands.md` "Dogbone") is the
last command of the SOLID tab's MODIFY group (registered after
Appearance), not pinned, found by the search also as `cnc`, `router`,
`relief`, `t-bone` and `corner`. Its icon `dogbone` is the timeline's
too (`featureIcon`).

- Inputs: *Corners* (`picks`: edges, faces or a body, any number, of one
  body; no mesh bodies; an edge only when straight), *Tool Diameter*
  (`diameter`, `6.35 mm`), *Extra* (`extra`, `0.1 mm`), *Type*
  (`dogbone_type`: Diagonal or Along a Side) and *Tool Axis* (`axis`: Z,
  Y or X), shown while a face or the body is picked.
- `build`: the body of the picks; a picked body sends neither `edges` nor
  `faces` (every corner of the body), otherwise the picked edges and
  faces; `diameter` and `extra` always, `dogbone_type` only for Along a
  Side, `axis` only for faces or a body about Y or X (`[0, 1, 0]`,
  `[1, 0, 0]`).
- `load`: edges and faces back as picks, the body when there are none;
  the values (the inputs' defaults where the definition has none, which
  are the model's); an `axis` that is no positive axis of the component
  is not editable (`canEdit`).
- Logged: `Dogbone Corners: 1 body [body F1.b0]` as any selection,
  `Preview Dogbone: ok`, and on OK `Added dogbone (Diagonal), tool
  diameter 6.35` (`Along a Side`).
- Tests: `tools/ui-dogbone-test.sh` (Linux, Xvfb) and
  `app.ui-windows-dogbone` (`tools/ui-windows-dogbone-test.ps1`): the
  command on a pocket's body picked in the browser, OK, the body's volume
  with four diagonal reliefs, `Dogbone1` in the timeline.

## Remembered values

A value input marked `withRemembered()` (`InputDef::remembered`,
mitcad#1028) starts a **new** feature's panel with the value given in it
on that command's last OK, from any design; without one, its
definition's default.

- Kept in the local settings, not in the design: `commands/<command
  id>/<input id>` (`commands/solid.fillet/radius=3 mm`), by
  `framework/RememberedValues` (plain Qt Core). What is kept is the
  field's expression as the model normalised it (a bare `3` typed in a
  millimetre design is kept as `3 mm`), without the name of a parameter
  it names (`r = 3 mm` keeps `3 mm`, so that the next feature does not
  name another parameter `r`).
- Written when the panel of a new feature ends with OK
  (`CommandSession::finish(true)`): the inputs shown then, of a list the
  first row's. Editing a feature (also an analysis) and Cancel write
  nothing; an empty field leaves the kept value as it was.
- Read when a new feature's panel sets its defaults
  (`CommandSession::setDefaults`): the kept text is evaluated in the
  design (the `evaluate` query with the input's kind); when it does not
  evaluate (a parameter the design lacks), the field starts with the
  default, without an error. Rows added with Add Set start with it too.
  Editing a feature shows the feature's own values.
- Logged `Panel Fillet radius: remembered 3 mm` (the command's name, the
  input's own id) when a field starts with a kept value, `Panel Fillet
  radius: remembered width / 4 does not evaluate here, 2 mm instead` when
  the default stands in for it.
- **Fillet**: Radius (the constant radius, the first size of the other
  radius types; default 2 mm). **Chamfer**: Distance (default 1 mm),
  Distance 2 (1 mm) and Angle (45 deg), each kept by an OK whose set type
  shows it: an Equal Distance chamfer leaves Distance 2 and Angle as they
  were.
- `MITCAD_REMEMBER_PANEL_VALUES=0` turns it off: nothing is read or
  written. The UI test libraries (`tools/ui-test-lib.sh`,
  `tools/ui-macos-lib.sh`, `tools/ui-windows-lib.ps1`,
  `tools/ui-windows-test.ps1`) set it, so that a value one step gives
  never changes where a later step's panel starts; a test of the
  remembered values sets it to 1 for its own steps.
- Tests: `app.unit` (`app/tests/remembered_values.cpp`: kept on a new
  feature's OK, not on an edit or Cancel, read back, an expression that
  does not evaluate falls back to the default, the switch);
  `tools/ui-fillet-handle-test.sh` (a fillet with 3 mm, OK; Fillet again
  starts with 3 mm; a cancelled 5 mm and an edit to 4 mm change nothing,
  also after a new start of the app), `tools/ui-chamfer-handle-test.sh`
  (Two Distances with 3 mm and 2 mm, OK; Chamfer again starts with both)
  and `app.ui-windows-remembered-values`
  (`tools/ui-windows-remembered-values-test.ps1`: Fillet and Chamfer with
  3 mm, also after a new start).

### Panel settings kept by size (mitcad#1298)

A command with `CommandDef::settingsKey` keeps its **whole panel** with
the size the feature was made for, and a new panel of the same size
starts from it. Thread is the only one: its size is the first cylindrical
face's diameter and side (inside or outside), the face that suggests the
size (`suggestSize`).

- **What is kept** (`framework/RememberedValues`: `PanelSizeKey`,
  `PanelSettings`, `keepPanelSettings`, `keptPanelSettings`): every value
  (as the remembered values keep it: the expression without a parameter's
  name), choice and check of the inputs outside lists, shown or hidden:
  Thread's Thread Type, Size, Designation, Class, Major Diameter, Pitch,
  Tapered, Direction, Modeled, Starts, the clearances, Full Length,
  Length, Offset, Thread Location and the end chamfer's inputs. One set
  per command, the last new feature's OK, whatever its size, in the local
  settings beside the remembered values: `commands/<command
  id>/last_settings/` with `key/diameter` (mm), `key/side` (`internal`,
  `external`) and `values/<id>`, `choices/<id>`, `checks/<id>`; from any
  design. An edit and Cancel keep nothing; an OK without a known size
  neither. Logged `Panel Thread: settings kept with Ø8.5 internal`.
- **When it is used**: once a pick or the faces selected before the
  command (`preselected`, `preselect`) make the size known
  (`CommandSession::considerKeptSettings`, called from `selectionChanged`
  and `start`), and each time it changes to another size; another pick of
  the same size changes nothing. A kept size of the same side whose
  diameter is within 0.001 mm (`PanelSizeKey::matches`) sets every kept
  input, in the inputs' order (a choice's options follow the ones before
  it; a kept option the choice no longer offers is left out, a value that
  does not evaluate in the design too), without their `onChange`. Logged
  `Panel Thread: settings of the last Ø8.5 internal thread restored` and
  `Panel Thread restored: direction=left, modeled=on, full_length=off,
  length=12 mm` (what it changed). Otherwise `Panel Thread: settings of
  the last Ø8.5 internal thread not used: Ø6.8 internal differs`, and the
  panel goes on as without them: Thread's suggested size and the
  defaults. A size taken back by another pick does not take the restored
  settings back.
- **What the user changed stays**: an input whose value, choice or check
  differs from where the panel started (`changedSettings`, the state
  before the pick's own `onPick`: Thread's suggested size is not the
  user's) keeps the user's; logged `Panel Thread left as changed:
  chamfer`.
- `MITCAD_REMEMBER_PANEL_VALUES=0` turns it off with the remembered
  values: nothing is kept, compared or restored.
- Tests: `app.unit` (`app/tests/remembered_values.cpp`: the size key's
  text and its 0.001 mm match, values, choices and checks kept on a new
  feature's OK and read back, nothing on an edit or Cancel, the next OK
  replacing them, the changed inputs); `tools/ui-thread-settings-test.sh`
  (an M10x1.5 6H Left Hand, Modeled, 12 mm thread in a Ø8.5 hole, OK; on
  the second Ø8.5 hole the panel starts from it, Chamfer Ends checked
  before the pick stays, and OK makes the same thread; on a Ø6.8 hole the
  size is suggested and the rest are the defaults) and its Windows
  counterpart, the Thread part of `app.ui-windows-remembered-values`.

## Help › User Guide (mitcad#1032)

**Help › User Guide** (`help.user_guide`, `MainWindow::registerCommands`;
the tooltip "Opens the user guide of this version in the web browser")
opens [docs/user-guide.md](../docs/user-guide.md) on GitHub in the
browser (`openExternalUrl`, `report/ReportCenter.hpp`), from any mode and
during commands.

- **Where:** the first entry of the Help menu, before the Keyboard and
  Mouse Overview, in the menu bar of both layouts (Floating and Docked;
  on macOS the native menu bar, which the AppKit frontend reads from the
  same Qt menu bar), and in the command search (keywords help, manual,
  documentation, guide, docs, contents).
- **The address:** `MITCAD_GUIDE_URL`, set in `app/CMakeLists.txt`:
  `https://github.com/mitcad/Mitcad/blob/<ref>/docs/user-guide.md`, the
  public repository README.md names. `<ref>` is the release's tag
  `v<version>` (the project's version); a build at `MITCAD_MAIN_VERSION`,
  the version main keeps because a release's version commit is made on
  its own branch only, is a development build and opens `main`. The cache
  variable `MITCAD_GUIDE_REF` names another branch or tag.
- **The table of contents** at the guide's top is written by
  `tools/check-guide-contents.py --write`; check-all's step `guide` fails
  when it differs from the headings ([development](../docs/development.md#the-check-script)).
- Logged, with `MITCAD_TEST_LOG_URLS=1` (the UI test libraries), as
  `Open URL (test, not opened): <address>` instead of opening it.
- Tests: `tools/ui-user-guide-test.sh` and `app.ui-windows-user-guide`
  (`tools/ui-windows-user-guide-test.ps1`), both through the test driver's
  `tools/ui-scripts/user-guide.mitcad-ui`, Docked and Floating: the Help
  menu's entry (`menu 'Help/User Guide'`) and the command each log the
  guide's address once.

## The Make tab

mitcad#1049 (`framework/Ribbon.*`, `MainWindowMake.cpp`,
`print/MakeBodyCard.*`): everything about making a design, by
manufacturing method. The tab `MAKE` (shown **Make**) is always there,
after Solid and Build, in the Floating and the Docked layout; a drawing
hides it with Solid and Build (*Drawings*). The native macOS toolbar
reads its groups from the same ribbon (`MainWindow::refreshNativeActions`
lists `MAKE` with `SOLID`, `BUILD` and `SKETCH`). No sub-mode selector
until CAM exists.

| Group | Commands (ids) |
|---|---|
| Materials | **Edit Materials…** (`solid.materials`, from the Solid tab's Modify group; the window manages the materials, mitcad#1059), **Material** (`make.assign_material`: the Material tool `solid.material` started with the selection, its place on this tab; [Material and Appearance tools](#material-and-appearance-tools)) |
| Annotate | **Dimension** (`make.dimension`), **Note** (`make.note`), **Datum Label** (`make.datum_label`), **Feature Control Frame** (`make.frame`), **Hole Callout** (`make.hole_callout`), **Material** (`make.material_note`), **Process Note** (`make.process_note`); after a separator **Annotations…** (`view.annotations`) |
| 3D Print | **Print Analysis** (`inspect.print_analysis`, from the Inspect group), **Send to Slicer** (`make.print3d`, once 3D Print: 3MF or STL to a slicer), **Printers…** (`make.printers`, once Edit Printers and Processes…), **Processes…** (`make.processes`, mitcad#1135) and **Plates…** (`make.plates`, mitcad#1050, [Plates…](#plates)) |
| Laser | **Export Flat Pattern…** (`sheet.export_dxf`, from the Sheet Metal group), **Export Face as DXF…** (`make.export_face_dxf`) |

- **The 3D Print icons** (mitcad#1096, mitcad#1135): Send to Slicer keeps
  the printer `print-3d`; Printers… has `print-settings`, the same
  printer with a gear beside its nozzle (also the Printers manager's
  icon); Processes… has `print-process`, three printed layers with the
  same gear (the Processes manager's icon); Print Analysis has
  `print-analysis`. The ribbon, the menus and the command search take the
  command's icon, so the print commands differ everywhere (`tools/ui-print-icons-test.sh`, the
  test driver's `expect-command-icon`).
- **One place each.** The moved commands keep their ids, shortcuts and
  keywords; they left the Solid tab (Render Image stays in its Render
  group, `RENDER`, named Make until mitcad#1070 so that Make names only
  this tab). A group lists its commands in registration order; CNC comes
  with CAM's commands (mitcad#1013): a group without commands or extras
  is not shown (`Ribbon::hasEntries`; also the Solid tab's Render group in
  a build without the render worker). In the view's context menu the Make tab's feature
  commands that take the selection are a **Make** submenu.
- **The Annotate group** is what the Measure panel's Keep as Dimension
  and Annotate ▾ did (*Measurement objects*): each a panel of its picks
  (`accept`, OK named **Add**) that adds the annotation outside the
  panel's undo range, one undo step. Material and Process Note are the
  model's notes written from the body (`material`, `process_note`:
  `core/model-api/src/commands.md`, *Material and process notes*); the
  Annotations window, the editor and the view show them as notes, their
  text not editable.
- **Previews** (mitcad#1097). While its picks and fields are complete, each
  Annotate panel shows the annotation its Add would make, drawn dimmed
  in the view (never picked, left out of snapshots and pictures): its
  leader, text, frame, letter or dimension where and as Add will put
  them. The panel's `build` gives the `add_annotation` command, and
  `CommandDef::acceptPreview` sends it with the view's direction and
  `"preview": true` (`core/model-api/src/commands.md`, *Annotations*:
  the model places it as it would add it and stores nothing); Add runs
  the same command, so the two cannot differ. It follows the pick, the
  text, the letter, the tolerance chosen and the view's direction (the
  camera at rest looking another way computes it again; a pan or a zoom
  only moves it with the view). What the panel lacks is its message as
  before; what the model refuses for the picks (a vertex for a datum
  label, a letter in use) is the panel's error, with Add disabled. The
  preview goes when the panel ends; after Add the annotation stands in
  its place.
- **Export Face as DXF…** takes the selected planar face (a hint asks
  for one): the body's outline seen along it (`export_face_dxf`, the
  model's *Export Face as DXF*) through the file dialog of the Export
  folder group; also in a planar face's context menu. Its tooltip says
  the file also serves waterjet and plasma cutters, as Export Flat
  Pattern's does.
- **The selected body's card.** On the Make tab, with one body (or a
  face, edge or vertex of it) selected outside commands, the selection
  card shows the **Make** section under the selection's text
  (`MakeBodyCard`), its rows from the widest choice to the body's own
  (mitcad#1239): the **Printer**, the **Process**, the **Material** (a
  drop-down of the design's materials; another one is set on the body
  with `set_body_material`) and every printer
  or process value set on a level rather than taken from a profile, each
  with the icon of the level that gives it (body, occurrence, component,
  as the Properties window's Source column has it) and its own field: a
  value typed there (Enter, or the field left) is set on the body, one
  undo step. The Properties window stays for full editing. Another tab or
  a command hides it. On the Make tab the card has no Create row
  (mitcad#1178): the Make section takes its place; the row comes back
  with another tab (`updateSelectionCreate` follows `Ribbon::tabChanged`).
  - **Printer and Process** (mitcad#1239) are searchable pickers as Send
    to Slicer's (`PickerComboBox`, `framework/PickerComboBox.*`, shared
    with the panels' choice pickers): the printers and processes of
    `library_items`, the design's and the libraries' (This project, My
    library, Built-in), in `profilePickerRows`' order under the same
    headings (the printers by vendor, the processes by printer, the
    body's printer's processes first, mitcad#1216, Any printer last),
    each by its short name with where it comes from; *Slicer default*
    first while none is chosen; last, below a line, **Printers…** or
    **Processes…**, which opens the Printers or Processes manager on the
    one chosen (on none selected for Slicer default; the choice stays).
    The printer is the whole design's: the one chosen is set on the root
    as the Printers manager and Send to Slicer set it (`set_property` of
    `Print Printer`/`profile` on `C0`), its tooltip *The printer of the
    whole design, for every body*, its level icon the root's (component)
    once chosen, never the body's. The process
    is the body's (`set_property` of `Print Process`/`profile` on the
    body). A library's profile is named by its `library` and copied into
    the design in the same undo step (`nameItem`; the design's copy
    reused); either choice is one undo step and the card shows it at once,
    the Process picker then with the new printer's processes first. The
    wheel and the arrow keys on a closed field skip the line and the
    manager's row.
  - **Add Print Value…** (mitcad#1178), a button under the values, opens
    the picker `PrintValuePicker` ("Add Print Value"): a search field
    over the settings the body can take as its own
    (`printValueChoices`, `print/PrintValueChoices.cpp`): the process
    keys, then the printer keys, under Process and Printer and the
    Properties window's category › sub-group headings, in the key
    table's order (`print_keys`' layout, `PrintKeyTable`), each with its
    plain name, the value the body prints with now (`print_settings`;
    *Slicer default* in grey italics without one) and its key in the
    tooltip. Left out as in the Properties window: a value kept per
    slicer and the filament's density; and every key the body sets
    itself. The filament values are the material's (`set_property`
    refuses `Print Filament` on a body): Edit Materials… sets them.
    Typing filters by the words of a name or key and makes the setting
    named as typed (else the first match) current; Up and Down move,
    Enter, Add or a double-click choose. The one chosen is set on the
    body at the value it prints with now (`set_property` of `Print
    Process` or `Print Printer`, one undo step `Set <key>`) and its row
    appears at once, with the body's icon and its field focused (the text
    selected) for another value. A setting without a value to start from
    gets a body row with an empty field (*Slicer default*), set when a
    value is typed; it goes with another body or its remove button.
  - **Remove** (mitcad#1178): a value set on the body has a small ×
    button after its field: `remove_property` on the body (one undo step
    `Remove <key>`); the row then shows the inherited occurrence's or
    component's value, or goes when the profile's value applies again.
  - With no values of its own the section says *No print values of its
    own: Add Print Value… adds one.*
  - **Send to Slicer** (mitcad#1377), the section's last row, a button
    named and drawn as the command (`print-3d`), opens Send to Slicer's
    panel (`make.print3d`) as the ribbon's button does (`trigger`), with
    the card's body alone in **Bodies**: the selection is made that body
    in its occurrence first (`MainWindow::sendMakeCardToSlicer`; a face,
    edge or vertex selected stands for its body), so `printStartBodies`
    starts the panel with it whatever else is shown. Everything else in
    the panel is as from the ribbon (Bed Face, Format, Open in, the
    plates' choice), and bodies can still be added or removed there
    before Send. The button is there only while the card is (one body),
    and greyed while the command is (it follows the command's action).
    Logged: `Make card send to slicer at x,y` (` (disabled)` after it
    while greyed) with the card's places, `Make card send to slicer:
    Body2` when clicked. Tests: `tools/ui-make-card-send-test.sh` and
    `tools/ui-windows-make-card-send-test.ps1`
    (`app.ui-windows-make-card-send`), the shared script
    `tools/ui-scripts/make-card-send.mitcad-ui`.
  - The values set this way are the body-level `Print Process` and
    `Print Printer` properties the Properties window sets: Send to Slicer
    and the 3MF export write them, and the Browser's Make marker names
    them.
  - **Width** (mitcad#1178): the selection card's page is never wider than
    the card shows (`QSizePolicy::Ignored` width in its scroll area) and
    the card's drop-downs take the width they are given
    (`AdjustToMinimumContentsLengthWithIcon`), so every section's frame
    (Make, Create, Autoselect) lies inside the card with the card's
    margin on both sides, at any card width; a long material or process
    name is elided. Before, a drop-down of a long name made the page
    wider than the card, which cut the sections' right frames.
  - **AppKit** (mitcad#1353): the generic bridge presents the card in the
    native inspector. Printer and Process are fields with the short label
    and a chevron that open the same picker as an AppKit popover under the
    field (`PickerComboBox::showPopup`, `showNativePicker`: `Native picker
    libraryPicker at makeCardPrinter: <n> rows`); the Material pop-up and
    other plain drop-downs keep the shared items' lines, bold headings and
    disabled items, which cannot be chosen (`Native choice <objectName>:
    Standard | Any printer (heading) | Draft | --- | Edit… (disabled)` when
    a drop-down has any). Add Print Value… opens through `openDialog`:
    window modal, on macOS a sheet on the window in both frontends
    (`Native sheet shown: Add Print Value (printValuePicker)`).
- **Browser markers.** On the Make tab the rows of the bodies whose
  material or print settings differ from their component's (the
  `make_differences` query) have a small dot in the accent colour after
  their name; its tooltip names what differs (`Own material: ABS`, `Own
  print settings: Walls, Process profile`). None on the other tabs. The
  AppKit outline draws the same dot with the same tooltip (mitcad#1352,
  `BrowserPanel::PresentationRow::makeTip`).
- **Log.** `Ribbon tab shown: MAKE` when a tab is shown; `Ribbon tabs:
  START, SOLID, BUILD, MAKE (shown SOLID)` after a drawing closes; the groups'
  places `Ribbon MAKE/ANNOTATE at x,y`, the buttons' `Ribbon button
  make.dimension at x,y` and the menus' `Ribbon menu MAKE/ANNOTATE:
  Dimension | Note | … | - | Annotations…`; `Make card: Body2: material
  PLA (component); printer Bench (component Root); process Standard
  (component Root); own: Walls = 5 (body Body2)` or `Make card: none`,
  the card's places `Make card printer at x,y`, `Make card process at
  x,y`, `Make card material at x,y`, `Make card value <key> at x,y`, its
  rows from the top `Make card rows: Printer, Process, Material, Walls`
  (mitcad#1239), its pickers' rows with the summary `Make card printers:
  Acme Lab: Acme Lab X1 | Other: Bench` and `Make card processes: Bench:
  Fine @Bench | Alpha: Coarse @Alpha | Any printer: Draft` (the names
  alone without headings; the pickers' own `Printer picker opened: …`,
  `Process picker sections: …`, `… search: …`, `… chose: …`), its edits
  `Make card Printer set: Bench`, `Make card Process set: Fine @Bench`,
  `Make card printer manager: design/bench` (`process`; `slicer
  default`: Printers… or Processes…), `Make card Walls set:
  3`, `Make card material of Body2: abs` and their refusals; with
  mitcad#1178 also `Make card value <key> icon body` (the level's icon:
  `body`, `insert-component`, `component`, `settings`), `Make card
  remove <key> at x,y`, `Make card add value at x,y`, the picker's
  `Add print value opened for Body1: 120 settings`, `Add print value
  search: Walls: 3 shown, current perimeters` (`none`), `Add print value
  chose perimeters`, then `Make card Walls added: 2` (`no value yet`),
  `Make card value perimeters focused`, `Make card Walls removed`, `Make
  card Walls dropped` (a pending row) and the refusals `Make card Walls:
  adding refused: …`, `… removing refused: …`; the selection card's
  sections against the card, 300 ms after the Make section or the Create
  row changed: `Selection card section Make: 1012..1290 of card
  1004..1298, visible to 1290` (`, scrolled` while the page's scroll bar
  shows; also `Create` and `Autoselect`), in the main window's
  coordinates (`MainWindow::logSelectionCardSections`); `Browser Make
  markers: Root/Bodies/Body2: Own print settings: Walls` (`none`);
  `Exported <path>: dxf outline of Body2 along F5:end(…), 1 outer and 1
  inner loops, 40 x 30 mm`; an Annotate panel's preview `Annotation
  preview: Note1 note` (`none`, `none: <why>`), `Annotation preview
  drawn: Note1 = Deburr` (`none`) and its text's place `Annotation
  preview label Note1 at x,y` (a length's line `Annotation preview line
  … at x,y`).

Tests: `tools/ui-make-tab-test.sh` (Floating, then Docked: the tabs, the
Solid tab without the moved commands, the Make tab's menus, each moved
command from its new place, Export Face as DXF… from the Laser group and
the context menu, every Annotate kind (the Note's preview before Add and
the note added where it was), the Measure panel without Keep,
the body card's one-step edit and undo, the markers on the Make tab
only), `app.ui-windows-make-tab` (`tools/ui-windows-make-tab-test.ps1`,
the same with the test's shortcuts for the Annotate entries) and

(`tools/ui-macos-make-tab-test.sh`: the tabs, the moved commands from the

The tests that kept measurements from the Measure panel

## Convert Mesh

**Convert Mesh** (`solid.convert_mesh`, `commands/ConvertMeshCommands.cpp`,
mitcad#1082; the model's `mesh_convert`, `core/model-api/src/commands.md`
"Convert Mesh" and its "Faceted solid") is the last command of the SOLID
tab's MODIFY group (registered after Mortise and Tenon), not pinned,
found by the search also as `stl`, `obj`, `mesh`, `solid`, `remix` and
`facets`. Its icon `convert-mesh` is the timeline's too (`featureIcon`).

- Inputs: *Mesh Body* (`body`: one body or a face of one whose geometry is
  `mesh`, a mesh face taken as its body; anything else is refused with
  `Convert Mesh works on mesh bodies; … is not one.`), *Type* (`mode`:
  Faceted Solid, the default, or Analytic), *Weld Tolerance* (`tolerance`,
  `0.01 mm`; labelled *Tolerance* for Analytic) and *Merge Angle*
  (`angle`, `0.5 deg`, Faceted Solid only).
- At the top of the context menus (`offeredAtTop`): the view's for a
  selection of one mesh body's faces or the body, and a mesh body's
  browser row (`BrowserController::browserMenu`, after Move/Copy), each
  starting the command with the body.
- `build`: `body`, `tolerance`, and for Faceted Solid `"mode":
  "faceted"` and `angle`; `load`: the body, Analytic for a definition
  without `mode`, the values (the inputs' defaults where the definition
  has none, which are the model's).
- The model's preview shows the new solid; OK adds the feature, which
  hides the mesh body in the same undo step, or refuses it with the
  reason (the panel stays: `the mesh has 3 open edges … after welding
  within 0.01 mm; …`, or the triangle count over 500000).
- **Insert Mesh** (`MainWindow::insertMesh`, `askMeshInsert` in
  `files/FileDialogs.cpp`): its dialog has the unit, **Convert to solid**
  (remembered as `insertMesh/convertToSolid`) and, enabled with it, *Weld
  tolerance* (mm) and *Merge angle* (degrees), 0.01 and 0.5 at first.
  With it, each mesh body of the import gets a faceted `mesh_convert`
  (`MainWindow::convertInsertedMeshes`); any that converts makes the
  import and the conversions one undo step `Insert <file>`
  (`merge_undo`); one the model refuses stays a shown mesh body, the
  status line saying why (`Inserted open.stl as a mesh body; not
  converted to a solid: open: …`).
- Logged: `Convert Mesh Mesh Body: 1 body [body F1.b0]` as any selection,
  `Preview Convert Mesh: ok`, on OK `Added convert mesh (Faceted Solid) of
  F1.b0, tolerance 0.01` (`Analytic`); Insert Mesh's `Insert Mesh dialog
  opened: unit mm (…)`, `Insert Mesh convert to solid off` (`on`, also
  when toggled), `Insert Mesh convert at x,y`, `Insert Mesh OK at x,y`,
  `Insert Mesh: unit mm, convert to solid on, weld tolerance 0.01 mm,
  merge angle 0.5 deg` (`off`), `Insert Mesh converted cube (2) (F4.b0) to
  a solid by ConvertMesh2` (the body's name: its file's, made unique),
  `Insert Mesh did not convert open (F3.b0): <reason>`.
- Tests: `tools/ui-convert-mesh-test.sh` (Linux, Xvfb: a cube's STL
  inserted, Convert Mesh from its browser row, the solid Body1 of 8000
  mm3 listed and Shell offering its faces, the mesh body hidden; Insert
  Mesh with Convert to solid of an open mesh refused with its 3 open
  edges, of the cube converted in one undo step) and
  `app.ui-windows-convert-mesh` (`tools/ui-windows-convert-mesh-test.ps1`:
  the cube inserted by mitcad-cli, the panel by its test shortcut, the
  body picked in the browser, OK, the solid listed and the mesh body
  hidden).

## Center of Mass

mitcad#1094 (`MainWindowCenterOfMass.cpp`, `view/CenterOfMass.*`,
`view/CenterOfMassView.cpp`, `browser/BrowserPanel.cpp`,
`browser/BrowserController.cpp`; the model's *Center of Mass* in
`core/model-api/src/commands.md`): the center of mass of the whole design
as a marker in the view, with a row in the browser.

- **Center of Mass** (`inspect.center_of_mass`, icon `center-of-mass`) in
  the Solid tab's Inspect group, after Physical Properties: an action,
  enabled while the design has bodies, that runs `add_center_of_mass` (a
  hidden marker is shown again; a shown one stays as it is). Display state
  as the Origin folder's light bulb: one undo step that recomputes
  nothing, allowed in a read-only window.
- **The marker** is drawn after every refresh (`MainWindow::followCenterOfMass`,
  `OcctViewer::setCenterOfMass`) where the snapshot's `center_of_mass`
  answer puts it (`DocumentSnapshot::centerOfMass`, read only while the
  design has a marker): every body counted once per occurrence that places
  it, at its place in the design and with the material it has there, so
  that it follows every recompute, component move and material. A crossed
  circle of constant size on screen (OCCT's marker of a vertex, painted
  pixel for pixel at the screen's ratio by `centerOfMassImage`): its upper
  right and lower left quadrants and its ring in `PreviewTarget` (what an
  inspection points at), the other quadrants and a ring around it on a disc
  in `SketchHalo` (the background's tone), drawn again when the background
  turns from light to dark or back. In the top layer, as the center lies
  inside the bodies; never picked.
- **Its tooltip**, in the view when the pointer rests on the marker and on
  the browser row: the coordinates (mm), the total mass, and how many
  bodies count as steel for lack of a material (`(15, 10, 1.8) mm, 0.035
  kg; 1 body without a material counted as steel`); why there is no center
  when the query failed or the design has no bodies.
- **The browser row** **Center of Mass** sits right under Origin while the
  design has the marker (`BrowserNode::Type::CenterOfMass`, key
  `center-of-mass`). Its light bulb runs `set_center_of_mass_visible`,
  in every mode as the Origin folder's (outside a command's undo range);
  its menu has Hide or Show and **Delete** (`delete_center_of_mass`, also
  the Delete key, in the AppKit frontend too, mitcad#1358). The marker and its light bulb are saved with the design
  (the display state of a project stays outside the design file, as the
  Origin folder's does).

Logs that UI tests read: `Center of Mass: none`, `Center of Mass: at x,
y, z mm, mass m kg, n bodies, k without a material (shown|hidden);
tooltip: …` (nine decimals, the mass with twelve), `Center of Mass: no
bodies (shown)`, `Center of Mass: failed: <error> (shown)`, when it
changes; `Center of Mass drawn: x, y, z on a light|dark background` or
`Center of Mass drawn: none` from the view; `Center of Mass added`,
`Deleted the Center of Mass marker`, and the browser's `Visibility
Root/Center of Mass: hidden|shown`.

Tests: `tools/ui-center-of-mass-test.sh` (the marker at the `properties`
query's total within 0.000001 mm, moved by Body2's share when its
component moves 20 mm, the tooltip, the row under Origin, its light bulb,
kept hidden in the saved design, Delete and undo),
`tools/ui-windows-center-of-mass-test.ps1` (ctest
`app.ui-windows-center-of-mass`), `app/tests/center_of_mass.cpp`
(`app.unit`: the row's state, tooltip and log from the answer, the
