## Comments

mitcad#1119 (`MainWindowComments.cpp`, `view/Comments.*`,
`view/CommentPinOverlay.*`, `view/CommentsWindow.*`; the model's
*Comments* in `core/model-api/src/commands.md`, the MCP side in
`docs/mcp.md` and `docs/ai-chat.md`): notes pinned to the place they are
about, which point an AI agent at it. The application draws what the
model's `comments` query gives (each comment's `place`, `label`, status
and `orphaned`) and changes comments only through `add_comment`,
`reply_comment`, `retarget_comment`, `resolve_comment`, `reopen_comment`
and `delete_comment` (the agent's `address_comment` comes over MCP), each
one undo step of the model's ("Add Comment C1", "Resolve C1") outside a
panel's undo range, as an annotation's (`runCommentCommand`,
`runVisibilityCommands`); refused with the reason (`Comment command
refused: <why>`) in Create Sketch's plane pick and a read-only window.
The user's commands carry `author: "user"`.

- **Add Comment** (`comment.add`, icon `comment`, **Shift+N**, the Solid
  tab's Inspect group after Center of Mass, the command search): a model
  command's panel (`modelCommand`, nothing previewed). **On** takes one
  face, edge, vertex or body, a shown sketch's curve or point, or a
  construction plane, axis or point (the feature that makes it; not the
  origin's); **At the Point Clicked** makes a pick on a face or an edge a
  free point where the click hit it (`{"at", "component",
  "occurrence"}`, in the body's component's coordinates; the root's
  component written empty); **Comment** is the text. OK (Enter) sends
  `add_comment`. A pick in empty space is no target. As an Inspect
  command the view's context menu offers it beside Measure for a face, an
  edge, a vertex, a body or a construction point, started with that pick.
- **Add Comment…** in the context menus of a body's, a sketch's and a
  feature's row in the browser, of the timeline's features (last, after
  Find in Timeline / Find in Browser) and of a user parameter's row in
  Edit Parameters… asks for the text (`askCommentText`: Enter takes it,
  Shift+Enter is a new line, Esc cancels) and sends `add_comment` on
  `{"body", "occurrence"}`, `{"feature"}` or `{"parameter"}`
  (`DocumentHost::addCommentOn`).
- **Pins** (`view/CommentPinOverlay`, a child of the view painted with
  QPainter over the bodies, as the annotations' overlay): a numbered pin
  at each comment's `place`, its head above a short stem whose tip is on
  the place, kept there as the camera moves; open ones in the inspection
  color (`PreviewTarget`), addressed ones dimmed (`kStateDimOpacity`),
  orphaned ones in the warning's colors (`WarningBadge`, `WarningMark`)
  at their last place, resolved ones and those without a place (a
  parameter) not drawn; a halo in the background's tone; a ring in the
  selection's color on the pin of the row selected in the panel. A
  click on a pin (outside commands, sketches and an annotation's pick)
  opens the Comments panel with its row selected; the pointer resting on
  one shows its tooltip (number, status, author, text, target,
  resolution, replies).
- **View › Comment Pins** (`view.comment_pins`, icon `comment-pin`,
  checkable, also the navigation bar's last button): all pins shown or
  hidden; this computer's choice (settings `view/commentPins`, on by
  default), not the design's.
- **View › Comments…** (`view.comments`, the command search): the
  Comments panel (`view/CommentsWindow`), a window beside the main window
  in the Docked and the Floating layout as the Annotations window is. Its
  rows: #, Comment, Author, On, Status (Open, Addressed, Resolved; ",
  target gone" with the warning icon for an orphan) and Resolution, the
  replies as rows under their comment; **Show:** **Open**, **Addressed**
  and **Resolved** (the first two at first) filter them. A row selected
  selects its target in the view (a face, an edge, a vertex, a body, a
  sketch's curve or point, a feature) and frames it (`revealInView`),
  outside commands and sketches; a free point or an orphan's last place
  is panned to; a parameter's names it in the status line. **Resolve**
  (Alt+R), **Reopen** (Alt+N; it asks for an optional reply, sent with
  `reopen_comment`), **Reply…** (Alt+P), **Retarget** (Alt+G, for an
  orphan) and **Delete** act on the selected comment. Retarget starts
  **Retarget Comment** (`comment.retarget`, no tab, enabled only from the
  panel), the same panel without Comment, with the selection made before
  as its pick; OK sends `retarget_comment`.
- **Preferences › AI Assistants › Agents may resolve comments**
  (`agentsMayResolveComments`, settings `ai/agentsMayResolveComments`,
  off by default): whether an MCP client's `resolve_comment` is carried
  out (the MCP bridge reads it and refuses it otherwise). Saved when
  Preferences is accepted, at once in the macOS Settings window.

Logs that UI tests read: after every refresh, when they change, `Comment
C1: open, user, Body1 › face: <text>` (`, orphaned` after the status),
`Comment C1 resolution: <text>`, `Comment C1 reply 1: <author>: <text>`,
`Comment C1 pin: open|dimmed|warning|hidden at x, y, z` (or `none`),
`Comments: none` and `Comments open: <n>`; `Comment command: <json>`,
`Comment command refused: <why>`; from Add Comment `Comment added on
<pick>`, and from the menus `Comment added on <label>`; from the view
`Comment pins drawn: C1 open | C2 dimmed` (`none`, `hidden (<n>)`),
`Comment pin C1 at x,y` (the pin's head, in the window's coordinates),
`Comment pin clicked: C1`, `Comment pins shown|hidden`; from the panel
`Comments window opened: <n> comment(s)`, `Comments row C1: <status>,
<author>, <label>, <text>, resolution: <text>|-, replies: <n>`,
`Comments shown rows: C1, C2` (or `none`), `Comments filter: Open,
Addressed`, `Comments selected: C1`, `Comments Resolve clicked: C1` and
the places `Comments row C1 at x,y`, `Comments filter Resolved at x,y`,
`Comments Resolve at x,y (disabled)`; `Comment target shown: C1: <items>
(view pan|zoom|none)`; the dialog's `Comment dialog opened: <title>:
<what>` and `Comment dialog: <text>`; `Preferences: agents may resolve
comments on|off`.

Tests: `tools/ui-comments-test.sh` (Add Comment on a face with Shift+N,
its pin, a click on the pin opening the panel with its row, the comment
addressed through the live MCP bridge, resolved in the panel and listed
under Resolved, undo, the navigation bar's Comment Pins, opened again in
the Floating layout), `tools/ui-windows-comments-test.ps1` (ctest
`app.ui-windows-comments`), `app/tests/comments.cpp` (`app.unit`: the
query's answer read, the pins' looks, the filter, the log lines, the
targets of picks, the pin's picture and its click area).


## Multiple document windows (mitcad#1172)

`WindowManager` owns one `MainWindow` and `DocumentSession` per document.
File › New Design and Open add a document when the caller has content or
an opened file; an empty, unmodified Untitled document is reused. A path
already open, including another spelling or a symbolic link, activates
its existing document. Open Recent, OS open requests, project designs and
Open Read-Only use the same routing. Read-only and new-project-design flags
are applied to the receiving window, not left on the caller.

Window › New Window (`window.new`, Ctrl+Shift+N; Cmd on macOS) always adds
a separate window. Window also lists every document, checks the active
one, activates it when chosen and offers Minimize. File › Close closes
that document using its existing save and lock questions; with only one
document it keeps the existing empty Untitled replacement behavior. Closing
the window itself always closes its owner. Quit applies
those guards to every document, stopping if one is cancelled; the last
closed document ends the process. An active command or worker finishes
cancelling before its document is destroyed.

Preferences › General stores `documents/openInCurrentWindow` (false by
default), which restores replacement for New/Open (Open and Open Recent
ask about the window's changes before the file is chosen, as before, and
the window's own file is read again rather than only brought forward), and
`documents/openDesignsIn` (`tabs` on Windows/Linux, `windows` on macOS),
in a group of their own: an INI file's `general` section is Qt's top level,
so `general/...` keys are not read back after a restart on Linux (no
setting uses the group `general`; mitcad#1190 moved the last one).
Qt frames use the latter for newly opened documents. A frame shows its
`documentTabs` bar only while it holds two or more documents
(`DocumentFrame::showsDocumentTabs`, the one place that decides it): with
one document the frame's own menu bar and the tab bar are hidden and the
document shows its own menu bar, so its window coordinates, its logged
places and its layout are those of a single document window; with two or
more the frame's menu bar follows the shown document and the tabs sit
below it, and the frame's Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab and Ctrl+W act on the
tabs (with one document Ctrl+W is File › Close, which keeps an empty
Untitled design). macOS supplies its own window tabs and adds no Qt document tab
bar. `tools/ui-document-frames-test.sh` runs the portable frame scenario
on Linux (Floating, Docked, Close All). Test logs identify the
stable UI window handle with `Document window created:` and
`Document window active:`; MCP uses its existing per-document UUIDs.

### Insert from an open design (mitcad#1172)

`insert.open_design` (**From an Open Design…**, Solid › Insert) opens the
`insertOpenDesign` dialog. `openDesignChoice` lists the other live document
windows or tabs; `openDesignDetails` shows the selected path and saved state.
Unnamed sources include their stable window handle; equal file names show
their folders. The current design is excluded and an empty list disables
`openDesignInsert`. **Insert** asks a modified or unnamed source to Save or
Cancel, using that source's normal save workflow, then calls the existing
Insert Component path and its Linked/Copy choice. Saving a source does not
insert anything until both choices succeed. The destination retains its own
undo history; the source retains its own. A path alias of the destination is
also refused.

`tools/ui-insert-open-design-test.sh`, the Windows ctest
`app.ui-windows-insert-open-design`, and the Qt/AppKit macOS ctests share
`tools/ui-scripts/insert-open-design-script.py`: actual combo input, saved-file
copy insertion and geometry, independent undo, modified-source Save/Cancel,
unsaved-source Cancel, and an empty self-excluding list. Only synthetic boxes
are used.


## Bill of Materials grouping and CSV files (mitcad#1176)

`build.parts_list` opens the Bill of Materials. **Group identical parts**
(`buildPartsGroupIdentical`) is a user view setting, stored as
`build/groupIdenticalParts`; it adds no model command or undo step. The
`parts_list` query receives `group_identical: true` when checked. Separate
single-body components and plain bodies are matched by kernel volume,
component-local bounding-box dimensions, face count and effective material;
the absolute comparison tolerance is 1e-6. Unsupported geometry stays separate.
An unstructured multi-body component contributes body rows instead of an
extra component row. Feature-created, linked and library parts retain their
component identity, including multi-body parts and purchased-item rows.
Requested **Material** or **Computed/Material** property columns use the row's
actual physical materials, including inherited placement context. Qualified
custom/library material fields and other property columns remain unchanged. Quantities include all placement paths, including inherited materials;
a row's tooltip names its grouped sources. Descriptive columns come from the
first source, and the cut list's own grouping remains unchanged.

**Save as CSV…** (`listSaveCsv`) opens **Save List as CSV** and atomically
writes UTF-8 CSV from `shownTables()`, with the same quoting and rows as
**Copy as CSV** (`listCopyCsv`). **Save as PDF…** (`listSavePdf`) continues
to export those same displayed tables. The Export folder is remembered.

The drawing Bill of Materials tool and its selected table's panel also offer
**Group identical parts** (`drawingTableGroupIdentical` in the panel).
`annotation.table.group_identical` defaults to false and is saved/undone with
the drawing. It uses the same Rust geometry/material key; every grouped
component's balloon resolves to the shared item number. Different material
placements remain distinct and retain their own balloon numbers.

`Build BOM row: <quantity> x <name>` logs each displayed row. The synthetic
`app.ui-<platform>-bom-grouping` regression drives Qt controls and file
choosers, checks 3 identical separate components plus 1 different, the
remembered view, row counts, clipboard and exact saved CSV rows, PDF, and
unchanged model geometry/undo. Its grouped and separate captures are
`bom-grouped.png` and `bom-separate.png`.

## Plates…

mitcad#1050 (`files/MainWindowPlates.cpp`, `print/OwnSettingsDialog.*`,
`OcctViewer::setPlateView`; the model's *Print plates* in
`core/model-api/src/commands.md`): the design's print plates, in a panel
of the Make tab's 3D Print group after Processes… (`make.plates`, icon
`print-plates`: two plates with printed blocks). The panel has one
**Close** button: every change is its own undo step, as Send to Slicer's
choices are, and Close keeps them. Floating and Docked alike.

| Row | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Plate** | The plates (`print_plates`), the chosen one drawn beside the design; "No plates yet" without any. **Add Plate** under it adds one (`add_print_plate`, `Plate <n>`) and chooses it; **Delete Plate** deletes the chosen one (`delete_print_plate`; what was on it goes on the first plate). |
| **Add Bodies** | A body picked in the view, or a component's occurrence picked in the Browser, goes on the chosen plate at once (`place_on_plate`, one undo step, `Put Body2 on Plate 2`); the row stays empty for the next pick. A surface or empty body is not taken. Without a plate, Plate 1 is added first. |
| **Item** | What is on the plate (shown while it has items), an item that is not in the design marked so. |
| **Count** | The item's count, 1 to 50 (a larger one the model keeps is listed too): `place_on_plate` with `count`. **Take Off Plate** under it takes the item off (`remove_from_plates`): it prints on the first plate again, as the design places it. |
| **Spiral Vase** | The plate's own `spiral_vase` (`edit_print_plate`; off takes the value away, the design's then). |
| **Settings** | The plate's own values in a line ("As the design's" without any); **Plate Settings…** opens them in the settings form of the profiles, the window titled "Plate 2 · Plate settings" (`OwnSettingsDialog::setPlate`): every process key from its tab, the plate's values set, what the design prints with as the placeholders; a change is `edit_print_plate`, emptying a field or ↺ takes the value away. |
| (note) | "*n* placements on no plate print on the first." while some are. |

- **The plate in the view.** While the panel is open the chosen plate is
  drawn beside the design (`plate_layout`): its bed's outline in the
  print bed's colour, the bed's left edge a fifth of its width right of
  the shown bodies, and its bodies where the plate puts them (each piece
  on its print bed face or the automatic orientation's, side by side and
  centred on the plate, as the export lays them out), shaded in the
  bodies' colour and never picked. It follows every change; Close takes
  it away. Fit (F6) takes it in.
- **Send to Slicer** sends the design's plates when it has any: **Send the
  Design's Plates** (with 3MF, on by default then) exports every plate
  instead of the bodies chosen (`export` with `plates`), each body in the
  colour shown. One 3MF of every plate for a slicer that keeps several
  (the Bambu family, PrusaSlicer from 2.9 on: `slicerTakesPlates`, a
  PrusaSlicer whose program names an older version takes a file per
  plate), else a 3MF per plate (`<design> - <plate>.3mf`; UltiMaker Cura,
  another program, no slicer); all the files go to the slicer in one start.
  No bed face is asked for. The last line says "Sent 2 plates to Bambu
  Studio."
- Logged: `Plates: <plate> chosen: <items>; <n> pieces`, `Plates: added
  <name>`, `Plates: <item> on <plate>`, `Plates: Spiral vase of <plate>
  on|off`, `Plate view: <plate>: <n> pieces: <body> x<count>, …` (`Plate
  view: none`), `Plate setting <plate> <key> = <text>`; Send to Slicer's
  `3D Print plates: <n>`, `3D Print plate <name>: <n> pieces in <file>`
  and `3D Print: plates one_file|file_per_plate for <dialect>: <files>`.
- Tests: `tools/ui-print-plates-test.sh` (Linux, light in Floating and
  dark in Docked), `tools/ui-windows-print-plates-test.ps1`
  (`app.ui-windows-print-plates`) and `tools/ui-macos-print-plates-test.sh`
  (`app.ui-macos-print-plates`, Qt, light and dark) run the shared script
  `tools/ui-scripts/print-plates.mitcad-ui`: two plates added, Body2
  picked onto Plate 2, Spiral Vase set, the plate in the view pictured
  (`print-plates-<scheme>.png`), and Send to Slicer's 3MF read back: two
  plates, the spiral mode on Plate 2 only.
## Auto Fix (mitcad#1223)

A feature whose reference a sketch change renamed is computed with what
the model found and warns (`region r{…} found as r{…} + r{…} after a
change in Sketch9`, `edge E{…} found as E{…} …`; shown in plain words,
"a region found as 2 regions after a change in Sketch9", "2 edges found
again …", mitcad#1334); its definition keeps
the old reference, so the warning stays until the reference is written.
**Auto Fix** (icon `ok`) writes it: the model's `auto_fix` command
(*Auto Fix* in `core/model-api/src/commands.md`) with the features, one
undo step `Auto Fix <feature>` (`Auto Fix <group>` for a group, `Auto
Fix <n> Features` for a selection), the bodies unchanged.

- **Where** (`BrowserController::featureMenu`, `groupMenu`): the context
  menu of a timeline feature, right after Edit Feature / Edit Sketch (and
  Redefine Sketch Plane); for a feature in the timeline's selection
  (Shift or Ctrl+click) it fixes the whole selection. The same entry is
  in the menu of the feature's row in the Browser (that feature alone)
  and of a timeline group's folder (the group's features).
- **When**: only when one of those features has a warning Auto Fix can
  write, the timeline query's `auto_fix` (`DocumentSnapshot::Feature::
  autoFix`); after the fix, or for a feature whose reference is gone or
  ambiguous (it fails), the entry is not offered.
- **What it says**: the model's summary, logged as it is and shown in the
  status bar, a success when nothing is left, else a warning naming what
  is left and what to do: `Auto Fix: 2 of 3 warnings fixed; Hole1: the
  body has no edge E{…}, pick it again`. A later feature that named the
  faces the fix renamed is updated in the same step (`…; also updated:
  Shell1`). A refused command logs `Auto Fix refused: <why>`.
- **MCP and scripts**: the same `auto_fix` command, class model.

Tests: `tools/ui-timeline-auto-fix-test.sh` and
`app.ui-windows-timeline-auto-fix` (`tools/ui-windows-timeline-auto-fix-test.ps1`),
the shared steps `tools/ui-scripts/timeline-auto-fix.mitcad-ui` on
`tools/ui-scripts/timeline-auto-fix.json`: an extrusion whose region a
sketch change split; Auto Fix from its timeline menu (offered after Edit
Feature), one undo step, the same volume, no longer offered; Undo brings
the warning and the entry back.

## The Start tab

mitcad#1258, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#125 (`files/StartPage.*`,
`files/RecentDesigns.*`, `files/StartBrowser.*` (mitcad#1301),
`MainWindowStart.cpp`, `framework/Ribbon.*`): a
page to start from and come back to. The ribbon's tab `START` (shown
**Start**) is the first, before Solid, Build and Make, and is there at any
time in both layouts; a drawing hides it with the model's tabs
(*Drawings*). Its page has no groups: the window shows the **Start page**
over the 3D view instead, as a drawing takes the view: its content right
below the workspace tabs (the Floating title row; the empty row of groups
under them takes no room), its footer above the Floating message band
while that shows (in full or as its stub), both followed as the tabs and
the band show, hide, move or resize. While it shows, the Floating
layout's cards are hidden (`FloatingLayout::showOnlyCards`), the Docked
layout's docks and its navigation bar too, and the AppKit frontend's cards
(`NativeMacWindow::setStartPageShown`); they come back as they were. The
AppKit frontend's workspace selector shows the retained ribbon's tabs, the
Start tab among them, and the page is the shared Qt page over the embedded
view.

- **Welcome**: "Welcome to MitCad" and **What's New in X.Y**, which opens
  this version's release page (`…/releases/tag/v<version>`) in the
  browser; nothing is fetched at start-up.
- **Quick actions**, each a card with its key as the menus show it: **New
  Design** (`file.new_design`, its line the default units for new designs,
  Preferences › General; *New designs' units*), **Open Design…**
  (`file.open`), **Open Project…** (`file.open_project`), **Import File…**
  (`file.import`).
- **The designs' browser** (mitcad#1301): one search at the top, the two
  view buttons (cards or a compact list, `start/compactList`), and two
  columns below them.
  - **Left**: **Recent** and **Pinned** (the recent designs, all or the
    pinned ones), then under **Projects** every project of the Projects
    panel that has versions (Local and Cloud, by name, as File › Open from
    Project lists them: `readProjects` on a thread of its own,
    `project_tree`, no network) with its state icon as the panel shows it
    (a Cloud project's sync state: synced, versions to send or newer ones,
    offline, a warning; a Local project a folder) and its state in words in
    the tooltip, and last **Add project**, which runs New Project
    (`file.new_project`). The row shown is highlighted.
  - **Right, for Recent and Pinned**: File › Open Recent's list (the
    setting `recentFiles`, at most ten, newest first) and the designs pinned
    with their star (`start/pinnedDesigns`; a pinned design stays listed
    when it drops out of the ten). A card shows the design's preview, its
    file name, its type (the suffix: MITCAD, STEP, F3D), its folder (the
    last two folders) and when it was last opened or saved
    (`start/recentOpened`; Today, Yesterday, 3 days ago, then the date; an
    older list without times shows the file's date).
  - **Right, for a project**: a breadcrumb (the project › its folder › …;
    each part goes there, so a click goes up), the place's sub-folders as a
    row of low folder buttons (a click goes into one), and its designs as
    cards in the same style: the preview (else the type's icon), the name,
    its project and folders, when it last changed (`project_tree`'s
    `modified`), the pin star. The place's contents are Open from
    Project's (`ProjectBrowserData`: sub-folders first, then designs, each
    by name). A Cloud project's cards show at once with the type's icon and
    get their previews as they are found on this computer; nothing is
    downloaded for a preview.
  - **The search** (*Search designs in all projects*) lists, as it is
    typed, the designs whose name (without its suffix) holds the text, case
    ignored, in every project and then in the recent list (a recent design
    that is in a listed project only once, as the project's). The results
    are cards whose second line names their project and folder ("Shop /
    parts"; a recent design its folder), so designs of the same name tell
    apart; none: *No designs match*. Clearing the field returns to the row
    shown, and choosing a row ends the search.
  - A click on a card opens the design as Open Recent does (in the window
    while it holds an untouched untitled design), and it joins the recent
    list; its context menu has Open, Pin or Unpin and (a recent design)
    Remove from List. A file that is no longer there is shown as missing,
    with **Remove**, which takes it off the list and its pin. Clear Recent
    Files keeps the pinned designs; a project's design pinned with its star
    is listed under Pinned too.
  - **Remembered**: the row and folder shown (`start/browseRow`: `recent`,
    `pinned` or `project`, with `start/browseRoot` and
    `start/browseFolder`) show the next time; a project or folder that is
    gone falls back to the project's top or to Recent.
  - File › Open from Project and its window are not changed by it.
- **Drop area**: a file MitCad opens or imports, dropped anywhere on the
  page, is opened (a design) or comes in (an import; the page goes), as
  on the window.
- **Resources**, each running what exists today: **Component Libraries**
  (`insert.library_component`, the component picker), **User Guide**
  (`help.user_guide`), **Keyboard Shortcuts** (`help.shortcuts`, the
  Keyboard and Mouse Overview), **Connect AI Assistant**
  (`help.connect_assistant`).
- **Footer**: **Show start page at launch** (`start/showAtLaunch`, on by
  default), **Preferences…** (`tools.preferences`) and **Report an
  Issue** (the issue list of the tracker the reports go to,
  `reports/issueUrl` or the build's, in the browser).
- **Leaving it.** A design that opens, a new design, a recovered design,
  an import and a command of the 3D view (a feature, a tool, a ribbon's
  command but the File commands: `MainWindow::trigger`) show the Solid
  tab; the File commands and those on no ribbon tab (Open, Import, Undo,
  Preferences, the user guide) leave the page where it is until a design
  opens or something comes in. A sketch or a drawing started
  from it goes back to Solid when it ends.
- **The design behind it** (mitcad#1313): the page clears the design's
  selection when it opens (unless a command is running, which keeps its
  own), and Delete (on macOS also Backspace) on the page or one of its
  controls deletes nothing (`MainWindow::keyPressEvent`); back on Solid
  the design is as it was. Tests: `tools/ui-start-page-delete-test.sh` and
  `app.ui-windows-start-page-delete`
  (`tools/ui-windows-start-page-delete-test.ps1`), the shared steps
  `tools/ui-scripts/start-page-delete.mitcad-ui` on
  `start-page-delete.json`, Floating and Docked: Sketch1 selected, the
  Start tab clears the selection, Delete and Backspace on the page and on
  its New Design card add no undo step and keep the block.
- **At launch** (`main.cpp`, `MainWindow::showStartPageAtLaunch`): the
  Start tab shows when Show start page at launch is on, unless MitCad
  opens a file (`--open`, a file argument), the demo block, a screenshot
  or `--set`; off, MitCad starts on the empty untitled design on the Solid
  tab as before. The recovery question (*Recovery*) comes after it, over
  the page; a design it restores shows on the Solid tab. The tests' runs:
  `MITCAD_START_PAGE=0` never shows it (the UI test libraries set it),
  `MITCAD_START_PAGE=1` follows the setting, and a UI test script's run
  (`MITCAD_TEST_INPUT`) without the variable does not show it.
- **Previews.** Every save writes the design's preview, the 3D view as it
  is (as a version's preview: `saveVersionThumbnail`), 256 px at most, a
  PNG in the user's local application data: `thumbnails/recent/<SHA-1 of
  the design's absolute path>.png` (`MITCAD_THUMBNAIL_DIR` in tests;
  `recent::designPreviewPath`). Not in the design's file nor its folder:
  files of every version read and write as before, and a project's
  history gets no picture. The Start page's cards and File › Open Recent's
  entries show it; a design without one (an imported file, a design not
  saved since) shows its type's icon.

Tests: `tools/ui-start-page-test.sh`, `app.ui-windows-start-page`
(`tools/ui-windows-start-page-test.ps1`) and `app.ui-macos-start-page`
(`app.ui-macos-native-start-page` for the AppKit frontend;
`tools/ui-macos-start-page-test.sh`), the shared steps

## Background evaluation of the rolled-back features (mitcad#1267)

An edit before the timeline marker gives every rolled-back feature after it
new inputs, so moving the marker forward again would evaluate each of them
as the marker passes it. The window evaluates them in the background
instead (`DocumentSession`, `docs/architecture.md`, *Background
evaluation*):

- **When.** At the session's idle point after a job (`whenIdle`), with no
  command panel or sketch open, the marker before the end of the timeline,
  and a state no background evaluation went through to the end yet; never
  after a job that was asked to stop (its meshing may have left bodies the
  view meshes itself). No timer. Only one runs at a time.
- **How.** A fork of the document with its marker at the end recomputes on
  a thread of its own at the lowest priority (`QThread::IdlePriority`, the
  Utility quality on macOS), not on the model worker: the user's jobs never
  queue behind it. When it ends, the document adopts its results on the
  window's thread while no job runs, if its definition is still the one
  the run was made from (the marker aside), the features nearest the
  marker first and within the memory cache's budget. A feature that fails
  in it is not reported: the user sees it when the marker gets there.
- **Cancelled.** At once when a command or a sketch opens (Create Sketch
  too), and before any job starts: the job cancels it and waits for it to
  stop (the kernel's long operations stop inside an evaluation, P7e), and
  the document takes what it evaluated by then. The job then starts as
  without it.
- **Off.** `MITCAD_BACKGROUND_EVALUATION=0`, or computing inline
  (`MITCAD_COMPUTE_INLINE=1`).

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `Background evaluation started: 2 features after the marker` | a run started at an idle point (the features after the marker that are not suppressed) |
| `Background evaluation: 2 features in 840 ms, adopted 2` | a run went to the end: the features it evaluated (cache misses), and the results the document took |
| `Background evaluation cancelled by a command after 120 ms: 1 features, adopted 1` (`by a sketch`, `by Create Sketch`, `by job set_marker`, `by closing`) | a run stopped by what the user started, with what it had evaluated and what the document took of it; logged before the job that stopped it logs `Computing <label> started` |

For tests, `MITCAD_TEST_RECOMPUTE_DELAY_MS="background evaluation=4000"`
makes each of its evaluations 4 s longer (`framework/Diagnostics.hpp`).

Tests: `tools/ui-background-evaluation-test.sh` and
`app.ui-windows-background-evaluation`
(`tools/ui-windows-background-evaluation-test.ps1`), the shared steps
`tools/ui-scripts/background-evaluation.mitcad-ui` on
`tools/ui-scripts/background-evaluation.json`: a join added before the
marker, the rolled-back fillets evaluated in the background and adopted,
the marker dragged to the end recomputing 0 features; an edit opened while
a run goes cancels it before its preview, which builds. The model's side:
`core/model-tests/api/src/rolled_back_tests.rs` (`core.model.api`).

## Envelope

**Envelope** (`solid.envelope`, `commands/EnvelopeCommands.cpp`,
mitcad#1276; the model's `envelope`, `core/model-api/src/commands.md`
"Envelope") is in the SOLID tab's CREATE menu in a section of its own
(`envelope`) after Mirror, before the Machine Elements submenu; not
pinned, found by the search also as `wrap`, `skin`, `placeholder`,
`simplify`, `layout` and `hull`. Its icon `envelope` is the timeline's too
(`featureIcon`). Editing an `envelope` feature opens the same panel. It
works in the Floating and the Docked layout as every panel does.

- Inputs: *Source* (`source`: components and bodies, any number; nothing
  is the active component with the components placed in it, one component
  picked in the browser is the occurrence that places it, bodies are of
  one occurrence; a mix, two components or bodies of two occurrences are
  refused with `Pick one component, or bodies of one occurrence.`, a pick
  outside the active component with `Pick a component or bodies placed in
  the active component.`), *Automatic Detail Size* (`automatic`, on: 1 %
  of the source's diagonal, at least 5 mm) and *Detail Size* (`detail`,
  `20 mm`, shown while Automatic Detail Size is off).
- `build`: `occurrence` (the pick's occurrence path from the active
  component, the feature's; left out for its own bodies), `bodies` (the
  picked bodies), `detail` (the expression, without Automatic Detail
  Size); `load`: the source back where the active component is seen (its
  first occurrence path), Automatic Detail Size for a definition without
  `detail`.
- The model's preview shows the envelope; OK adds the feature.
- Logged: `Envelope Source: 1 component [...]` as any selection, `Preview
  Envelope: ok`, on OK `Added envelope of 1 component in O1, detail size
  20 mm` (`… detail size automatic`; `of the active component` without a
  source).
- Tests: `app.ui-windows-envelope-command`
  (`tools/ui-windows-envelope-command-test.ps1`: Machine:1 picked in the
  browser at 20 mm in the Docked layout, edited to 30 mm, both undone; at
  the automatic size in the Floating layout; Show as Envelope… on one of
  two occurrences of a linked machine and Show in Full, the other in full
  throughout), the CREATE menu in `tools/ui-sketch-create-menu-test.sh` and
  `tools/ui-windows-pattern-options-test.ps1`.

## View › Show (mitcad#1287)

GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#142. `MainWindowVisibility.cpp`
(`registerViewShowCommands`, `toggleViewShow`, `syncViewShowChecks`), the
menu in `ViewController::createMenus`, the model's `set_view_show`
(`core/model-api/src/commands.md`, "View › Show of the whole design").

- **Commands:** `view.show_origins` (**Origins**: the design's origin
  planes, axes and point, and the joint origins), `view.show_construction`
  (**Construction**: construction planes, axes and points) and
  `view.show_sketches` (**Sketches**), actions of mode Any without a ribbon
  place (`def.tab` empty), checkable entries of the View menu's **Show**
  submenu (object name `viewShowMenu`) in the Docked and the Floating
  layouts alike, and so of the macOS native frontend's menu bar, which
  reads the Qt menus (`refreshNativeActions`); also in the command search,
  Keyboard Shortcuts and the quick-access group's View menu.
- **What they do:** each turns its kind of the whole design off or on,
  every component's, linked ones too, as display state the design keeps
  (`set_view_show`, one undo step `Hide All Construction` / `Show All
  Construction`, saved in the design file, per user in a project). No
  light bulb changes: `MainWindow::showDatums` leaves out the hidden kinds'
  datums (the root's origin while Origins is off, unless Create Sketch asks
  for a plane), `sketchShown` the hidden sketches (the sketch being edited
  and the sketches a command shows for its time stay, lighter, as a hidden
  light bulb's do), and the Browser greys the rows of a hidden kind (the
  Origin folder and its rows, the Sketches and Construction folders and
  their rows, joint origins) with their light bulbs as they are. Showing
  the kind again shows what the light bulbs show.
- **Every mode:** as the light bulbs (`runVisibilityCommands`): while a
  command's panel or a sketch is open, outside the command's undo range;
  in a read-only document too (`readOnlyModelCommand`).
- **Check marks** follow the `document` query's `display.show`
  (`DocumentSnapshot::showOrigins`, `showConstruction`, `showSketches`) on
  every refresh, also after an undo or a refused change.
- **Logs:** `View show construction: hidden` (`… shown`), `View Show menu:
  Origins on | Construction off | Sketches on` (the submenu's entries and
  check marks when they change), `Construction shown: Plane1 in O1, Plane2`
  (the construction datums drawn, `none`, when they change), with the
  existing `Sketches shown: …`, `Design origin … in the view; the Origin
  folder's light bulb …` and `Browser row colours: …`.
- **Tests:** `tools/ui-view-show-test.sh` and
  `tools/ui-windows-view-show-test.ps1` (`app.ui-windows-view-show`): Delete
  on a row of an imported base feature's body (Docked), then Construction
  off and on in two components (the planes drawn and greyed, the sketches
  and the origin kept, the saved design's `display.hidden` and no light
  bulb set), Sketches and Origins (Floating); `core.model.api`
  (`view_show_tests.rs`).
